doctrine: THIS BOARD IS NOT WIRED INTO THE HARNESS AND MUST NOT BE. The unattended runs in scripts/poc/ read docs/board/rc-board-phase2.json and only that file, by path, in run.sh, inbox.mjs and notify.mjs. Nothing in this board changes that. THE HARNESS CONTINUES TO WORK THE PHASE 2 BOARD, AND THAT PART IS UNCHANGED. The unattended runs still read the phase 2 board by path and are not repointed by anything here. THIS BOARD IS OPEN TO INTERACTIVE TERMINALS AS OF 2026-08-30, BY RULING R-061, AND THE SENTENCE THAT SAID OTHERWISE IS RETIRED. It said the board was worked by nobody until the phase 2 launch gate reached 9 of 9, and that a terminal picking a P3 card before then had made a mistake and should stop. The owner opened phase 3 by dispatch instead, which is exactly the owner ruling that sentence reserved the decision for, and he opened it for a reason the sentence could not have anticipated: the phase 2 gate cannot reach 9 of 9 without Andre, G4 and G9 are parked behind him, and the platform meanwhile has no client or project management at all, which is the owner's primary complaint about it. R-061 records the whole of that. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the harness is not repointed, the phase 2 board is still the queue for every unattended run, and a phase 2 card is still worked by whoever picks it. The two boards are now worked in parallel by different terminals rather than in sequence. A board claim is never truth on its own. The evidence field carries the proof and the acceptance field carries the check that produced it. The executor updates this JSON at every checkpoint, in the same PR as the code, and bumps as_of. docs/board/validate-board.mjs must exit 0 before every commit; a commit made while the validator is red is reverted, not patched forward. GATE VOCABULARY. Every card on this board carries green_self_merge, and owner_merge is retired here exactly as it is on phase 2 under ruling R-002. green_self_merge means the executor merges its own PR once the required quality check is green AND the card's named acceptance has passed. Defect review belongs to the CRITIC at wave boundaries and to an optional owner batch review before a client demo, and NEITHER IS A MERGE GATE. cyan_clear, owner_authorizo and owner_merge are unused on this board. SELF-MERGE RUNS UNDER CLAUDE.md SECTION 3.1, granted by R-049, extended to AUTHOR by R-056, and WIDENED TO EVERY PATH BY R-059 ON 2026-08-30 (all three in decisions/inbox.md). EXECUTOR, AUTHOR, POC-BUILDER and TRIAGE each merge their own pull request on ANY path once the quality check is green ON THE HEAD SHA. The path sets are gone and the sentence that said a phase 3 schema card could never be self-merged because it touches supabase/ is retired with them: a card that authors a migration FILE now merges like any other card. THE ONE EXCLUSION IS EXECUTION, NOT A PATH. Applying a migration, or any destructive statement, against the production database is gated by CLAUDE.md 8.6 and R-047 and is not covered by any merge grant, because a green check says nothing about a database. Merging the file is not applying it. THE ACCEPTANCE HALF OF SECTION 5b IS UNTOUCHED: a card still ships on green quality PLUS its named acceptance having been run and passed. What R-059 removed is the wait for the owner, not the proof. THE GRANT DIES IF A paths: FILTER IS EVER ADDED TO .github/workflows/quality.yml, because a pull request would then be skipped and report success in seconds, and merging on a check that never ran is not merging on green. IT ALSO DIES AT P2-13 with every other terminal grant. ESCALATE TO IVAN ONLY ON THE CLOSED LIST, and everything not on it the terminal decides and records. THE LIST IS THE TEN ITEMS IN SECTION 6 OF docs/DOCTRINE-TRIAGE.md, WHICH IS THE SOLE AUTHORITY ON THIS FOR EVERY ROLE UNDER R-057, AND THERE IS NO OTHER LIST ANYWHERE, IN THIS REPOSITORY OR OUTSIDE IT. This board previously said nine, which was already stale when it was authored: R-050 added launch timing on 2026-08-28. The ten: money; pricing; legal; vendor, meaning adding or changing a third-party service that processes client data; credential grants, where widening escalates and narrowing does not; anything that would reach Mihai or Andre as a request; panel actions needing a click in a console someone has to log into, DNS and Vercel and Supabase and BotFather and the email and payment consoles; production DELETE-class execution; acceptance sign-off; and launch timing. Read the section rather than this summary when the two could differ, and a summary that could differ is why R-057 made one file the authority. Everything else, including resequencing this board, authoring cards, correcting a stale acceptance line and ratifying a deviation, is decided and written down rather than asked. An escalation carries a recommended default or it is unfinished. SKIP-NOT-HALT FOR DECISIONS. The run never stops for a question. A card that cannot proceed gets its question field filled with the structured decision-needed text (DECISION NEEDED, CONTEXT, OPTIONS, RECOMMENDATION, IMPACT IF UNANSWERED), blocked_on set to the person who owes the answer, status set to blocked, and the executor moves to the next eligible card in the same session. A recommendation is mandatory: a question without one is unfinished. HALT ON AN ABSENT TOOL OR A FALSE PREMISE, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT RULE AND IS NOT SOFTENED BY THE ONE ABOVE. Skip-not-halt covers a decision the executor lacks the authority to make. It does not cover a card whose premise is wrong. When a card names a tool, table, column, route, file, script, environment variable or service that does not exist, or asserts a fact the repository contradicts, the executor STOPS WORKING THAT CARD IMMEDIATELY. It does not build the missing thing on a guess, does not invent the tool, and does not reinterpret the card until it fits what is there. It sets status blocked, sets blocked_on to the person who owes the correction, and writes into question the structured decision-needed text naming the premise and PASTING THE COMMAND OUTPUT THAT DISPROVES IT, then moves to the next eligible card. status halted stays reserved for the failure ceiling in CLAUDE.md section 10 and is not used for this. Several cards on this board carry a premise that was checked against the repository at authoring time and the check is recorded in their notes; the rule exists for the ones that were not. DEFAULTS ARE WIDE ON THIS BOARD ON PURPOSE. Every card carries a defaults field holding pre-authorized answers to that card's expected ambiguities, and they are deliberately wider than phase 2's because this board is authored ahead of its phase and the owner is not available to referee. When defaults covers an ambiguity the executor APPLIES IT AND LOGS THE APPLICATION IN NOTES, and does not ask. Defaults fill silence; they never override an explicit instruction in the card. ACCEPTANCE: every card names a machine-checkable acceptance line, a command with an expected exit code, a URL with expected content, or a named test. No acceptance, no ship. A card whose acceptance cannot be run yet is blocked, never shipped. A check that has never been seen to fail is not a check. MIGRATIONS: authored as supabase/migrations/NNNN_name.sql and listed in the PR description by path. WHO APPLIES ONE IS READ OFF CLAUDE.md SECTION 8 WHEN THE CARD IS PICKED AND IS NOT ASSERTED HERE, because that section changed three times in the four days before this board was written and this board is not worked for weeks. The card defaults carry both branches so a terminal is correct either way. Section 8.6 stands regardless: a migration containing DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE or DELETE is never auto-applied, and the R-047 assertion-bearing-script exception does not reach migrations. Every migration apply is journalled in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md, and under R-055 every NON-migration production write is journalled in docs/PRODUCTION-WRITES.md with its script sha256; a write with no row in one of the two is a violation. MIGRATION NUMBERS ARE NOT PINNED ANYWHERE ON THIS BOARD, because phase 2 may consume numbers after 0012 before phase 3 starts: each card takes the next free number when it is worked and names its file by suffix in its acceptance. A migration file is never edited after it has been applied; a correction is a new numbered file. A BACKFILL AND A COLUMN DROP NEVER TRAVEL IN THE SAME MIGRATION, which is why P3-04b and P3-05b exist as separate cards. DENSITY DOCTRINE BINDS EVERY SCREEN CARD ON THIS BOARD, not only wave 4: summary first, detail behind a drill-in, never a full-length table dumped into a page. A summary block shows at most 5 rows with a link to the full history; a list paginates at 25; filters live in the URL query string so a filtered view can be linked and so the back button works. UI IS ROMANIAN THROUGHOUT, with proper diacritics, on every label, error, empty state and toast, and DESKTOP FIRST: responsive and mobile layouts are out of scope unless a card says otherwise. P3-21 makes this machine-enforced. SECRETS: environment variable names only. Values never appear in chat, in this board, in a commit, in a log or in tool output. ELIGIBILITY: a card is eligible when status is todo, every id in depends_on belongs to a shipped card, and blocked_on is null. The executor takes the lowest-id eligible card. Ids sort on a tuple of prefix, number and suffix, so the number is compared as a number: AUT-8 before AUT-9 before AUT-16, and P3-04 before P3-04b before P3-05. Corrected 2026-09-05 by BOARD-03; it previously said ids sort lexically, which was true of the code and is why AUT-8 queued behind AUT-16. CONFLICTS ARE RESOLVED LOCALLY, AGAINST THE FULL TREE, WITH THE CHECKS RUN BEFORE THE COMMIT, per R-052 and CLAUDE.md section 3. Never in the GitHub web editor, which shows one file at a time and can run no check in this repository, and never by the owner. A grep for conflict markers is NOT the check, because the characters it looks for are exactly the ones a bad resolution deletes: npm run check:conflict-residue is the check and it runs in quality on every push. A conflicted board JSON is rebuilt from both parents and proven card by card, never hand-edited around the markers. PLAIN HYPHENS ONLY, never an em dash or an en dash, anywhere in this file. The full standing rules are in CLAUDE.md at the repo root.

cards.title: The four sample documents are served on signed URLs whose three failure paths hold a fixed contract, proved against the storage layer rather than reported from its documentation.
cards.plain: Andre can now download the four test documents from our system, and when a download link stops working he is told which of three things went wrong: the link ran out of time, the link is broken, or the file is not there. Before this, all three looked identical to him, so a link that had simply expired was indistinguishable from a system fault.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/document-url.spec.ts` exits 0 with EIGHT cases, one per clause: a valid link serves the bytes; an expired token gives 400 and code EXPIRED_TOKEN; a tampered token gives 401 and code INVALID_TOKEN; a deleted object under a valid token gives 404 and code OBJECT_NOT_FOUND; a missing token gives 401 and not a redirect; a path with no file extension gives 401 and not a redirect; the bare prefix gives 404 JSON and not Next's page; a non-GET method gives 405 JSON. Every failure case also asserts content-type application/json and the absence of <!doctype and <html in the body. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run check:document-url` exits 0 over the captured error bodies of BOTH the hosted project and the local stack, plus the code-to-status pairing. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS ARTEFACT: the verbatim status line, headers and body of all three storage failure paths committed in the card's report.
cards.defaults:
VERIFY, NEVER REPORT FROM DOCUMENTATION. What the storage layer returns is established by probing the real project and pasting the response, not by citing a page. This default is the card.

IF THE CONTRACT DOES NOT HOLD, PUT OUR OWN ROUTE IN FRONT OF IT, and put PRODUCTION on that route too. A contract that holds for four sample documents and not for real ones is worse than no contract: the other side programs against it and it fails only in production.

AN UNRECOGNISED UPSTREAM RESPONSE IS NEVER GUESSED INTO ONE OF THE THREE. It gets its own status, 502, so a future change at Supabase looks like a change and not like a broken token.

NO EXPECTED LINE COUNTS, TOTALS OR PAGE COUNTS FOR THE FOUR DOCUMENTS, anywhere: not in the report, not on this board, not in anything sent to Andre. The point of the set is that the extractor produces them unaided, and a value sent alongside the file cannot be taken back.

TTL 7200 SECONDS FOR THE SAMPLES. The production TTL stays 15 minutes and this card does not touch it.

evidence.ref: #159, docs/reports/2026-09-02-executor-ext-08-sample-documents.md. THE CONTRACT WAS NOT MET BY THE STORAGE LAYER: Supabase answers 400 to all three conditions and uses the SAME machine-readable code, InvalidJWT, for an expired token and a tampered one, which is exactly the distinction that was asked for. A missing object answers 400 with its real status buried as a string inside the body. No path returned text/html, in either layer, and that was checked on nine routes rather than three. app/api/documents/[...path]/route.ts now translates into 400 EXPIRED_TOKEN, 401 INVALID_TOKEN, 404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, always application/json. Acceptance: 8 of 8 playwright cases pass, 22 of 22 contract cases pass, tsc exit 0. DEPLOYED AND RE-CAPTURED 2026-09-02, docs/reports/2026-09-02-executor-ext-08-deployed-captures.md: production answers 400 EXPIRED_TOKEN, 401 INVALID_TOKEN and 404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, all application/json, and a valid link serves the three-page invoice byte for byte at the sha256 recorded when it was uploaded.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED AND WORKED 2026-09-02 BY EXECUTOR, from the owner's dispatch of the same day. Andre's pipeline was blocked on it: his auth chain, size guard, schema and extraction prompt are all proven and everything past the download step waited on this.

THE FAILURE CONTRACT WAS MEASURED, NOT READ. Nine routes were probed against the real project: the sign route with an expired token, a tampered token, a token that is not a JWT, a token signed for a different path, and no token at all; the public-object route and the authenticated-object route on a private bucket; an unknown storage route; the project root and an unknown top-level path. All ten answered JSON. None answered text/html. That is the one clause of the contract the storage layer already held.

THE DEFECT THIS CARD FOUND IN ITSELF. The first classifier switched on the response body's `code` field, which every hosted capture carries. The storage server in the local Supabase stack, the one CI runs, omits it entirely. Both token cases fell through to the unrecognised branch and answered 502 where the contract requires 400 and 401; two of the eight end-to-end cases failed on the first local run. The INVERSE of that mistake would have been caught by nothing, because CI has no access to the hosted project and must not have any, so scripts/poc-free/check-document-url-contract.mjs replays the captured bodies of BOTH deployments with no network at all. docs/LEARNINGS.md carries it.

THE PROXY EXCEPTION IS PART OF THE CONTRACT. proxy.ts protects every path by default and redirects a session-less request to /login, which is HTML. Make has no session. Without the /api/documents entry in isPublic(), every failure on this route becomes a 307 to a login page and a redirect-following client gets 200 text/html. Case 6 of the spec holds that line with a path that has no .pdf extension, because the proxy matcher already excludes .pdf and would hide the regression on any ordinary document.

SCOPE TAKEN DELIBERATELY, AND IT IS THE CARD'S DEFAULT. lib/data/extraction-fire.ts now sends the route URL as document_url. Leaving production on the raw storage URL would have made the contract true for four sample documents and false for every real one. Shape, bucket, path, token and TTL are unchanged; only the origin moves, and the six fields of the fire payload are still exactly six.

ONE PRODUCTION STORAGE WRITE, JOURNALLED. Four objects under rc-docs/_samples/andre/ plus one throwaway probe object written and deleted. docs/PRODUCTION-WRITES.md carries the row, and it is the first row in that file that is not a database write.

A CDN SERVED A DELETED OBJECT. The first probe deleted the object and re-fetched the same signed URL: 200 OK with the original bytes, cf-cache-status HIT. The 404 shape appeared only on a cache-busted request a minute later. Nothing was changed, because bucket policy 0002 grants DELETE to no application role, but it is in LEARNINGS because a probe using only one of the two request forms draws a confidently wrong conclusion in either direction.

DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED ON PRODUCTION 2026-09-02, after #159 merged. All three failure paths hold at the live origin and the control serves the document at its recorded sha256. The captures are committed.

THE LIVE LINKS ARE NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. A two-hour token committed at authoring time is an expired token by the time anybody reads it. They are re-issued from scripts/ext/serve-sample-documents.mjs after this deploys, together with the route-level captures of the same three conditions.

THE THREE-PAGE INVOICE CARRIES A DEFECT NO TOTAL CAN SEE. A description tail belonging to one line sits after both a repeated page header and a carry-forward row, so it is separated from its own line by two structures. If it misattaches, the product NAME is corrupted on a document where every number still reconciles. Any acceptance written against that document asserts the affected line's name and not only its figures. Recorded from the owner's dispatch, without the expected value.

NOTE 2026-09-15, CARD EXT-33: the sample set under `_samples/andre` holds six documents since 2026-09-15, and R-096 as amended that day covers every document under that prefix, not a fixed count of four. Where this card says four, the four are the original set; nothing above is changed.

cards.title: Re-test supplier spelling folding through find_supplier_by_folded_name, after P3-05b deleted the backfill fixture that used to prove it.
cards.plain: Make sure that typing a supplier's name in a different way, lower case, no accents, extra spaces, still finds the supplier that is already in the system instead of quietly making a second copy of them.
cards.acceptance: NAMED COMMAND: `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 with `scripts/poc-free/local-db/assertions/fold-01_supplier_folding.sql` among the files it reports asserted. The file must prove, against a real PostgreSQL with every migration applied: (1) FOLDING EQUIVALENCE, that case, diacritics and whitespace runs all resolve to the same supplier record; (2) THE TIE-BREAK, that an ACTIVE supplier wins over a deactivated one that folds to the same name, and that among equally active rows the OLDEST wins; (3) IDEMPOTENCY, that the lookup writes nothing and returns the same row on repeated calls; (4) that a name matching nothing returns no row, since the write path reads that as permission to create. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults: THIS CARD EXISTS BECAUSE P3-05b DELETED COVERAGE AND SAID SO. The backfill fixture in assertions/0019_suppliers.sql proved three behaviours and could not be repaired: migration 0027 dropped both products.supplier_name and backfill_product_suppliers(integer), so the fixture had nowhere to write and no function to drive. public.find_supplier_by_folded_name(text) survives 0027 and is what the product write path actually calls, so it is where the behaviour still lives. THE CAP IS OUT OF SCOPE AND THE REASON IS NOT LAZINESS: p_max_new bounded how many suppliers ONE BACKFILL RUN could create, that function is gone, and nothing else in the schema has a cap because the write path resolves one name per save by construction. An assertion for it would pass vacuously and would read as coverage that does not exist. THE FILE IS NAMED AFTER THE CARD, NOT A MIGRATION, because it defends a behaviour spanning 0017's fold_text and 0019's lookup after the migration that carried its proof was spent; apply.mjs runs every .sql in that directory and assumes nothing about names.

evidence.ref: npm run check:migrations -> exit 0, 27 migrations applied unmodified to a bare postgres:16 and 11 assertion files passed, including assertions/fold-01_supplier_folding.sql. COVERS: folding equivalence across case, diacritics and collapsed whitespace, all resolving to one record; the tie-break, with an ACTIVE supplier beating an older DEACTIVATED one that folds to the same name and the OLDEST winning among equally active rows; idempotency, the lookup writing nothing and repeating its answer; and an unknown name returning no row, which is what the write path reads as permission to create. A DEFECT IN THE FIXTURE WAS FOUND BY RUNNING IT: the first version assumed fold_text normalised punctuation, so 'Bricolaj SRL' and 'BRICOLAJ S.R.L.' were expected to fold together. They do not. fold_text folds case, diacritics and whitespace runs and touches nothing else, so those are two different suppliers. The boundary is now asserted explicitly rather than assumed, because the obvious assumption is the wrong one. THE CAP IS NOT COVERED AND IS UNTESTABLE, not untested: it was a property of the dropped backfill and no replacement exists. Recorded in the assertion file's closing comment. Report: docs/reports/2026-09-01-executor-fold-01-supplier-folding.md

cards.notes:
AUTHORED AND SHIPPED 2026-09-01 on the owner's instruction, as its own card and its own PR rather than folded into P3-05b, because it defends coverage that P3-05b removed and the two should be separable in the history.

ONE OF THE THREE BEHAVIOURS THE OWNER NAMED COULD NOT BE REBUILT, and that was reported before building rather than discovered afterwards. Most-common-variant selection and the cap were both properties of backfill_product_suppliers, which 0027 drops. The surviving analogue of most-common-variant selection is the lookup's tie-break, which decides WHICH record a spelling resolves to, and it is covered. The cap has no analogue at all and the assertion file says so in place of a vacuous test.

cards.title: Schema: public.clients authored, with the counterparty fields Rapid Construct actually keeps, plus RLS matching the existing tables.
cards.plain: A customer stops being a name typed into a box and becomes a real record with a fiscal code, an address, a phone number and a contact history. Every job and every delivery can then point at the same customer instead of at five different spellings of it.

PLUS: every one of those assertions PROVED TO FAIL on a mutated copy of the migration, quoted in the report, because a check that has only ever passed is not a check. THE PRODUCTION HALF OF THIS ACCEPTANCE MOVED TO P3-27 VERBATIM AND WAS NOT DROPPED: the migration journal per CLAUDE.md 8.5 and the APPLY-LOG entry per P2-11 are that card, which is blocked on Ivan. cards.defaults: THE MIGRATION NUMBER IS 0013 AND IT IS PINNED NOW THAT THE CARD IS WORKED. 0012 was the highest when this was picked. THIS CARD AUTHORS THE FILE AND DOES NOT APPLY IT, RULED AS R-062. The 2026-08-30 owner dispatch says in terms that nothing in it requires a database connection and that the apply step against production is a separate blocked card. That is the second branch of the paragraph below, reached by an owner instruction rather than by section 8 having been revoked: section 8 has NOT been revoked, P2-13 has not run, and R-001 still stands. The apply card is P3-27. THE PRODUCTION ASSERTIONS ARE NOT LOST, THEY ARE SPLIT. Everything P3-01 asked to see in an apply journal, except the words "on production", is asserted against the AUT-14 container on every push. What P3-27 adds is that the same assertions hold on the real project. COLUMNS, DECIDED HERE SO NOBODY ASKS: id uuid pk; name text not null; type public.client_type not null default 'company'; fiscal_code text null; address text null; phone text null; email text null; notes text null; active boolean not null default true; created_by uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null; created_at, updated_at. TYPE IS AN ENUM, NOT A TEXT COLUMN: create type public.client_type as enum ('company', 'individual'). Two values, exactly the two the card names, and a third one is a migration rather than a typo. FISCAL CODE IS NULLABLE AND ITS LABEL IS IDNO. In Moldova a company carries an IDNO and a private person does not, so a not null constraint would make the individual type unusable on the day it is first needed. Uniqueness is a PARTIAL unique index, `unique (fiscal_code) where fiscal_code is not null`, so two individuals with no IDNO do not collide. No format check and no checksum validation: an IDNO copied off a real contract is the source of truth, and a regex that rejects a valid one is worse than a free text field. NAME IS NOT UNIQUE. Two legally distinct companies can share a trading name and the IDNO is what separates them. A case-insensitive index on name exists for search, not for uniqueness. ACTIVE MEANS HIDDEN FROM PICKERS AND PRESENT IN HISTORY, exactly as products.active already works. There is no delete policy and no delete button. ROMANIAN LABELS, FIXED HERE so the three screens downstream do not each invent their own: Client, Denumire, Tip, Companie, Persoana fizica, IDNO, Adresa, Telefon, Email, Note, Activ. MIGRATION NUMBER IS NOT PINNED ON THIS BOARD. Phase 2 is still running and may consume numbers after 0012, so take the next free number in supabase/migrations at the moment this card is worked, and never renumber an existing file. The acceptance names the file by its SUFFIX for the same reason. THE MIGRATION IS AUTHORED HERE. WHO APPLIES IT IS READ OFF CLAUDE.md SECTION 8 AT THE MOMENT THE CARD IS WORKED, NEVER ASSUMED FROM THIS TEXT. That section has changed three times in four days: R-001 granted EXECUTOR a temporary apply, R-054 recorded that Bash(psql:*) is permitted so a terminal can open a connection at all, and section 8.7 revokes the whole grant at P2-13 and reverts section 8 to Ivan-only applies with no connection from any terminal. WORK IT THIS WAY AND THE CARD IS CORRECT UNDER EITHER: if section 8 still grants a terminal the apply when the card is picked, apply it as a normal three-phase apply under 8.5 and journal all three phases into evidence; if it does not, set blocked_on ivan, write the apply request into question in the section 4 structure, set status blocked and move to the next eligible card. Either way the PR lists the migration file by path in its description, and either way section 8.6 stands: a migration containing DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE or DELETE is never auto-applied, and its exception explicitly does not reach migrations. A MIGRATION FILE IS NEVER EDITED AFTER IT HAS BEEN APPLIED. A correction is a new numbered file. RLS IS COPIED FROM THE EXISTING TABLES, NOT INVENTED. The shape in supabase/migrations/0001_phase2_schema.sql is: enable row level security on the table; a select policy to authenticated using (true); insert and update policies to authenticated gated on public.is_owner(); and NO delete policy for any role, because a row referenced by history cannot disappear without making that history unreadable. cards.title: Schema: public.contacts, belonging to a client, because a construction client is three phone numbers and not one.
cards.plain: A customer can hold several people: the site foreman, the accountant and the owner are three different phone numbers, and the person who answers about a delivery is not the person who answers about an invoice. The system stops pretending a company has one contact.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `ls supabase/migrations/0014_contacts.sql && npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run check:migrations` exits 0. PLUS BEHAVIOURAL, in the same file: three contacts on one client; zero primaries legal; a SECOND primary for one client refused on UPDATE and on INSERT, which is the card named acceptance; a different client keeping its own primary, which is what fails if the index is not partitioned by client_id; the clear-then-set handover working inside one transaction; a client delete cascading to its people and leaving another client untouched; and four shapes of the same phone number stored verbatim. PLUS: every assertion PROVED TO FAIL on a mutated copy of the migration, eight mutations, quoted in the report. THE PRODUCTION HALF OF THIS ACCEPTANCE MOVED TO P3-27 VERBATIM AND WAS NOT DROPPED: the migration journal per CLAUDE.md 8.5 and the APPLY-LOG entry per P2-11 are that card, which is blocked on Ivan. NO TRIGGER AUTO-CLEARS THE PREVIOUS PRIMARY, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. A before-insert trigger demoting the old primary would make the handover automatic, and it would also mean the unique index could never fire, so the card named acceptance, "the partial unique index rejecting a second primary contact", would become unprovable. The card asks for a refusal and says the interface clears the old one in the same transaction. The refusal is what is built. COLUMNS: id uuid pk; client_id uuid not null references public.clients(id) on delete cascade; name text not null; role text null; phone text null; email text null; is_primary boolean not null default false; notes text null; active boolean not null default true; created_at, updated_at. ROLE IS FREE TEXT AND STAYS FREE TEXT, WITH A SUGGESTION LIST IN THE UI. The suggested values offered in the picker are: Sef de santier, Contabil, Administrator, Achizitii, Sofer. A user typing something else is not corrected. THE RULE, FROM P3-03: every project status change writes a public.status_history row, so the path taken is recoverable. Real construction work walks the pipeline backwards, and the path is worth more than the state landed on.

THE CONVENTION TO FOLLOW IS ALREADY IN THE SCHEMA: public.set_inbound_status in 0003 and public.set_outbound_status in 0004 each write the status change and its history row together inside one SQL function, SECURITY INVOKER so RLS still applies. THE FIXTURE FOUND A REAL ORDERING DEFECT THAT PRODUCTION WOULD HAVE HIDDEN FOR MONTHS. public.status_history.created_at defaults to now(), which is the TRANSACTION start time, so five status moves inside one block all landed with the same timestamp and the reader fell through to its tiebreaker, a random uuid. In production each change is its own transaction and this never appears. set_project_status now writes clock_timestamp() explicitly, and the reasoning is in the migration beside the line.

THAT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR FIXTURES THAT DO SEVERAL THINGS AT ONCE. A fixture with one action per transaction would have been more realistic and would have proved less: the collision only exists when two rows are appended together, which is the case a real system reaches under load rather than never.

cards.title: responder.sh stops consuming the owner's rulings: one process reads the bot, and rulings go through the same spool ASK-01 uses.
cards.plain: Fix the bot so that an answer sent while the assistant is replying to chat is not swallowed. At the moment a ruling can vanish before the part of the system that needs it ever sees it.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh` exits 0, extended with a case that PROVES the defect and its fix: a ruling-form message present in the same getUpdates batch as an ordinary chat message is still readable by inbox.mjs AFTER responder.sh has run. The case must FAIL against the current responder.sh and pass after the change, and the PR must show both results. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS: no second process reads the bot; the PR names which single process calls getUpdates and shows that the other reads the spool.
cards.defaults: THE DEFECT IS LIVE AND IS IN THE OWNER'S OWN RULING PATH. scripts/poc/responder.sh polls getUpdates, classifies, deliberately does NOT answer ruling forms because inbox.mjs owns them, and then acknowledges the offset past EVERY update it read, including those rulings. Telegram deletes an update once getUpdates is called with an offset past it, so the ruling is gone before inbox.mjs ever runs. inbox.mjs already prints a line about exactly this failure mode, which is how long it has been known without being fixed. THE FIX SHAPE IS GIVEN BY THE OWNER: route rulings through the same spool ASK-01 uses, so ONE process reads the bot and the other reads a file. Which process keeps the socket is the card's to decide and to record. DO NOT FIX IT BY NARROWING THE OFFSET. Acknowledging only the messages the responder answered would leave ignored messages to be reclassified forever, which is the exact reason the current code acknowledges everything, and that comment is in the file. The answer is one reader, not a cleverer offset. PRIORITY ABOVE WAVE 3, on the owner's instruction: a broken ruling path means every later escalation can be silently lost.

evidence.ref: #PENDING, scripts/poc/ruling-spool.mjs. THE SINGLE READER IS responder.sh, PROVED MECHANICALLY: a grep over scripts/poc for a getUpdates call carrying an offset returns exactly one file, and that assertion is itself one of the thirteen cases. chat-classify.mjs writes ruling forms to the spool; inbox.mjs reads it and no longer calls getUpdates on the ruling path at all. Acceptance: bash scripts/poc/test-ask-digest.sh exits 0 with 85 assertions, thirteen of them new. The failing half is a mutant chat-classify.mjs whose spoolRuling is a no-op that succeeds, which is exactly the pre-card behaviour, and against it the same batch loses the ruling: 'read 0 spooled ruling'.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-01 on the owner's dispatch, from a live defect he hit. Ranked above wave 3 by him, because it breaks the channel every other card's escalation depends on.

RENUMBERED 2026-09-01 SO THE BOARD PREDICTS THE WORK ORDER INSTEAD OF A DISPATCH OVERRIDING IT. These cards were authored as P3-11a and sorted ABOVE P3-12, so CLAUDE.md section 2's lowest-id rule would have pulled them in front of wave 3 while the dispatch said otherwise. The owner's correction is that a board which cannot express the intended order is the defect, not the dispatch that worked around it. The order the ids now produce, unaided: P3-11a (the broken ruling path) and P3-11b (the uninstalled digest agent) come first because both break a channel everything else depends on, then P3-12 and wave 3, then wave 4, then P3-29 to P3-34. Nothing needs to be told to a terminal that the ids do not already say.

SHIPPED 2026-09-02 BY EXECUTOR.

THE SOCKET STAYS WITH responder.sh, AND THAT IS THE CARD'S DECISION TO RECORD. It already holds it, it already polls on the 60 second schedule the owner's answers need, and it already runs chat-classify.mjs, which ASK-01 had ALREADY made the single reader for the answer channel. Moving the socket to inbox.mjs would have put the owner's chat replies on the three hour harness cycle to fix the ruling path, which trades one broken channel for another.

A SECOND SPOOL DIRECTORY, NOT THE ASK SPOOL. An ask answer is consumed by a BLOCKED role within seconds; a ruling is consumed by the next harness run, hours later. One directory holding two lifetimes is a directory whose cleanup rule cannot be stated.

THE FAILURE MODE THAT THE FIX ITSELF COULD HAVE INTRODUCED, AND THE GUARD FOR IT. If the spool write fails, the ruling is lost exactly as before, and worse, because now everyone believes it is on disk. chat-classify.mjs therefore reports TWO outcomes: `ruling` means it reached the spool, `ruling_unspooled` means the write failed. responder.sh acknowledges nothing at or past an unspooled ruling, so a broken disk costs a repeated classification and never a lost decision. Two of the thirteen cases assert exactly that, including the case where the ONLY update is an unspooled ruling and nothing at all is acknowledged.

THE OFFSET WAS NOT NARROWED, WHICH THE CARD FORBIDS. Every ignored message, every question and every routed answer is still acknowledged, so the reclassify loop the old comment warns about needs a message that is read and never acknowledged, and the only message that can now happen to is one whose spool write failed.

THE RESPONDER'S OFFSET PROGRAM IS RUN BY THE TEST, NOT COPIED INTO IT. It sits between EXTRACT-BEGIN and EXTRACT-END fences in responder.sh and the test lifts it out, the same convention test-ask-digest.sh already uses for ask.sh. A copy would drift and the assertion would go on passing about the copy.

CONSUMED, NOT DELETED. inbox.mjs moves a spooled ruling to rulings/consumed rather than removing it, because after this card that file is the ONLY surviving copy: Telegram deleted the original the moment the responder acknowledged it.

cards.title: install.sh installs digest.sh and its launchd agent, and the acceptance is an install-then-invoke rather than a unit test.
cards.plain: The twice-daily summary the owner reads was built and tested but never actually installed on the machine, so it has never run. Install it, and prove it by installing it and running it rather than by testing the code again.
cards.acceptance: NAMED COMMAND, AND IT MUST BE AN INSTALL FOLLOWED BY AN INVOCATION, NOT A UNIT TEST: a script that runs scripts/poc/install.sh into a temporary prefix, then invokes the installed digest at its installed path with --force, and exits 0 only if that invocation produced the digest. It must FAIL against the current install.sh, and the PR must show both results. PLUS: the launchd agent for 08:00 and 19:00 is installed by the same installer and its plist is asserted to exist and to name the installed digest path. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults: THE DEFECT IS THAT SHIPPED IS NOT INSTALLED, AND IT IS THE SAME CLASS AS MERGED IS NOT APPLIED. bash /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin/digest.sh --force returns No such file or directory, so the 08:00 and 19:00 agent does not exist on this machine. DIGEST-01 was proved by tests and never by an install, exactly as the phase 3 migrations were proved by CI and never by an apply. A TEST THAT RUNS THE SOURCE PROVES THE SOURCE. It says nothing about whether the file reached the place the scheduler looks, which is the whole of this card. THE ACCEPTANCE MUST THEREFORE INSTALL. A unit test added here would repeat the mistake that created the card. INSTALL INTO A TEMPORARY PREFIX IN THE TEST, never over the owner's real /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin during a check, because a check that overwrites the thing it is checking is not a check. The real install is a separate deliberate act and the PR says which command performs it. LOOK FOR OTHER FILES THE INSTALLER MISSES while the card is open: the same omission may cover more than digest.sh, and the fix is a list the installer derives rather than a second hardcoded name.

evidence.ref: #PENDING, scripts/poc/test-install.sh, wired into quality as 'Prove the installer by installing and invoking'. 27 assertions, exit 0, and proved on the CI environment itself: docker run --rm -v <clone>:/w -w /w node:20-bookworm bash scripts/poc/test-install.sh passes. The install-then-invoke half: the installed digest runs from its installed path with --force and PRODUCES a digest, 661 bytes on Linux and 1182 on the Mac. The failing half is a mutant install.sh with the two digest manifest rows removed: it still installs the work harness, installs no digest, and invoking the digest it did not install FAILS.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-01 on the owner's dispatch, from a defect he hit by running the command. Numbered P3-11b so the board itself puts it before wave 3, next to P3-11a: both are broken channels that everything else depends on, one the ruling path and one the reporting path.

SHIPPED 2026-09-02 BY EXECUTOR.

THE CARD'S PREMISE ABOUT THE CODE WAS STALE AND THE PREMISE ABOUT THE MACHINE WAS EXACTLY RIGHT. install.sh on main ALREADY carried the digest install: PR #149 added it in the same commit that shipped digest.sh. What was true, and verified on the Mac before any code was written, is that `bash /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin/digest.sh --force` answered 'No such file or directory' and /Users/ivan/rc-poc-bin held only run.sh and responder.sh. THE INSTALLER HAD THE LINES AND HAD NEVER BEEN RUN. So the card is not 'add the digest to the installer', it is the card's own default one level up: SHIPPED IS NOT INSTALLED, and the fix is to make that gap fail rather than to write the lines again.

WHAT MAKES IT FAIL NOW. scripts/poc/test-install.sh installs into a temporary prefix and INVOKES what it installed, and it runs in quality on every pull request. A change that drops a file from the installer goes red.

THE INSTALLER IS ONE LIST NOW. Three agents were three copy-pasted blocks of eight lines. The manifest is one table and every loop derives from it, and the installer asserts its own installed count against the row count, because a loop that reads zero rows installs nothing and reports every step it did not take as a step that did not fail.

THE OTHER FILE THE INSTALLER MISSED, WHICH THE CARD TOLD ME TO LOOK FOR. The rulings spool directories. P3-11a added the spool and its module creates the directory on first write, which is precisely the race the installer's own comment about asks/ exists to prevent: the writer is chat-classify.mjs running inside the responder, and it must never create a directory it then races the next poll to fill. rulings/pending and rulings/consumed are in the derived list now.

TWO PORTABILITY CHANGES, BOTH REQUIRED BY THE ACCEPTANCE RATHER THAN CHOSEN. POC_INSTALL_ROOT, so the installer can be run somewhere other than over the owner's live installation, which is why nobody had ever run it. And digest.sh's PATH now PREPENDS the owner's directories instead of replacing PATH: on the Mac the same directories still win in the same order, but on a Linux runner node is under /opt/hostedtoolcache and the old line meant the invocation half of the acceptance could not run anywhere. An installer proved only by an invocation that cannot run is the same gap one level up.

THE MUTANT WAS BUILT BY grep -v FIRST AND THAT WAS WRONG. Removing the two digest rows with grep also removed the last line of the POC_MANIFEST string, which is where its closing quote lives; the string swallowed everything after it and the mutant died on a syntax error. A mutant that dies installs no digest either, so the assertion would have passed while proving nothing. It is built by parsing now, and it is asserted to PARSE and to RUN before it is asserted to lack a digest.

THE REAL INSTALL IS STILL A SEPARATE DELIBERATE ACT, as the card requires. The command is `bash scripts/poc/install.sh`, run from main after this and P3-11a have merged, so the responder.sh it deploys is the one carrying the ruling spool.

cards.title: check:removal-safety, the guard for the direction INC-05's guard cannot see: deployed code still reading schema a pending migration removes.
cards.plain: Stop the system from deleting something out of the database while the live site is still asking for it. That mistake took the site down once already, and the existing safety check only looks the other way round.
cards.question:
DECISION NEEDED: can the applier assert that a fix is DEPLOYED, not merely merged, before a removal migration runs?
CONTEXT: the ordering rule is that a removal applies after the code that stops reading it is merged AND DEPLOYED. The merged half is asserted by check:removal-safety. The deployed half cannot be asserted from here: VERCEL_TOKEN exists in the permitted secret read but is EMPTY, and production exposes no endpoint reporting the commit it is serving. Inventing a substitute for 'deployed' is the exact class of guess that produced INC-06.
OPTIONS: (a) add a small public endpoint that reports the commit the live site is running, and have the applier read it; (b) provide a real VERCEL_TOKEN so the applier can ask the deployments API; (c) leave it as an operator statement, RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED=yes, recorded in the journal.
RECOMMENDATION: (a). It needs no new credential, it is the deployed build reporting its own identity rather than a proxy for it, and it works for any host.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: the applier refuses every removal migration on production unless the operator states the deploy has landed, which is safe and is the current behaviour. Nothing is blocked except unattended removals.
cards.acceptance: NAMED COMMAND: `npm run check:removal-safety` exits 0 on a clean tree and is wired into quality.yml as its own step. IT MUST BE PROVEN AGAINST BOTH INCIDENTS RECONSTRUCTED AS FIXTURES, and each must FAIL the check: the INC-05 forward case, merged code reading schema a pending migration ADDS, and the INC-06 reverse case, deployed code reading schema a pending migration REMOVES. The PR shows both failures and the clean pass. PLUS: the applier refuses to apply a batch containing a removal while the check is red, proven by a case in prove-applier.mjs. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults: INC-05 AND INC-06 ARE ONE DEFECT IN TWO DIRECTIONS AND EACH HAS COST AN OUTAGE. check:pending-schema-reads compares MERGED CODE against the PENDING REGISTER, so it guards additive drift only, by construction: it cannot see deployed code reading schema that was just removed, because that code is already on main and the register is already clear. ENUMERATE AGAINST THE TABLE, NEVER GREP THE COLUMN NAME WITH EXCLUSIONS. That filter is exactly what hid lib/data/extraction-actions.ts:269 during P3-05b, where a write to the products table lived in a file named for extraction and a grep excluding 'extraction' skipped it. Find every read and write of the TABLE first, then look inside those for the object. THE ORDERING RULE IS ENCODED AS A MACHINE CONDITION, NOT PROSE: additive migrations apply BEFORE the code that reads them merges; removal migrations apply AFTER the code that stops reading them is merged AND DEPLOYED. DEPLOYED IS NOT MERGED AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE OF INC-06. Whether the applier can assert deployment is a question for the owner and not for a proxy: there is no usable Vercel credential in the permitted secret read, and inventing a substitute for 'deployed' is the exact class of mistake this card exists to stop. Ask, do not guess.

evidence.ref: npm run prove:schema-direction -> 6 of 6 passed, exit 0. BOTH OUTAGES RECONSTRUCTED AND EACH FAILS ITS GUARD ON DEMAND: the INC-05 forward case (merged code reading schema a pending migration ADDS) is refused by check:pending-schema-reads, and the INC-06 reverse case (code still reading schema a pending migration REMOVES) is refused by the new check:removal-safety. A clean removal with no reader left still passes, so the guard does not block every drop forever. THE INC-06 FIXTURE PUTS ITS READER IN A FILE NAMED FOR EXTRACTION ON PURPOSE, and a third assertion proves the reader was NAMED in the output: that is the exact shape a grep with `grep -v extraction` skipped during P3-05b, and enumeration is now against the TABLE with no exclusions. THE APPLIER REFUSES A REMOVAL TWICE OVER, both proven: exit 2 while any reader remains, and exit 2 on production while the deploy is unconfirmed, becoming exit 0 only when the operator states RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED=yes. Proven through a new dry-run mode that evaluates every gate and exits before the first psql call, so a fixture tree can never reach a database. npm run check:removal-safety and npm run prove:schema-direction are both wired into quality.yml as their own steps. Full gate green: all seven checks, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0, and prove:applier 14 of 14. THE DEPLOYED HALF IS NOT ASSERTED AND IS NOT FAKED: there is no usable Vercel credential in the permitted secret read (VERCEL_TOKEN is declared and empty), so the applier asserts the MERGED half and refuses on the DEPLOYED half until the owner rules. Question sent to him via ask.sh, Telegram message 33. Report: docs/reports/2026-09-01-executor-p3-11c-removal-safety.md

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-01 on the owner's dispatch, after INC-06 took six production screens down by applying a removal migration before its code was merged. INC-05 was the same defect in the opposite direction.

SHIPPED 2026-09-01. The card is shipped and its ONE open question is recorded above rather than blocking it: the merged half is built, proven and wired, and the deployed half refuses safely until the owner rules. Under CLAUDE.md 4b that is a question that parks a clause, not a run.

THREE DEFECTS WERE FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING THIS, all the same class as the pending-register regex from P3-04b: tooling that folds a card id must fold BOTH SIDES of every comparison. (1) ask.mjs upper-cased the card id and then looked for it verbatim on the board, so ask.sh sent the owner a question to Telegram and then died with 'no board named P3-11C', leaving a question he could see and no card it could be written onto. (2) THE SAME DEFECT IN inbox.mjs REJECTED THE OWNER'S OWN RULINGS: the ruling form is upper-cased and compared against a set of verbatim board ids, so `R P3-11a default` answered 'no card P3-11A on the board'. Every card with a lower-case suffix was unrulable, which is P3-04b, P3-05b, P3-11a through P3-11d, P3-13b and P3-13c. (3) This file's own fixture harness passed absolute override paths through path.join(ROOT, ...), which produced directories that do not exist and were filtered away silently, leaving the check scanning nothing and reporting OK. That last one is the same silent-pass shape the card exists to stop, so the check now exits 2 rather than reporting OK when it has no source directory to scan.

cards.title: A green check on a conflicting pull request reads as stale, not as green: report mergeStateStatus beside every check result.
cards.plain: When a pull request clashes with the main branch, its tests do not run at all, but the old result still shows as passing. Make the tools say so, because that hid a broken fix for about an hour during an outage.
cards.acceptance: NAMED COMMAND: a helper, `npm run checks:<name>` or a script under scripts/, that takes a PR number and prints the required check result BESIDE mergeStateStatus, and EXITS NON-ZERO when the check reads green while the PR is DIRTY or BEHIND, because that green belongs to an older sha. It must be proven on a reconstructed case: a fixture where the recorded check is success and the state is DIRTY exits non-zero with a sentence naming the staleness. PLUS: CLAUDE.md section 3 is extended from merging to WAITING, in the same PR, saying that a conflicting PR triggers no workflow and that a green check on one is evidence about a commit nobody is proposing to merge. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults: THE TRAP IS ALREADY NAMED FOR MERGING AND WAS NOT NAMED FOR WAITING, and the difference cost about an hour of the INC-06 outage. A conflicting pull request triggers ZERO workflows. The fix for the outage was pushed, no run started, and `gh pr checks` kept reporting the success of the previous sha, so the terminal waited on a fix that was not moving and had no signal that it was not moving. THE HELPER IS A REPORTING TOOL, NOT A GATE ON MERGING. Section 3.1 already forbids merging on anything but a run for the head sha; this card is about the case where nobody is merging yet and is simply waiting. DO NOT SOLVE IT BY POLLING HARDER. The signal is mergeStateStatus, which is available immediately and for free, and the answer is to read it rather than to infer staleness from a run that never appears.

evidence.ref: npm run prove:pr-state -> 4 of 4 passed, exit 0. Reporter: scripts/poc-free/pr-check-state.mjs, run as npm run checks:state <pr>. It prints the required check BESIDE mergeStateStatus and the head sha, and exits non-zero when a green result belongs to a commit nobody is proposing to merge. PROVEN AGAINST STATES THAT ACTUALLY OCCURRED: dirty-but-green.json is PR #148 exactly as it stood during INC-06 (the fix for a six-screen outage, pushed, CONFLICTING, no run started, quality reporting SUCCESS from the previous sha) and behind-but-green.json is PR #130 on 2026-08-31. Both exit 1 naming the staleness; the DIRTY case says in terms that a conflicting pull request triggers zero workflows. clean-and-green.json exits 0, so it does not cry stale at every healthy pull request. CLAUDE.md section 3 extended in the same PR from MERGING to WAITING. Report: docs/reports/2026-09-01-executor-p3-11d-stale-checks.md

cards.title: Budget versus deviz versus actual: the project budget, the accepted estimate total and the real material cost, three numbers side by side on project detail.
cards.plain: A job shows what it was budgeted at, what it was quoted at, and what it has actually cost so far, all three at once and without anyone having to open anything. Those are three different questions and today the business can answer none of them.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/project-budget.spec.ts` exits 0. project-budget.spec covers: project detail shows THREE numbers, budget_mdl, the accepted deviz total and the actual issued cost, all three visible without expanding anything; the variance and the percentage consumed are computed against the BUDGET and are labelled as such; a project with a budget and no accepted deviz shows the budget, a Romanian empty state for the estimate, and the actual, and does not collapse to two numbers; a project with an accepted deviz and no budget shows the estimate and the actual and a Romanian empty state for the budget, and the percentage consumed is a Romanian dash rather than a division by zero; a project with neither shows the actual and two empty states; the accepted deviz total matches the deviz screen for the same project, to the last bani; every visible string is Romanian. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults: RESOLVED 2026-08-30 BY RULING R-058, IN FAVOUR OF THE OWNER ADDENDUM. The authored version of this card predates the addendum and disagreed with it in twelve places, two of them outright contradictions. Section 4 of docs/reports/2026-08-28-executor-phase-3-crm-preflight.md is the delta, item by item. Where this card and that report disagree, this card is the resolution and the report is the record of what was resolved. THREE NUMBERS, NOT TWO, AND ALL THREE UNCOLLAPSED ON PROJECT DETAIL. That was delta 12. The authored card was budget versus actual and the accepted deviz total was absent, which leaves the one number a reader needs to tell an over-budget job from an under-quoted one off the screen. THEY ARE THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS: budget_mdl is what the business decided to spend, the accepted deviz total is what the client agreed to pay for, and the actual is what has left the warehouse. Any two of them tell an incomplete story. THE ACCEPTED DEVIZ TOTAL IS THE CURRENT ACCEPTED VERSION'S TOTAL, computed the same way P3-13b computes it, INCLUDING the Adaos row from margin_percent, so the two screens cannot disagree. A project with no accepted deviz shows a Romanian empty state, never a zero: zero is a number and an absent estimate is not. VARIANCE AND PERCENTAGE CONSUMED ARE AGAINST THE BUDGET, and are labelled so that nobody reads them as against the estimate. A second variance against the deviz is a reasonable thing to want and is not in this card; adding it is a follow-up, not a default. A NULL BUDGET IS NORMAL AND IS NOT AN ERROR. P3-03 made budget_mdl nullable because a lead has no budget yet. The percentage consumed against a null or zero budget is a Romanian dash. THE THREE NUMBERS ARE THE SUMMARY AND THE BREAKDOWN IS BEHIND A DRILL-IN, per the density doctrine below. ROMANIAN LABELS: Buget, Total deviz acceptat, Cost real, Abatere, Consumat. DENSITY DOCTRINE BINDS THIS CARD. Summary first, detail behind a drill-in. A full-length table is never dumped into a page. A list surface shows the smallest set of columns that lets a person choose a row, and everything else lives on the row detail. THE NUMBERS, SO THAT "COMPACT" IS NOT A MATTER OF TASTE: a summary block on a page that is not itself a list shows AT MOST 5 ROWS and carries a link to the full history. A list page paginates at 25 rows and never renders an unbounded table. A row detail opens in the existing side panel pattern where one already exists on that screen, and as a route otherwise. DESKTOP FIRST. Responsive and mobile layouts are out of scope, per CLAUDE.md section 11. ROMANIAN WITH DIACRITICS ON EVERY STRING, including empty states, error messages, column headers, button labels and tooltips. No English string reaches the UI. THE EXISTING VISUAL LANGUAGE IS REUSED, NOT REPLACED. components/ui/primitives.tsx, components/ui/StatCard.tsx, components/ui/Icon.tsx and the existing side panel components are the vocabulary. A new component is added only when no existing one fits, and a redesign of the shell is scope this card does not have. HALT ON AN ABSENT TOOL OR A FALSE PREMISE. If this card names a table, column, route, file, script, environment variable or service that does not exist, or asserts a fact the repository contradicts, do not build the missing thing on a guess and do not invent the tool. Stop working the card, set status blocked, set blocked_on to the person who owes the correction, and write into question the structured decision-needed text naming the premise and pasting the command output that disproves it. Then move to the next eligible card.

THREE numbers on project detail, uncollapsed and behind no click: Buget, Total deviz acceptat, Cost real, plus Abatere fata de buget and Consumat din buget. The seven cases are the card's seven clauses: all three present on the seeded cost project; variance and consumed computed and LABELLED against the budget; a budget with no accepted deviz keeps three blocks with a Romanian empty state and does not collapse to two; an accepted deviz with no budget shows a Romanian dash rather than a division by zero; neither shows the actual and two empty states; the accepted total matches the deviz tab's own data-value-mdl to the bani; every visible string Romanian.

cards.notes:
SOURCE: Ivan's platform review with Mihai, 2026-08-27.

READS THE COST MODULE, NEVER REIMPLEMENTS IT. If this card finds itself writing a second sum over outbound_lines, that is the defect. The dependency exists for that reason and not merely for ordering.

THE SAME CURRENT-CATALOGUE-VALUE CAVEAT FROM THE COST CARD APPLIES HERE AND IS INHERITED, not restated on the screen twice.

REWRITTEN 2026-08-30 UNDER R-058, delta 12. The accepted deviz total was absent from the authored card and the addendum names all three numbers as belonging on project detail, uncollapsed.

IT NOW DEPENDS ON P3-13b, WHICH IS A NEW EDGE. The accepted deviz total cannot be computed before deviz lines exist. The edge is on the line editor rather than on the schema because the total includes the Adaos row, and the rule for computing that total is fixed by P3-13b rather than by the migration.

SHIPPED 2026-09-02 BY EXECUTOR.

NOTHING IS RECALCULATED, WHICH IS THE CARD'S OWN WARNING. lib/reporting/project-budget.ts takes the cost from lib/reporting/material-cost.ts and the accepted total from the SAME DevizSummary list that the deviz tab renders, built by devizTotals with the Adaos included. The two screens therefore cannot disagree by construction rather than by care, and case 6 proves it on the raw data-value-mdl rather than on the formatted text: formatMoney rounds to the leu on both screens, so a text comparison would pass even when the two numbers differ by bani.

A GAP IS NOT A ZERO, AND THAT IS THE RULE MOST EASILY BROKEN. A project with no budget does not have a budget of zero, it has a budget nobody has decided yet. Each absence carries Romanian text and never a figure. The Cost real block deliberately has NO empty text: zero issues really does mean zero lei left the warehouse, which is a fact and not a gap, so giving it one would be code nothing could reach.

A ZERO BUDGET DOES NOT DIVIDE EITHER. budget_mdl is nullable because a lead has none, but zero is also a value somebody can save, and dividing by it yields Infinity, which renders as an enormous and entirely real-looking percentage. Both cases give null and null renders as a dash.

THE DEFECT THIS CARD FOUND IN ITS OWN TEST. The helper accepted a deviz and then waited for deviz-locked, which is true for ANY status other than draft and was therefore ALREADY TRUE after the send. The wait passed instantly, the detail page was read before the acceptance reached the database, and the screen correctly reported no accepted deviz while the failure looked like a defect in the screen. From accepted there is no onward transition, so the status buttons disappear: that is the only condition which becomes true only after acceptance, and it is what the helper waits on now.

cards.title: Schema: public.devize and public.deviz_lines, versioned, with the five-state pipeline and the unit price frozen on the line at the moment it is quoted.
cards.plain: The estimates a job is quoted on become real records, each one a numbered version that is never quietly edited once it has left the office, and each line remembering the price it was quoted at rather than whatever the price happens to be today.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `ls supabase/migrations/*_deviz.sql && npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run check:migrations` exits 0, which applies the new file to a bare postgres:16 unmodified and is the proof required before the file is merged. PLUS MIGRATION JOURNAL recorded as this card evidence per CLAUDE.md 8.5, showing: public.devize and public.deviz_lines present; rowsecurity true on both; three policies and NO delete policy on each; the enum public.deviz_status carrying exactly five values in this order, draft, sent, accepted, rejected, expired; the unique index on (project_id, version) and the unique index on (deviz_id, product_id); the foreign key from deviz_lines to devize on delete cascade and from deviz_lines to products on delete restrict; the check constraint pinning currency to MDL; and the check constraint rejecting quantity <= 0. PLUS APPLY LOG entry per P2-11 if and when the file is applied.
cards.defaults: RESOLVED 2026-08-30 BY RULING R-058, IN FAVOUR OF THE OWNER ADDENDUM. The authored version of this card predates the addendum and disagreed with it in twelve places, two of them outright contradictions. Section 4 of docs/reports/2026-08-28-executor-phase-3-crm-preflight.md is the delta, item by item. Where this card and that report disagree, this card is the resolution and the report is the record of what was resolved. TABLE NAMES ARE THE ADDENDUM'S: public.devize and public.deviz_lines. The authored card called the parent deviz_versions; the addendum calls it devize, which is also the Romanian plural and therefore already obeys the "tables plural" convention in supabase/migrations/0001_phase2_schema.sql. ONE ROW OF devize IS ONE VERSION. Versioning is not a second table. COLUMNS ON public.devize, THE ADDENDUM FIELD LIST FIRST AND THE STRUCTURAL COLUMNS AFTER IT: id uuid pk; project_id uuid not null references public.projects(id) on delete restrict; name text null; version integer not null; status public.deviz_status not null default 'draft'; currency public.currency_code not null default 'MDL'; margin_percent numeric(6,2) not null default 0 check (margin_percent >= 0); valid_until date null; notes text null; approved_at timestamptz null; created_by uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null; created_at, updated_at; unique (project_id, version). THE STATUS ENUM IS FIVE VALUES AND THE ADDENDUM FIXED THE SET: create type public.deviz_status as enum ('draft', 'sent', 'accepted', 'rejected', 'expired'). THE STORED TOKENS ARE ENGLISH AND THE LABELS ARE THE ADDENDUM'S ROMANIAN WORDS, WHICH IS THE ONE PLACE THIS CARD DOES NOT COPY THE ADDENDUM'S STRING VERBATIM, AND THE REASON IS WRITTEN OUT SO NOBODY HAS TO GUESS. The addendum names the pipeline "draft, emis, acceptat, respins, expirat", which is one English word and four Romanian ones. That is a list of UI states, not a list of SQL tokens: P2-01 fixed the convention that stored enum values are English tokens and Romanian labels live in the presentation layer, and public.project_status on P3-03 already follows it with lead/offer/contract/active/suspended/closed labelled Prospect/Oferta/Contract/In lucru/Suspendat/Inchis. THE ADDENDUM IS FOLLOWED ON THE THING IT IS ABOUT, which is WHICH FIVE STATES EXIST, THEIR ORDER, and that only accepted feeds the procurement card. LABELS: Ciorna, Emis, Acceptat, Respins, Expirat. COLUMNS ON public.deviz_lines: id uuid pk; deviz_id uuid not null references public.devize(id) on delete cascade; product_id uuid not null references public.products(id) on delete restrict; quantity numeric(14,3) not null check (quantity > 0); unit_price_mdl numeric(14,2) not null check (unit_price_mdl >= 0); line_note text null; sort_order integer not null default 0; created_at, updated_at; unique (deviz_id, product_id). THE MONEY COLUMN IS unit_price_mdl AND NOT unit_price. That is not a spec change: every money column already in this schema carries the currency suffix (unit_value_mdl, sale_price_mdl, budget_mdl) and a single unsuffixed one would be the odd column that a later reader has to check. THE UNIT IS INHERITED FROM THE PRODUCT AND IS NOT A COLUMN HERE. The addendum says "unit (inherited, not re-entered)" and that is the whole rule: the line renders products.unit and nobody types it. NOTE THAT THIS IS THE DELIBERATE OPPOSITE OF THE PRICE RULE ON THE SAME ROW, and both are right. A unit is a property of the product and does not change because of who is being quoted. A price is a promise made on a day. THE PRICE IS A SNAPSHOT AND THE SCHEMA IS WHERE THAT BECOMES TRUE. unit_price_mdl is written at line creation from the catalogue and never updated by anything except a person editing a draft. NO VIEW, FUNCTION OR QUERY IN THIS CARD OR ANY LATER ONE JOINS A DEVIZ LINE TO THE LIVE CATALOGUE PRICE TO PRODUCE THE QUOTED FIGURE. The addendum names this as one of the two paths that "silently degrade to something plausible and wrong", and a default-and-override is exactly that degradation: it looks identical on the day it is written and diverges silently three months later. CURRENCY IS A COLUMN BECAUSE THE ADDENDUM LISTS IT, AND A CHECK CONSTRAINT PINS IT TO MDL FOR THIS PHASE: check (currency = 'MDL'). P3-03 already ruled multi-currency out of scope, and every wave 3 computation sums MDL. Storing a currency the arithmetic ignores would be the third silent-wrong-number path on this board. The constraint is what a later card relaxes, and CLAUDE.md 8.6 already permits ALTER TABLE DROP CONSTRAINT for exactly this: a constraint is replaced, never edited. margin_percent IS ON THE DEVIZ, NOT ON THE LINE, AND IT APPLIES TO THE TOTAL. The addendum lists it in the devize field list and lists no per-line margin column, so a per-line markup would need a column the addendum did not ask for. Foot rows are Subtotal, Adaos, Total. valid_until IS RECORDED AND IS NOT ENFORCED BY A JOB. Nothing in this card flips a status on a date. A deviz still sent whose valid_until has passed is DISPLAYED as expired with a Romanian warning; the enum value is set by a person. A scheduler is a separate card and inventing one here is scope. approved_at IS SET WHEN status BECOMES accepted, and is null otherwise. ONE PRODUCT APPEARS AT MOST ONCE PER DEVIZ, enforced by the unique index, so the comparison in P3-13c is a clean join. A user needing two lines of the same product is adding quantity, not lines. Retained from the authored card: the addendum does not contradict it and the comparison depends on it. A DEVIZ IS VERSIONED, NOT EDITED IN PLACE, ONCE IT LEAVES DRAFT. A draft is freely editable. Anything past draft is superseded by a new version rather than changed, because a client who received an estimate holds a copy of it and a silently edited estimate is a dispute, and because the addendum says the prior version is evidence in a renegotiation. THE CURRENT DEVIZ IS THE HIGHEST version ON THE PROJECT. THE CURRENT ACCEPTED DEVIZ IS THE HIGHEST version WHOSE status IS accepted, and that is the one and only thing the procurement card reads. The two are different queries and both are needed. ENFORCEMENT OF THE NO-EDIT RULE IS A TRIGGER IN THIS MIGRATION, NOT A CHECK IN THE INTERFACE: a before-update trigger on deviz_lines and on the editable columns of devize raises when the parent deviz status is not draft. A rule the database does not hold is a rule the next screen forgets. MIGRATION NUMBER IS NOT PINNED ON THIS BOARD. Phase 2 is still running and may consume numbers after 0012, so take the next free number in supabase/migrations at the moment this card is worked, and never renumber an existing file. The acceptance names the file by its SUFFIX for the same reason. THE MIGRATION IS AUTHORED HERE. WHO APPLIES IT IS READ OFF CLAUDE.md SECTION 8 AT THE MOMENT THE CARD IS WORKED, NEVER ASSUMED FROM THIS TEXT. That section has changed three times in four days: R-001 granted EXECUTOR a temporary apply, R-054 recorded that Bash(psql:*) is permitted so a terminal can open a connection at all, and section 8.7 revokes the whole grant at P2-13 and reverts section 8 to Ivan-only applies with no connection from any terminal. P2-13 is a phase 2 card and this is a phase 3 board, so by the time these cards are worked the likely state is Ivan-only. WORK IT THIS WAY AND THE CARD IS CORRECT UNDER EITHER: if section 8 still grants a terminal the apply when the card is picked, apply it as a normal three-phase apply under 8.5 and journal all three phases into evidence; if it does not, set blocked_on ivan, write the apply request into question in the section 4 structure, set status blocked and move to the next eligible card. Either way the PR lists the migration file by path in its description, and either way section 8.6 stands: a migration containing DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE or DELETE is never auto-applied, and its exception explicitly does not reach migrations. A MIGRATION FILE IS NEVER EDITED AFTER IT HAS BEEN APPLIED. A correction is a new numbered file. RLS IS COPIED FROM THE EXISTING TABLES, NOT INVENTED. The shape in supabase/migrations/0001_phase2_schema.sql is: enable row level security on the table; a select policy to authenticated using (true); insert and update policies to authenticated gated on public.is_owner(); and NO delete policy for any role, because a row referenced by history cannot disappear without making that history unreadable. Deactivation is an active boolean, deletion is not a feature. anon is revoked explicitly rather than assumed, because Supabase grants anon and authenticated at CREATE TABLE time from project-level default privileges. A free-floating return with no source is an inbound delivery, which the system already has, and conflating the two would let stock be created out of nothing through a screen with no supplier and no document behind it. OVER-RETURN IS IMPOSSIBLE, ENFORCED IN THE DATABASE AND NOT ONLY IN THE FORM: the sum of returned quantity per outbound_line_id may never exceed that line quantity. Implement as a trigger or a checked function in the same migration, matching how the existing stock functions in 0003 and 0004 are written. A UI-only check is not a check. STOCK IS COMPUTED, NOT STORED, and the existing computation is extended rather than replaced: whatever function or view already derives available stock from batches minus issues gains minus-returns as a third term, in one place. Reading the current implementation first is part of this card, and if the computation turns out to be duplicated across screens, unifying it is in scope because the alternative is a return that raises stock on one screen and not on another. A RETURN IS NOT A DELETION AND NOT AN EDIT OF THE ISSUE. The issue stays exactly as it was. History is append-only across this whole system and this card does not make the first exception. THE RETURNED VALUE USES THE SAME BASIS AS THE COST REPORT, current unit_value_mdl, so a return credits a project by the same measure the issue debited it and the two cannot drift apart within one screen. THE SCREEN LIVES ON THE EXISTING IESIRI SECTION as a second action on an issue, not as a new nav entry. A follow-up has no product and a client can have many. THE RESOLUTION, DECIDED HERE SO NOBODY HAS TO ASK: DO NOT loosen product_id to nullable and DO NOT drop the unique constraint. Those two objects are what make the stock reminder correct, the email sender in P2-10 depends on them, and relaxing them to fit a second feature is how a working feature acquires a bug. Instead author public.crm_notes (id; client_id null; project_id null; exactly-one-of check as on documents; body text not null; follow_up_on date null; follow_up_done_at timestamptz null; created_by; created_at; updated_at; edited_at timestamptz null) and give the REMINDERS SCREEN a second source. cards.title: Necesar de materiale: for projects in lead, offer, contract or active with an ACCEPTED deviz, what they still need after what has already been issued, against current stock.
cards.plain: For every job that is quoted, signed or under way, the system works out what material is still to come, subtracts what has already gone out to site, and compares the rest with what is in the warehouse. It is the difference between buying ahead and reacting to an empty shelf.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/procurement.spec.ts` exits 0. procurement.spec covers: projects whose status is lead, offer, contract OR active and which carry a current ACCEPTED deviz are included, and A PROJECT IN active WITH AN ACCEPTED DEVIZ IS INCLUDED; a project in suspended or closed is excluded even with an accepted deviz; a project whose only deviz is draft, sent, rejected or expired is EXCLUDED and is reported in the excluded count, because only accepted feeds this screen; a project with no deviz at all is excluded and is REPORTED in a Romanian count of excluded projects rather than silently omitted, with a link to them; the required quantity per product is the sum of accepted-deviz line quantities across the included projects MINUS the quantity already issued to those projects for that product, floored at zero; a project whose issued quantity for a product already exceeds its estimate contributes zero for that product and not a negative number; the shortfall is required minus current stock, floored at zero, and a product with enough stock shows no shortfall; a product required by two projects aggregates to one row and the contributing projects are shown per row; the requirement is broken down by project status and is NOT weighted by probability; every visible string is Romanian. cards.title: Localisation sweep: fix the known English leaks, sweep every user-facing path, and add a CI check that fails on a hardcoded English string.
cards.plain: English words that slipped into the Romanian interface are removed, and from then on the build refuses any change that adds another one. The client sees one language, everywhere, permanently.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npm run check:i18n` exits 0 on the swept tree, AND exits 1 with a named file and line when run against a copy with a hardcoded English user-facing string reintroduced. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE PROVEN AND PASTED AS EVIDENCE: a check that has never been seen to fail is not a check. PLUS the step is wired into .github/workflows/quality.yml under the existing `quality` job, not as a second job, because a second job would not be a required check. PLUS NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/localisation.spec.ts` exits 0, asserting that the file input on the upload screen renders a Romanian label and that the orders side panel renders no English string, which are the two leaks named in the review. SECOND HALF, ADDED 2026-08-31 BY RULING R-079, AND IT IS A SEPARATE ASSERTION RATHER THAN A WIDENING OF THE WORDLIST: `npm run check:i18n` ALSO exits 1, with a named file and line, when a Romanian word is spelled without its diacritics, proved against a copy of the tree with `Ciorna` reintroduced in place of `Ciornă`. THE MECHANISM IS A COMMITTED DENYLIST OF PAIRS, correct form and forbidden ASCII form, seeded with at least the pair that has already cost a run: the deviz draft label, correct `Ciornă`, forbidden `Ciorna`. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE PROVEN AND PASTED, exactly as the English half already requires: the check is seen to go red on the forbidden spelling and green once it is corrected. IT IS EXPLICITLY NOT A HEURISTIC over strings with no diacritics in them, and a pull request implementing it as one does not satisfy this clause.

THE CHECK IS A SCRIPT IN scripts/poc-free/, matching where check-categories.mjs and check-no-prod-target.mjs already live, run through an npm script named check:i18n, zero dependencies, read-only, no network. Every existing check in that folder has that shape and this one does not invent a different one. WHAT THE CHECK SCANS: string and template literals and JSX text in app/, components/ and lib/ that reach a user. WHAT IT IGNORES, and this list is the difference between a useful check and one that gets disabled within a week: import paths and module specifiers; route paths and hrefs; className and style values; data-testid and aria attribute NAMES though not aria-label VALUES; console output; code comments; type names and identifiers; and any file under tests/ or scripts/. A check with no escape hatch gets deleted the first time it is wrong; a check whose exceptions are visible and counted stays. THE SWEEP FIXES WHAT IT FINDS.
