cards.notes:
AUTHORED AND SHIPPED 2026-08-31 on the owner's dispatch. This card exists because P3-27 was blocked on ivan with no ruling that could unblock it, and the missing thing was authority rather than code.

WHAT SHIPPED: ruling R-082, an amendment to CLAUDE.md 8.6, scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs with 11 SQL assertions, and scripts/poc-free/local-db/prove-applier.mjs which proves it three ways against the AUT-14 shim.

THREE DEFECTS IN THE APPLIER WERE FOUND BY THE MUTATIONS AND NOT BY READING, which is the argument for building the proof harness first. (1) pg_get_function_identity_arguments returns parameter NAMES as well as types, so both the 0018 gate and the signature assertion were comparing against a string that never matches; the gate was silently skipping and reporting nothing to drop. Both now compare format_type over proargtypes. (2) the transaction-control locator used the grammar's stmt_location, which points at the start of a statement INCLUDING its leading comments, so it blanked a comment instead of the keyword; it now scans dollar-quote-masked text and is held to the grammar's own count and order. (3) the harness's own 0018 mutation used a plain string replace, which hit the copy of the DROP statement quoted in that file's header comment rather than the statement, so the mutation changed nothing and passed; it is anchored to the start of a line now.

NO PRODUCTION CONNECTION WAS MADE BY THIS CARD. The applier's path overrides are honoured only when RC_APPLY_TARGET=shim, so the mutated trees the proof harness builds cannot be pointed at the client's database even by accident.

P3-27 IS STILL BLOCKED ON IVAN and this card does not unblock it: it makes the apply possible, and the run is a separate act. The report carries the exact DROP statement so it can be quoted to him before that run, and it carries one operational risk he has to see first: hasPhase3Schema() is memoised for 60 seconds, so for up to a minute after the commit a warm server can still take the four-argument fallback branch in lib/data/outbound-actions.ts, which 0018 has just dropped.

cards.title: Schema and module: outbound_lines freezes the unit value at the moment of issue, so a project cost total stops moving when somebody edits a product price.
cards.plain: A job's material cost is worked out from today's product prices, so changing a price silently rewrites what past jobs appear to have cost. This records the price onto the release at the moment it happens, the way an invoice does, and the warning currently printed on the screen comes off.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/project-cost-snapshot.spec.ts` exits 0. The spec covers, and the second case is the whole card: an issue is created against a project and the project cost total is read; the product's `unit_value_mdl` is then changed in the catalogue; the project cost total is UNCHANGED, to the leu, on both the total and the by-product breakdown; a NEW issue of the SAME product raised after the price change is costed at the NEW value, so one project legitimately holds two different unit values for one product and the total is their sum; a row issued before this migration still carries a value and is not null and not zero; and the Romanian footnote naming the current-catalogue caveat is GONE from the Cost tab, because it has stopped being true. PLUS `ls supabase/migrations/*_outbound_unit_value_at_issue.sql` exits 0, and `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 with that file in the set applied to the bare postgres.
cards.defaults:
THE COLUMN IS `unit_value_at_issue_mdl` ON `public.outbound_lines`, numeric(14,2) not null check (>= 0). The name is the one the AUTHOR wrote on P3-11 and it carries the currency suffix every other money column in this schema carries (unit_value_mdl, sale_price_mdl, budget_mdl, unit_price_mdl).

NOT NULL WITH A BACKFILL, NEVER NULLABLE WITH A FALLBACK. Add the column nullable, backfill every existing row from products.unit_value_mdl, then set not null in the same migration and the same transaction. A nullable column read as `coalesce(unit_value_at_issue_mdl, p.unit_value_mdl)` is a default-and-override, not a snapshot: it is indistinguishable from correct on the day it is built and diverges silently afterwards. R-058 named exactly that shape on the deviz price and rejected it, and the same reasoning binds here.

THE BACKFILL IS HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT CANNOT KNOW, IN A COMMENT IN THE FILE. Rows issued before this migration get today's catalogue value because no other value has ever existed. That is not a repair of history and the comment says so: this card freezes the value from now on, and the rows it backfills keep whatever drift they already had.

THE WRITE PATH IS THE ISSUE PATH AND NOTHING ELSE EVER UPDATES THE COLUMN. Whatever creates an outbound line today (see supabase/migrations/0004_outbound_functions.sql and 0018_outbound_issue_project_write.sql before writing anything new) reads the catalogue once, at insert time, and writes it. No trigger recomputes it, no later card refreshes it, and no screen offers to.

ONE FORMULA STILL. `public.project_material_cost()` and `lib/reporting/material-cost.ts` switch to the new column. The card does not add a second cost path, does not leave the old one behind a flag, and does not compute a "current price" total anywhere. P3-11 shipped one formula in one module and that property is the thing this card must not break.

THE FOOTNOTE COMES OFF. P3-11 put a Romanian footnote on the Cost tab saying values are calculated at the current catalogue price. Once this ships that sentence is false, and a stale caveat is worse than none: it teaches the reader to distrust a number that is now right. Removing it is named in the acceptance for that reason.

NO DROP, NO DELETE, NO TRUNCATE ANYWHERE IN THE FILE. products.unit_value_mdl stays exactly as it is: it is the current catalogue price and it is still correct for what it is for. Nothing about this card removes a column.

MIGRATION NUMBER IS THE NEXT FREE ONE at the moment this card is worked, four digits, never a renumber of an existing file. The acceptance names the file by its SUFFIX for that reason.

THE PENDING REGISTER LINE IS PART OF THE CARD. Add `<NNNN>_outbound_unit_value_at_issue.sql, card de aplicare <the open apply card>` to the Pending section of docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md in the same pull request. That is P3-27 while it is open. tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts fails the suite if a migration file is in neither place or in both.

WHO APPLIES IT IS READ OFF CLAUDE.md SECTION 8 AT THE MOMENT THE CARD IS WORKED, never assumed from this text. If a terminal still holds the apply, apply it as a normal three-phase apply under 8.5 and journal all three phases. Keyed by name alone the batch appears to both drop and keep the function and the declaration contradicts itself. The last verb on each name(args) wins, walked in register and file order, the same way funcState already does it for names.

cards.title: Drop _meta.characters_extracted from the extraction contract and put a model-reported page count in its place.
cards.plain: Replace a field the extraction service can never fill in with one that catches a real and otherwise invisible failure: the reading service quietly processing only the first page of a multi-page document.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0, with a case posting a callback carrying _meta.page_count and NO characters_extracted, accepted with the contract's success code and the value readable afterwards. THAT CASE MUST FAIL BEFORE THE CHANGE AND THE PR MUST SHOW BOTH RESULTS. PLUS a case asserting a callback that still carries characters_extracted is not rejected for carrying it. PLUS: docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md updated in the same PR, with the field removed from the shape and page_count documented in its place. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE FIELD IS REMOVED FROM WHAT WE EXPECT, NOT FROM WHAT WE TOLERATE. A callback that still carries characters_extracted is accepted and the field ignored: Andre's side and ours do not deploy in the same second, and a contract change that makes the previous version's payload invalid is an outage scheduled for whenever he ships first.

PAGE COUNT IS NULLABLE AND ITS ABSENCE IS NOT AN ERROR. It is a safety signal, not a required field, and a missing signal must not reject a document that was read correctly.

WHETHER A MISMATCH BLOCKS OR FLAGS IS NOT THIS CARD. This card carries the field. Comparing it against the true page count of the stored PDF, and deciding what happens when they differ, is separate work and needs a page counter on our side that does not exist yet.

cards.title: A health route reports the live commit and the applied ledger version, and the applier requires it to match, so INC-06 closes mechanically instead of by rule.
cards.plain: The system gains a page that states exactly which version of the code is live. The tool that changes the database then refuses to remove anything until it can see that the live site has already stopped using it, instead of relying on somebody remembering to check.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `curl -s <production origin>/api/health` returns 200 application/json carrying the live commit sha and the applied ledger version, and the sha matches the head of main at the time of the request. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run check:removal-safety` exits 0 and, on a removal batch, REFUSES when the deployed commit does not contain the code that stopped reading the removed object. THAT REFUSAL MUST BE PROVEN ON A FIXTURE, exit non-zero, in the PR. PLUS: scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs no longer accepts RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED as the sole proof of deployment for a removal batch against production. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
NO VERCEL API AND NO VERCEL_TOKEN, ON THE OWNER'S INSTRUCTION. VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA is exposed to the application at build time by the platform itself, so the deployed build can state its own commit with no credential at all. This SURVIVES P2-13's credential revocation, which is the point: a check that dies when the credentials rotate is a check that dies on the day it matters.

THE ROUTE IS PUBLIC AND CARRIES NOTHING ELSE. A commit sha and a migration version number. No environment names, no counts, no health of any dependency. Anything more is a card of its own, because a health route is the one endpoint everybody adds one more field to.

RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED IS REPLACED, NOT KEPT AS A FALLBACK. An operator statement that survives beside a machine check is the one that gets used at three in the morning. If the health route cannot be reached, the applier REFUSES; it does not fall back to asking.

THE LEDGER VERSION IS READ FROM THE DATABASE THE APP IS CONNECTED TO, never from the repository. The repository says what SHOULD be applied; only the database says what IS.

evidence.ref: #PENDING, app/api/health/route.ts + scripts/poc-free/check-deployed-commit.mjs. RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED is GONE and is proved dead: prove:schema-direction asserts that setting it no longer buys past the refusal. Acceptance: npm run prove:deployed-commit passes 12 cases, eleven refusals each paired with a control, including the INC-06 case where production is BEHIND the commit being applied. npm run prove:schema-direction 7 of 7, npm run prove:applier 14 of 14, npm run check:migrations 28 applied to a bare postgres:16 with 12 assertion files. Migration 0028_applied_ledger_version.sql AUTHORED AND MERGED, NOT APPLIED, registered under this card.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-02 FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH, answering the question scripts/poc/ask.sh put to him as Telegram 33: assert DEPLOYED rather than merged, and do it without VERCEL_TOKEN.

WHAT IT REPLACES, VERBATIM FROM THE CODE. scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs today: 'REFUSED. This batch removes schema and the DEPLOY cannot be verified from here.' followed by an invitation to re-run with RC_DEPLOY_CONFIRMED=yes, recorded as an operator statement. The comment above it says the deployed half 'is not faked' and names this as an open question, which it now is not.

INC-06 IS THE INCIDENT THIS CLOSES. A removal was applied against a production database whose live code still read the removed object. check:removal-safety, shipped by P3-11c, proves the MERGED half: no reader remains on main. This card proves the DEPLOYED half, which is the half that actually broke.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING AND BLOCKS THE TWO REMOVAL CARDS ALREADY SHIPPED FROM EVER RECURRING. It is a guard, not a fix, and the thing it guards has already happened once.

SHIPPED 2026-09-02 BY EXECUTOR.

THE QUESTION IT ASKS IS git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit being applied> <live commit>. If the live commit CONTAINS the tree being applied, every line in that tree is already deployed, including the line that stopped reading the removed object. That is stronger than 'my deploy finished': it is false when production runs something older AND when production runs something unrelated.

EVERY FAILURE IS A REFUSAL. Unreachable, redirected, HTML, 5xx, unparseable, no commit, blank commit, a commit git has never heard of, a commit that is not a descendant. There is no path on which not knowing is treated as yes, because 'I could not tell, so I assumed it was fine' is INC-06 in one sentence.

THE PROXY EXEMPTION IS PART OF THE MECHANISM. Without /api/health in isPublic() the applier reads an HTML login page instead of a commit and refuses forever, for the wrong reason. One of the eleven proved refusals is exactly that case and names proxy.ts in its own output.

THE LEDGER VERSION WALKED INTO INC-05'S GUARD, CORRECTLY. check:pending-schema-reads refused the health route for naming applied_ledger_version() while 0028 is pending. Its usual remedy does not apply: hasPhase3Schema answers a different question, and a gate for 0028 would itself be a function in an unapplied migration, which is the trap schema-capability.ts's own header names. It is an EXEMPT entry with its reason written down, which is what that list is for: the rpc call is inside a try, any error becomes null, and null reads as 'I do not know', never as 'none'. A health route that crashes is worse than useless. The applier does not depend on that field at all: it decides on commit, which touches no database.

THE MIGRATION IS PORTABLE AND THAT WAS NOT FREE. A language sql body is resolved at CREATE time, so the first draft could not apply to the bare postgres:16 shim that check:migrations runs every migration against. It is plpgsql with a to_regclass guard now. A migration that can only be parsed against production is a migration whose first real test is production.

THE MISTAKE MADE BUILDING THE PROOF. The first version drove the check with spawnSync while the fake health route ran in the SAME process. spawnSync blocks the event loop, so the server could never accept the connection: every case timed out and every refusal passed for the wrong reason, controls included, which is how it was caught. It is async now, the accepting control is re-run LAST after every refusal, and the same lesson is why scripts/poc-free/fake-health-server.mjs is a separate process.

0028 IS AUTHORED AND MERGED, NOT APPLIED. Merging a migration file changes one text file and changes nothing in any database. The apply is a separate act with its own three phases and its own journal.

cards.title: Every assertion in the four production guards is proved able to fail, and one arriving without a failing case fails the build.
cards.plain: Check that every safety check protecting the live database can actually detect the problem it claims to detect. Three of them could not, and had been reporting success for weeks.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npm run prove:assertions` exits 0, running EVERY assertion the applier ships against a correct database, where it must hold, and against a database perturbed to violate it, where it must raise. The bodies are read from the applier itself so what is proved is the shipped text. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run prove:schema-direction` exits 0 with a case for every refusal path in check-removal-safety and check-pending-schema-reads, each paired with a control. PLUS COMMAND: `npm run check:assertion-register` exits 0 and is PROVEN to fail on a fixture: an assertion added to the source with no row in docs/ASSERTION-REGISTER.md, shown in the PR with its non-zero exit. PLUS: any assertion found to be incapable of failing is deleted or fixed, and the PR names which and why.
cards.defaults:
AN ASSERTION WITH NO FAILING CASE IS DELETED OR FIXED, NEVER LEFT. That is the owner's instruction and it is the card.

BOTH HALVES ARE REQUIRED FOR EVERY ASSERTION: a control that holds on a correct database and a perturbation that raises. A body that raises on everything passes the perturbation and fails the control; a body that raises on nothing passes the control and fails the perturbation. Only one that does both is doing its job.

THE BODIES ARE READ FROM THE SHIPPED SOURCE, never copied into the proof. A copy drifts and the proof goes on passing about the copy, which is the same reason test-ask-digest.sh lifts responder.sh's offset program out from between fences.

ONE CONTAINER, NOT ONE PER ASSERTION. Eleven containers would put minutes into every run of a proof that fits in one, and a proof nobody can afford to run is a proof that gets filtered out.

A PERTURBATION IS WRITTEN BY HAND, never generated from the assertion. A generated one would be a second implementation of the same rule and would agree with it by construction.

evidence.ref: #PENDING. npm run prove:assertions: 11 assertions read from the applier through RC_APPLY_PRINT_ASSERTIONS, each holds on a correct database and RAISES when perturbed, plus 2 notices asserted to carry no raise exception. npm run prove:schema-direction 12 of 12, four cases new: a TABLE drop with a reader, a FUNCTION drop reached through rpc(), a check pointed at a source directory that does not exist refusing rather than reporting clean, and a stale exemption naming a deleted file. npm run check:assertion-register OK over 18 assertions and refusals across 3 files, and proved to REFUSE an unregistered assertion on a fixture.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED AND WORKED 2026-09-02 BY EXECUTOR, on the owner's dispatch, ranked ahead of wave 3 by him: 'Never-failing assertions in the guard that protects production is the worst place this class can live.'

THREE DEFECTS FOUND, ALL OF ONE CLASS.

1. Three assertions in prove-applier.mjs read a psql boolean with includes('t') against a column named untouched. They matched the COLUMN NAME. Found under APPLY-01 and fixed there; recorded here as the reason this card exists.

2. outbound-destination-backfill and supplier-backfill sat in the applier's assertion list with raise notice as their only statement. NO raise exception on any path, so they COULD NOT FAIL, and they were counted in 'N assertions passed' and in the row this script writes to docs/PRODUCTION-WRITES.md. The record said thirteen guards held when eleven did and two printed a number. They are kept and are useful; they are now declared through N() instead of A(), reported separately, and prove:assertions asserts that they remain incapable of raising so nobody moves them back by accident.

3. Four refusal paths across the two checks had never been watched fail: a TABLE drop, a FUNCTION drop, a check pointed at a missing source directory, and a stale exemption. The third is the worst shape a check can have, pointed at nothing, finding nothing, reporting clean, and it now exits 2 with a case that proves it.

THE REGISTER IS THE DURABLE HALF. The proofs answer 'do these cases pass'. They cannot answer 'is there a case for every assertion', because an assertion nobody wrote a case for is invisible to them: add one to the applier with no perturbation and the proof covers ten of eleven and still prints all-passed. docs/ASSERTION-REGISTER.md plus check:assertion-register is what notices, and it is NOT path-filtered, deliberately.

CLAUDE.md 3.1 WAS AMENDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY EXTENDED. That section says in terms that a second path-filtered step is a change to it and not an application of it. prove:assertions is that second step, so the section now carries the paragraph naming it, why it shares the existing filter rather than adding one, and that check:assertion-register must never be filtered.

client_ref IS UNCHANGED, in the owner's words. This card touches the SUPPLIER's identifier only.

It runs in the quality step that applies every migration to a bare postgres and then runs every assertions file. cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-02 FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH, relaying Andre, confirmed by the owner. His words: 'TG 0009312, not 0009312. The series is part of the identifier in Moldovan invoicing; two suppliers can both issue number 0009312.'

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. order_ref is what the system matches a document against. Two suppliers each issuing 0009312 collide on it, and a collision on a document identifier is either a duplicate that gets rejected or a document attributed to the wrong supplier. Neither is visible on the screen where it happens.

P3-31 SPLIT order_ref INTO THEIRS AND OURS. This card is about the shape of THEIRS and does not re-open that split.

IN FLIGHT 2026-09-07, run 20260907-010004, branch card/ext-11.

WHAT THE RUN ESTABLISHED, AND IT CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THE CARD. order_ref is
stored NOWHERE today. The acceptance line says "wherever order_ref is stored, on
orders and on extraction drafts", and the answer is: nowhere. extraction_drafts
has no such column, inbound_orders carries `reference` which is OUR reference,
and contract section 4.1a says order_ref arrives, is accepted and is IGNORED.
P3-31 assumes the column exists too, and P3-31 has not shipped. Neither card
creates it. So this card lands the SUPPLIER's identifier whole: order_ref and
order_ref_series, on extraction_drafts and on inbound_orders. client_ref stays
untouched, per this card's own defaults, and remains P3-31's.

WHY ONLY THE FAILING TESTS ARE ON THE BRANCH SO FAR. The acceptance demands the
new case FAILING BEFORE THE CHANGE AND THE PR SHOWING BOTH RESULTS. The quality
check runs about 22 minutes and the workflow cancels in-progress runs on the same
ref, so the before-run and the after-run cannot both survive inside one 45 minute
harness window. The tests are pushed alone so the check records the RED. The next
run pushes the implementation onto the same pull request and records the GREEN.

SHIPPED 2026-09-07, run 20260907-040001, on the same branch and the same pull
request the previous run opened. The plan recorded above was followed as written,
with two decisions taken under this board's wide defaults and logged here rather
than asked:

DECISION 1, THE GATE IS ONE PROBE FOR BOTH COLUMNS AND NOT TWO. Every other
capability gate in lib/data/schema-capability.ts asks its own question because
0032, 0033 and 0035 are separate FILES and reach production separately. These two
columns are added in ONE transaction in ONE file, so no state exists in which one
is present and the other is not, and a second probe would spend a second query a
minute learning the same fact. The probe asks for order_ref_series, which is the
column that could not have existed under another name.

DECISION 2, THE SUPPLIER REFERENCE REACHES inbound_orders THROUGH AN UPDATE AFTER
THE RPC, NOT THROUGH THE RPC. confirm_extraction_draft is a SQL function with a

cards.title: The extraction latency target is raised to 120 seconds above 20 lines and 60 below, wherever the timeout and any monitoring live.
cards.plain: Give the reading service longer to finish a big document before the system calls it late. Almost all of that time is the AI model itself, which neither side can speed up.
cards.acceptance: REWRITTEN 2026-09-07 ON OWNER RATIFICATION. The ship is ratified and the RECORD was not: this card shipped on an acceptance whose first clause could not be met as written. That clause is quoted at the foot of this field and marked impossible, under CLAUDE.md 9c, rather than deleted. What follows is what was actually run and passed. COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS: the three owner numbers are named ONCE, in lib/data/extraction-budget.mjs, as EXTRACTION_LINE_THRESHOLD 20, EXTRACTION_BUDGET_ABOVE_MS 120000 and EXTRACTION_BUDGET_BELOW_MS 60000, and are read everywhere they are used through extractionBudgetMs(). The module is .mjs with a .d.mts beside it, following EXT-08's precedent, because the runner is node 20 and cannot import a .ts file. PLUS: the acknowledgement clock in lib/data/extraction-fire.ts reads ACK_TIMEOUT_MS from that same module instead of carrying its own literal, and STAYS at 15 seconds, because it measures whether Make accepted the job and not how long the model took. PLUS NAMED CASE, COMMAND: `npm run prove:extraction-budget` exits 0, 13 of 13, wired into quality by name and NOT path filtered. It asserts the three numbers; that 21 and 200 lines take the long budget and 19, 1 and 0 the short one; THE BOUNDARY, that exactly 20 takes the SHORT budget because the rule is ABOVE 20; that an unknown count and a NaN both take the LONG budget, which is the case that actually runs in production; and that the acknowledgement clock is still 15 seconds and still a different number from either budget. PLUS: docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md section 4.4a carries both budget numbers, the reason, the statement that the line count is not knowable at fire time, and the table of all three clocks on this path. PLUS: every other place naming a timeout on this path is found and listed by file and line in this card's evidence. There are three, they answer three different questions, and only one of them moved: ACK_TIMEOUT_MS into the budget module; app/api/documents/[...path]/route.ts:42 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS 20s left where it is with the reason written down; lib/reminders/resend.ts:33 TIMEOUT_MS 10s named as the email path and not this one. PLUS COMMAND: `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` over all three boards exits 0. THE CLAUSE THIS FIELD REPLACED, QUOTED AND MARKED IMPOSSIBLE, KEPT UNDER CLAUDE.md 9c: "PLUS: the timeout in lib/data/extraction-fire.ts is derived from the line count threshold rather than a single constant, with the two values named once and read everywhere they are used, asserted by a named unit case that a document above the threshold gets the longer budget and one below gets the shorter." IMPOSSIBLE IN BOTH HALVES, AND THE CARD ITSELF HAD ALREADY SAID SO. There is no line count at fire time: docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md section 3 fixes the request payload at exactly six fields, order_id, document_url, document_filename, mime_type, size_bytes and callback_url, and the line count is the RESULT of the extraction rather than an input to it. And the timeout in extraction-fire.ts is the ACKNOWLEDGEMENT clock, not the extraction budget, so deriving it from a line count would hold an operator's screen for two minutes and would measure nothing about the model. The card's own defaults pre-decided the first half in terms, and its notes named the second as the first thing the card had to establish, so it shipped under CLAUDE.md 5 as a default applied and logged rather than under section 4 as a block. THIS REWRITE CHANGES NO CODE AND NO SHIP. It changes what this field CLAIMS was proved, so the claim matches the evidence beneath it.
cards.defaults:
120 SECONDS ABOVE 20 LINES, 60 BELOW. The owner's numbers, not a range to be tuned here.

PER-PAGE SPLITTING WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, by the owner, on the record: it adds cost and a reassembly failure mode. This card does not re-open it.

THE THRESHOLD IS ON LINES AND WE DO NOT KNOW THE LINE COUNT BEFORE THE EXTRACTION. That is the one thing this card must resolve rather than assume. If the count is not knowable at fire time, the longer budget applies to every document and the PR says so plainly instead of inventing a proxy for it.

ONE SOURCE FOR BOTH NUMBERS. A timeout that exists in two files is a timeout that will disagree with itself.

evidence.ref: Branch card/ext-12, cut from main at cf69032. THE FIRST THING THIS CARD ESTABLISHES, WHICH ITS OWN NOTES NAMED AS SUCH: the 15 second TIMEOUT_MS in lib/data/extraction-fire.ts is NOT the extraction budget. It is the ACKNOWLEDGEMENT clock. The POST carries callback_url in its body and the function returns as soon as Make answers 2xx, so what it waits for is Make ACCEPTING the job; the result arrives later by callback. The operator's screen waits on this clock, so raising it to 120 seconds would hold that screen for two minutes and would measure nothing about the model, which is what the card's note forbids in terms. It stays at 15 seconds and now reads that value from the same file as the budget so the two cannot be confused a second time. AND THE LINE COUNT IS NOT KNOWABLE AT FIRE TIME. Section 3 of the contract fixes the payload at exactly six fields, order_id, document_url, document_filename, mime_type, size_bytes and callback_url, and none of them is a line count: the count is the RESULT of the extraction. The card pre-decided this case in its defaults, so the LONGER budget applies to every document and this pull request says so plainly. size_bytes was deliberately NOT used as a proxy: a one-page scan can be heavier than a three-page digital document, and a proxy invented here would become the threshold within six months without anybody having decided it. ONE SOURCE FOR BOTH NUMBERS: lib/data/extraction-budget.ts exports EXTRACTION_LINE_THRESHOLD 20, EXTRACTION_BUDGET_ABOVE_MS 120000, EXTRACTION_BUDGET_BELOW_MS 60000, extractionBudgetMs() and ACK_TIMEOUT_MS. extraction-fire.ts imports the last one rather than carrying its own literal. THE NAMED UNIT CASE: npm run prove:extraction-budget, 13 of 13, run in quality and NOT path filtered. It asserts the three owner numbers; that 21 and 200 lines get the long budget; that 19, 1 and 0 get the short one; THE BOUNDARY, that exactly 20 gets the SHORT budget because the rule is ABOVE 20 and not 20-or-more; that an unknown count and a NaN both get the LONG budget, which is the case that actually runs in production; and that the acknowledgement clock is still 15 seconds and still a DIFFERENT number from either budget, so a future edit that conflated them turns the check red. NO TEST FRAMEWORK WAS ADDED. This repository has no vitest, jest or node:test harness, and every unit-shaped assertion in it is a scripts/poc-free/prove-*.mjs wired into quality by name. That is what a named unit case means here, and adding a second framework for thirteen assertions is a dependency CLAUDE.md forbids taking without asking. THE SURVEY THE ACCEPTANCE ASKS FOR, BY FILE AND LINE. There are exactly three clocks on this path and they answer three different questions. lib/data/extraction-budget.ts:80 ACK_TIMEOUT_MS 15s, whether Make accepted the job, read by lib/data/extraction-fire.ts:39. lib/data/extraction-budget.ts extractionBudgetMs(), 120s and 60s, how long the model may take, which is Make's own limit and which our code declares rather than enforces. app/api/documents/[...path]/route.ts:42 UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS 20s, how long WE wait on storage when Make fetches the file; it does NOT move to the budget module because it is not an extraction budget, and moving it would put a third question under a name that answers a different one. lib/reminders/resend.ts:33 TIMEOUT_MS 10s was found by the same sweep and is the email path, not this one. THE CONTRACT CARRIES BOTH NUMBERS AND THE REASON: docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md section 4.4a, with the owner's quote relayed from Andre, the statement that the count is not knowable at fire time so the long budget applies to every document, the refusal to use size_bytes as a proxy, and the table of all three clocks. It sits beside section 5.2's timeout code, which already read the extraction exceeded Make's OWN limit and which is now explained rather than merely stated. COMMANDS: npm run prove:extraction-budget 13 of 13; npx tsc --noEmit exits 0; npm run check:action-pins, check:live-fixtures, check:conflict-residue, check:card-ids, check:unique-ids and check:grant-revocation all exit 0; node docs/board/validate-board.mjs over all three boards exits 0. IT IS REMOVED FROM WHAT WE READ AND SHOW, NOT FROM WHAT WE TOLERATE. A callback that still carries confidence is accepted and the field ignored. Andre's side and ours do not deploy in the same second, and a contract change that makes the previous version's payload invalid is an outage scheduled for whenever he ships first.

THE COLUMNS STAY IN THE DATABASE FOR NOW AND THIS CARD DOES NOT DROP THEM. extraction_drafts.confidence and extraction_draft_lines.confidence are nullable with a range constraint. Dropping a column is a REMOVAL migration, which under P3-11c and P3-11e requires proving that nothing reads it and that the deploy which stopped reading it is live. That is its own card with its own apply, and folding it in here would put a removal migration inside a screen change.

A CONSTANT IS WORSE THAN AN ABSENCE ON A REVIEW SCREEN, and the scan result is the proof rather than the argument. The reviewer reads 1.0 as 'the machine is sure'. On a document where four of seven lines were wrong it was actively misleading, which is a stronger claim than decorative and is the owner's word for it.

So that case would have been TRUE BEFORE THE CHANGE, which is exactly the class PROVE-01 named the same week: an assertion whose passing path is reachable without the condition being true. It is not written, and the acceptance rests instead on two cases that CAN fail: a payload that sends confidence is accepted and the field is not stored, and a payload that omits it is accepted identically.

cards.title: A scan-sourced payload that fails reconciliation is rejected as failed with NO line items, and the screen says the contents were not read.
cards.plain: When the reading service cannot read a scanned document, the system must show the document's header, say plainly that its contents were not read, and offer no way to book it. Half-read lines look like real ones and there is no way for a person to tell.
cards.acceptance: FIRST, AND EVERYTHING ELSE DEPENDS ON IT: the payload carries the SOURCE of the extraction, declared by the extractor, because nothing in the contract says today whether a document was read as text or looked at as an image. Contract updated, validator accepts it, a callback omitting it is still accepted and treated as the safe value. PLUS MIGRATION: a new numbered file stores the source on extraction_drafts, nullable. `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 with an assertions file. PLUS COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 with THREE new cases: a scan-sourced payload that fails reconciliation is stored as failed with ZERO lines and its header fields intact; the SAME payload marked digital-sourced is stored as partial WITH its lines, unchanged from today; a scan-sourced payload that reconciles is unaffected by this card. Each must fail before the change and the PR must show both results. PLUS COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0 with a case asserting that on such a draft the screen states in Romanian that the contents were not read, shows the header fields, renders NO line inputs, and offers NO confirm control. PLUS: a grep-proof in the PR that no route from that screen reaches the booking action, and if one is found the card returns NOTHING instead of the header, per the owner's instruction. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE DISTINCTION IS THE SOURCE, NOT THE FAILURE, in the owner's words. A digital document that fails reconciliation stays partial with its lines attached, exactly as today. Only a SCAN-sourced failure loses its lines.

OUR SIDE CANNOT TELL A SCAN FROM A DIGITAL DOCUMENT TODAY, AND THAT IS THIS CARD'S FIRST PROBLEM. The contract has no source field. mime_type does not answer it: one of the four sample documents is a PDF with no text layer, so application/pdf covers both cases. _meta.characters_extracted was the only proxy and EXT-09 removes it because it could only ever be null. Only the extractor knows whether it read text or looked at an image, so the extractor declares it.

THE SAFE VALUE WHEN THE SOURCE IS ABSENT IS 'SCAN'. An unknown source gets the strict treatment, because the failure mode of guessing 'digital' is invented stock and the failure mode of guessing 'scan' is a document somebody has to key in by hand.

HEADER FIELDS ARE RETURNED AND THEY ARE THE POINT OF THE SCREEN: supplier, order_ref, client_ref, date, currency, VAT rate, printed totals. They read correctly on the observed scan and they let the owner identify the document and key the lines against a known total.

HARD REQUIREMENT, THE OWNER'S WORD: no accept path, no pre-populated line fields, and the screen must say the contents were not read. IF ANY ROUTE EXISTS FROM THAT SCREEN TO BOOKING THE DOCUMENT, RETURN NOTHING INSTEAD OF THE HEADER. That is not a preference to be balanced against usefulness.

NO LINE IS STORED, NOT EVEN HIDDEN. A row in extraction_draft_lines that no screen renders is a row the next screen will render.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-03 FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH, on Andre's scan result: four wrong lines in seven, every one arithmetically self-consistent, with status extracted and confidence 1.0.

WHY LINES ARE DROPPED RATHER THAN FLAGGED. A flagged line is still a line: it carries a product name, a quantity and a price, and it sits in a form field somebody can accept. The observed failure produced lines that were internally consistent and wrong, so there is nothing on the line itself for a reviewer to notice. The only safe rendering of a line that might be invented is no line.

THE SOURCE FIELD IS THE PREREQUISITE AND IT IS INSIDE THIS CARD RATHER THAN A SEPARATE ONE, because a card that cannot tell which rule to apply has no acceptance line that can pass. EXT-16 and EXT-17 both depend on it and both depend on this card.

SHIPPED 2026-09-03 BY EXECUTOR.

A FAILED DRAFT HAD NO ROUTE TO ITS OWN HEADER, AND THAT WAS FOUND BY THE TEST RATHER THAN BY READING. The upload screen showed a failed document its error code and a Retrimite button and nothing else: the supplier, the document number, the date and the printed totals, which READ CORRECTLY on the observed scan, were not visible anywhere. The card asked for a screen that shows them, so the card had to add the way in. The control is called 'Vezi antetul' and NOT 'Verifica', because a button named like the other one promises an accept path that does not exist and must not.

THE PREDICATE IS DEFINED ONCE AND USED BY BOTH THE LIST AND THE PANEL. Two copies of 'is this an unread scan' could disagree, and the disagreement that matters is the one where the list offers a button to a panel that renders the form.

THE REFUSAL IS ALSO IN THE SERVER ACTION, NOT ONLY ON THE SCREEN. confirmExtractionDraft reads the status and source BACK FROM THE DATABASE and refuses. A server action is an execution path of its own: anyone can call it, and a guard proven on one execution path is not a guard. Same doctrine EXT-16 carries about reconciliation, applied to an edge instead of a number.

A TEXT COLUMN WITH A CHECK, NOT AN ENUM, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. P3-33 added two labels to unit_code the day before and the migration had to be SPLIT IN TWO, because a new enum label cannot be used in the transaction that added it and supabase db reset wraps each file in one. A third source value here would cost the same split; widening a check constraint costs one migration with no transaction hazard on any of the three runners.

NO COLUMN DEFAULT, DELIBERATELY, AND THE ASSERTION FILE CHECKS FOR ITS ABSENCE. A default of 'scan' would have rewritten every draft stored before this migration into a claim nobody made. Rows that predate it are genuinely unknown and stay null; only the APPLICATION reads null as scan, and only for new payloads.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND WHILE SHIPPING IT, ALL RECORDED IN docs/LEARNINGS.md.

1. check-pending-schema-reads MATCHED THE WORD `if` AS A COLUMN NAME. Its added-column pattern did not accept `add column IF NOT EXISTS`, which 0032 uses, so it captured `if`, searched every source file for it, found it almost everywhere, and reported the whole application as reading unapplied schema. The pattern now accepts the clause, and a captured object name that is a SQL keyword STOPS THE RUN rather than being searched for. That is the mirror of the class PROVE-01 named: a check whose FAILING path is reachable without the condition being true, which is worse, because a false green is ignored once and a false red is ignored forever.

2. THE CAPABILITY PROBE ASKED ON THE WRONG CONNECTION. hasExtractionDocumentSource built its own SESSION client. The callback is a machine endpoint with no session and the RLS policies are `to authenticated`, so the probe got a permission refusal, read it as 'column absent', and the gate answered NO FOREVER on the one path that mattered. It takes the caller's client now: a capability probe is only meaningful on the connection whose capability is in question, and anon, authenticated and service_role see different schemas through PostgREST.

3. THE GUARD RECOGNISED ONE CAPABILITY GATE BY LITERAL NAME. check-pending-schema-reads exempted a file containing the string hasPhase3Schema, which was the same thing as 'is this read gated' only while one gate existed. It derives the list from lib/data/schema-capability.ts now, and REFUSES TO RUN if that yields zero names, because zero gates would report every guarded file as unguarded.

THE GATE IS WHY THIS CARD IS NOT INC-05 AGAIN. 0032 is merged and unapplied, so this code reaches production before the column. Until it exists the behaviour is TODAY'S, not the new one: not knowing the source does not mean `scan`, it means the EXT-15 rule does not apply yet and the lines are kept. The `scan` default in effectiveSource is about a payload that did not DECLARE a source on a database that CAN store one, which is a different question.

NOTE 2026-09-15, CARD EXT-33: the sample set under `_samples/andre` holds six documents since 2026-09-15, and R-096 as amended that day covers every document under that prefix, not a fixed count of four. Where this card says four, the four are the original set; nothing above is changed.

cards.title: Reconciliation is enforced by our validator, not only inside Andre's scenario, because a control on one execution path is not a control.
cards.plain: Check on our side that a scanned document's line values add up to the total printed on it. The same check already exists in the reading service, but a control that lives only there is skipped by any other way a document might arrive.
cards.acceptance:
UNBLOCKED 2026-09-03: Andre's tolerance is given in the defaults and is implemented as stated.

COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 with cases, each failing before the change and both results shown in the PR: a scan-sourced payload INSIDE the tolerance is accepted; one OUTSIDE it is rejected as failed with no lines, per EXT-15; a DIGITAL-sourced payload outside the tolerance is unaffected by this card; and the three cannot-run conditions, each with its own case: target null REJECTS, any null line_total REJECTS, and prices_include_vat null reconciles against BOTH targets and is accepted only when one matches. PLUS COMMAND: a named check exits 0 over the tolerance arithmetic itself, including Andre's two fixture values: a 7-line document tolerates 0.07 and a 54-line document tolerates 0.54, plus a 3-line document tolerating 0.05 because the floor wins. PLUS: the tolerance is ONE named expression read from one place, and docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md records the formula, the rounding, the target selection, the three cannot-run rules, and Andre as its source. PLUS: the check runs on the callback route, proven by a case posting directly to the route rather than through a helper. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE TOLERANCE IS ANDRE'S, VERBATIM, IMPLEMENTED AS GIVEN AND NEVER RE-DERIVED:

  pass when abs(sum_of_line_totals - target) <= max(0.05, 0.01 * line_count)
  both sides rounded to two decimals BEFORE comparing
  target selected by prices_include_vat: false -> subtotal, true -> document_total

TWO CHECKS DISAGREEING ON THE INTERESTING CASES IS WORSE THAN ONE CHECK. That is the owner's reason for forbidding a second number, and it is why the formula is copied rather than reasoned about.

THE THREE CONDITIONS WHERE THE CHECK CANNOT RUN. NONE OF THEM IS A FREE PASS:

  1. target is null, because the document does not print it  -> REJECT
  2. prices_include_vat is null -> reconcile against BOTH subtotal and document_total,
     and accept only if ONE of them matches
  3. any line has a null line_total -> REJECT, the sum is incomplete by construction

READING NOTE, STATED BECAUSE THE DISPATCH CAN BE READ TWO WAYS. It heads these three with 'All three FAIL, none passes' and then gives rule 2 its own resolution. The reading implemented here is that NONE OF THE THREE IS AN AUTOMATIC PASS and that rule 2 carries the procedure deciding it. The alternative reading, that rule 2 also fails unconditionally, would make its own instruction unreachable text. If that reading is wrong the correction is one branch and one case.

ROUNDING HAPPENS BEFORE THE COMPARISON, ON BOTH SIDES, and that is not a detail: rounding after subtracting gives a different answer at the boundary, and the boundary is the only place a tolerance is ever consulted.

WHICH TOTAL RECONCILES IS ALREADY THE CONTRACT'S ANSWER. prices_include_vat decides it. This card uses that field and does not re-open it.

SAME DOCTRINE THE REPOSITORY ALREADY HOLDS: a guard proven on one execution path is not a guard. That is why this card exists rather than being satisfied by Andre's scenario.

evidence.ref: PR #195, merged as 53df12c. THE BOARD FLIP WAS OMITTED FROM THAT PULL REQUEST AND IS MADE HERE; the omission is recorded rather than hidden. ACCEPTANCE, run in quality on head a154a27: npx playwright test, 145 passed and 0 failed. Cases 12 to 15 are this card's. 12: Andre's THREE OBSERVED SUMS (49035.40, 39242.00, 38429.40) against a printed 50336.40 excl VAT on a 7-line document all FAIL, and the refusal has EXT-15's shape: status failed, error_code reconciliation_failed, ZERO stored lines, header fields kept. 13: a scan INSIDE the tolerance is accepted WITH its lines. Without it, an implementation refusing everything passes case 12 entirely. 14: a DIGITAL payload with the same wrong arithmetic is UNTOUCHED. 15: the three cannot-run conditions, each its own case, and prices_include_vat null gets TWO sub-cases, one where a target matches and one where neither does. npm run check:reconciliation exit 0, with three mutants each turning it red: tolerance 0.10 per line; <= becomes <; target_missing becomes a pass. It asserts Andre's three fixture values (7 lines 0.07, 54 lines 0.54, 3 lines 0.05 where the floor wins) and that NO SECOND FILE computes a tolerance. MIGRATION 0034_error_code_reconciliation_failed.sql, in its own file because a new enum label cannot be used in the transaction that adds it. APPLIED ON MERGE by the Supabase integration, which is R-124's behaviour and was predicted in the migration's own header: applied_ledger_version() went 0033 to 0034 and the label went absent to present within about two minutes. Journalled in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md with a READ-ONLY probe per R-122. check:no-destructive-migration passed on this pull request: one AlterEnumStmt, one SelectStmt, no row removed. A CAPABILITY GATE NOTHING WOULD HAVE REQUIRED: hasReconciliationFailedCode. check-pending-schema-reads is blind to alter type ... add value, so no check would have refused writing the label before the migration applied. Carded as MIG-02. Report: docs/reports/2026-09-04-executor-dispatch-drain-and-doctrine.md.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-03 FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH. His words: 'a control living only in Make is bypassed by a scenario rebuild, a second ingest path, or a manual upload, and it is now the only thing between a scan and invented stock.'

BLOCKED ON ANDRE FOR ONE NUMBER AND NOTHING ELSE. Everything else in the card is buildable, and per CLAUDE.md section 4 the question carries a recommendation and a stated interim. It blocks THIS CARD and not the run: EXT-15 and EXT-17 are both claimable and neither needs the tolerance.

THE INGREDIENTS ARE ALREADY IN THE CONTRACT: subtotal, vat_amount, document_total, prices_include_vat and vat_rate are all document-level fields today. What is missing is the tolerance and the source, and the source is EXT-15's.

UNBLOCKED 2026-09-03 BY THE OWNER, WITH ANDRE'S TOLERANCE VERBATIM. The question this card carried is answered and removed.

THE TWO FIXTURE VALUES DISCLOSE TWO LINE COUNTS, AND THAT IS SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN SLID PAST. An earlier dispatch forbade committing expected line counts or totals for the four sample documents, so that Andre's extractor produces them unaided. These two numbers are tolerances, 0.07 and 0.54, and they imply line counts of 7 and 54. They are used because the owner supplied them for exactly this purpose, and because the earlier rule is about what is SENT TO ANDRE: a fixture in our own suite is not sent to him and does not help his extractor. Nothing derived from them goes into anything he receives.

cards.title: A scan-sourced document never auto-accepts, reconciled or not, and its lines are marked as machine-read from an image.
cards.plain: A document that was photographed or scanned always goes to a person before it changes stock, even when its numbers add up. Numbers that add up are not proof they were read correctly.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 with a case proving that a scan-sourced payload which RECONCILES still lands in review and is not booked, and a case proving the digital path is unchanged. Each must fail before the change and the PR must show both results. PLUS COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0 with a case asserting the lines of such a draft are visibly marked, in Romanian, as machine-read from an image, on the line and not only in a page-level banner. PLUS: a grep-proof in the PR enumerating every path from a draft to a booked inbound order and showing that each one requires the operator's confirm, with the scan case named. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
RECONCILED IS NOT READ CORRECTLY, AND THIS IS THE CARD'S WHOLE RATIONALE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WILL BE ARGUED WITH. Reconciliation caught the observed failure ONLY because the model read the totals correctly and the lines wrong. A set of manufactured lines that happened to sum to the printed total would pass it. Unlikely, not impossible, and the cost is invented stock.

THE MARK IS ON THE LINE, NOT ONLY ON THE PAGE. A banner at the top of a screen is read once and then scrolled past; the line is what somebody is looking at when they decide.

IT IS ROMANIAN AND IT SAYS WHAT HAPPENED, not a severity word. 'Citit de masina dintr-o imagine' tells the reviewer what to do differently. 'Atentie' does not.

NO AUTO-ACCEPT EXISTS FOR ANY SOURCE TODAY, AS FAR AS THE REPOSITORY SHOWS, AND THIS CARD MUST PROVE THAT RATHER THAN ASSUME IT. If the grep finds a path that books without a confirm, that path is the card and the marking is the smaller half.

evidence.ref: Branch card/ext-17, cut from main at b365c3f. THE CHANGE IS TWO FILES: lib/data/extraction-types.ts adds SCAN_LINE_NOTICE and scanReadLines() as ONE named definition each, and components/orders/ExtractionReviewPanel.tsx renders the notice INSIDE each review-line container, keyed on the source and NOT on the reconciliation result. COMMANDS, on a local Supabase stack with the CI recipe (supabase start, db reset, the four seed scripts): `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0, 34 of 34, up from 30. THE FOUR NEW CASES: extraction 16, a scan-sourced payload summing EXACTLY to the printed 50336.40 is stored extracted with its 7 lines, carries confirmed_at null and confirmed_inbound_order_id null, leaves the inbound order count unchanged across the callback, and appears in the review list with its Verifica button; extraction 17, the same payload marked digital, identical outcome; review 12, each line of a reconciling scan carries data-scan-read=true and the Romanian notice INSIDE the line element, with the form and the confirm button still whole; review 13, the same lines marked digital carry data-scan-read=false, no per-line notice, and the notice string appears NOWHERE on the page. THE FAILING HALF: review 12 and 13 were run against the pre-change component and BOTH FAILED on `data-scan-read` resolving to null, output in the report. Extraction 16 and 17 PASSED before the change, which is the card's own default ('no auto-accept exists for any source today, and this card must PROVE that rather than assume it'), so they were driven against a MUTANT callback route that writes confirmed_at, and both FAILED on it, output in the report. THE GREP-PROOF of every path from a draft to a booked inbound order is in the report and in the pull request: public.confirm_extraction_draft has exactly ONE caller in application code, lib/data/extraction-actions.ts:345, inside confirmExtractionDraft, whose only caller is the review panel's confirm button; confirmed_at is written by nothing else and only READ elsewhere; the callback route names inbound_orders, confirmed_at and confirm_extraction nowhere at all; and the two other order-creating RPCs, create_inbound_order and receive_inbound_order, are the manual form and the operator's receive button and take no draft. NO AUTO-ACCEPT PATH WAS FOUND. `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-03 FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH, with the rationale recorded at his instruction.

IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON EXT-16. Reconciliation passing or failing changes nothing about this rule, which is exactly why the rule exists: it is the answer to 'what if the arithmetic check is satisfied by a wrong document'.

IT DEPENDS ON EXT-15 for the source field, because a rule about scan-sourced documents cannot be applied by a system that cannot tell which ones they are.

BUILT AND SHIPPED 2026-09-04 BY EXECUTOR.

THE MARK IS ON THE LINE AND THE PROOF IS TOO. review 12 asserts the notice is a DESCENDANT of the review-line element rather than merely present on the page, which is the exact distinction the card draws: a banner at the top would satisfy a text search and fail that assertion.

IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE RECONCILIATION RESULT, BY CONSTRUCTION. scanReadLines() reads the source and nothing else. The fixture in review 12 is a document that ADDS UP: subtotal 18450.00 against a single line of 18450.00, tolerance 0.05, difference 0. That is the case the card exists for.

WHAT THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE CASES GOT WRONG, RECORDED BECAUSE THE TEST IS WHAT CAUGHT IT. Cases 16 and 17 were first written on orderWithDocument, which attaches a document to an inbound order that ALREADY EXISTS. listReviewDrafts excludes exactly that shape, by design and with the reason in its own header, so the draft could never have appeared in the review list and 'not booked' could not have been measured: the order was already there. Both cases were rebuilt on the extraction band, where no order exists until somebody confirms one, which is what makes the count assertion mean anything.

NO SERVER-SIDE GUARD WAS ADDED, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. EXT-15 already refuses a FAILED scan inside confirmExtractionDraft. A reconciling scan is a document the operator IS allowed to accept; the card asks that the acceptance be his, informed, and never automatic. Adding a refusal there would have removed the operator's own path, which is the opposite of the card.

cards.title: Header self-consistency: subtotal plus VAT equals the total, and VAT equals subtotal times the rate, on the same tolerance.
cards.plain: Check that a document's own summary numbers agree with each other before trusting any of them. It does not prove the document was read correctly; it means a wrong reading has to be wrong consistently in more places to get through.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 with cases, each failing before the change and both results shown in the PR: a payload where subtotal + vat_amount is outside the tolerance of document_total is rejected; one where vat_amount is outside the tolerance of subtotal * vat_rate is rejected; one where both hold is unaffected. PLUS COMMAND: the named check from EXT-16 is extended and exits 0 over ALL FOUR sample documents' header figures, which held both checks, used as fixtures. PLUS: docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md records both checks, that they use the SAME tolerance formula as EXT-16, and what they do and do not prove. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
SAME TOLERANCE FORMULA AS EXT-16, read from the same one place. A second formula here would be the second number the owner forbade, one level up.

REUSE `/api/health`'s SHAPE. Same `force-dynamic`, same `no-store`, same one-object response. A second convention for a second public read is two things to remember.

THE VERSION STRING IS THE APPLIED LEDGER VERSION, `applied_ledger_version()`, which already exists and is already read by `/api/health`. It answers `is what I am looking at the same schema you are talking about`, which is the question a poller actually has.

DO NOT MAKE IT A WEBHOOK. He polls. A push needs a URL from him, a retry policy and a failure mode, and none of that is needed to answer a question whose answer changes once a month.

OUT OF SCOPE, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN LEFT AMBIGUOUS: the error-code set. R-123 already requires a new code to reach him BEFORE it can be emitted or received, in both directions, which is a stronger guarantee than polling. Adding codes here would give two answers to one question.
