cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 FROM THE OWNER'S DISPATCH. NOT BUILT.

THE GAP IT CLOSES IS A DIRECTION THE ORDERING DOCTRINE DOES NOT COVER. The enum-ordering rule is about OUR VALIDATOR ACCEPTING BEFORE HE EMITS: we widen first, he sends second, and nothing breaks. It is written entirely about values travelling from him to us.

IT HAS NO COVERAGE OF THE OTHER DIRECTION: our own RECORD saying pending while production is already live. That is what happened on 2026-09-03. docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md listed 0028 to 0031 as pending, production had all four, and /Users/ivan/rc-samples/ANDRE-STATUS.md was written from the register. It told him the nineteenth category and the units t and l would 'land when the pending migration batch is applied to production, which is a separate owner-run step'. That was false when it was written.

THE COST WAS A DAY OF HOLDING BACK THREE SAFE VALUES, and he was right to hold them back: he was told they were not there yet.

WHY A MECHANISM AND NOT A RULE, which is the whole argument for this card. The failure is INVISIBLE WHILE IT HAPPENS. Nothing went red. No check failed. Both sides were behaving correctly against the information they had, and the information was wrong. A rule saying 'keep the status document accurate' would have been obeyed by everyone involved and would have changed nothing, because the person writing it believed it was accurate. The only thing that removes this class is Andre being able to ASK PRODUCTION rather than read what we wrote about it.

IT ALSO RETIRES A HAND-MAINTAINED FILE. ANDRE-STATUS.md exists because there was no other way to tell him. Once this endpoint is live that document becomes commentary, and the contract should say the endpoint wins.

RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED INTO THIS CARD: MIG-01 is about the write path that made the register wrong. This card is about the read path that let the wrongness reach a third party. Fixing either one alone leaves the other.

--- PICKED UP 2026-09-07 BY EXECUTOR ---
Worked on branch card/ext-21, flipped to in_flight in the commit that cut the branch and BEFORE any code was written, which is what CLAUDE.md 2 asks for and what RULE-10 exists to make mechanical.

--- SHIPPED 2026-09-07 BY EXECUTOR ---
BUILT ON app/api/health's SHAPE, as the defaults require: same force-dynamic, same no-store, same one-object response, same service-role read. The RLS policies in migration 0001 grant select on categories and units to `authenticated` only, so an ANON read would return an EMPTY LIST rather than an error, which is precisely the silent lie this card exists to remove. The service-role client never leaves the server and no key is ever printed.

A 503 AND NEVER A 200 WITH EMPTY LISTS. When the key is missing, or either select errors, the route answers 503 with `state_unavailable`. A poller cannot tell `we accept nothing` from `I could not look`, and the first of those readings is the one that makes him hold back values that are already safe.

proxy.ts GAINS ONE LINE AND IT IS PART OF THE CONTRACT RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. Without it the middleware answers 307 to /login and a client following redirects reads 200 and text/html: a success code for an authentication page. EXT-08 and P3-11e carry the same line for the same reason and both say so.

THE UNIT LABELS COME FROM CODE AND THE CODES FROM THE DATABASE, said out loud in the route because it is the only half of the answer that is not read live. The enum fixes the values, public.units says which are in use and in what order, and lib/data/units.ts translates. Andre emits the CODE, so the code is the half that has to be live, and it is.

A FINDING THIS CARD DID NOT ACT ON, RECORDED SO THE NEXT ROLE DOES NOT REDISCOVER IT. There is no way to deactivate a category anywhere in the product. The column exists and is read; no screen and no action writes it. That is a gap in the settings screen rather than in this card, and this session's dispatch forbade authoring scope beyond the cards it named, so no card was written for it.

cards.title: The phase 3 schema is verified on production read-only, and the deployed screens are looked at: the four launch conditions that now need nothing but a check get their evidence.
cards.plain: The database work for the new customer and project features is switched on in the live system, but nobody has yet opened the live site and confirmed it works there. This is that check: look at the screens, confirm the access rules really refuse what they should, and write down what was seen, so four of the nine readiness lines stop being unanswered.
cards.acceptance: A COMMITTED REPORT AT docs/reports/<date>-executor-p3-35-production-verification.md CARRYING FOUR NAMED SECTIONS, EACH WITH ITS OUTPUT PASTED VERBATIM, machine-checkable by `grep -c '^## ' docs/reports/<that file>` printing at least 4 and by each heading below appearing in it exactly once. (1) RLS REFUSAL, for launch condition G1: against production, an UNAUTHENTICATED request to clients, contacts and suppliers returns ZERO rows, and a write from a role without permission is refused AT THE DATABASE and not only hidden in the interface, proven the way phase 2 proved it, with real sessions rather than by reading the policy text. (2) UNASSIGNED COUNT, for G2: `select public.unassigned_outbound_count();` run read-only against production and the number PASTED, whatever it is. (3) CROSS-LINK WALK, for G4: all nine directions walked on the deployed site, each landing page identifying the record it was linked from, one line per direction with the URL and what was seen. (4) DEPLOYED SCREENS, for G3: the two list screens and the two detail screens opened on production, with pagination present, filters reflected in the address bar, and no full-length table dumped into a page, one line per screen. PLUS THE GATE EVIDENCE IS WRITTEN: `evidence.ref` on G1, G2, G3 and G4 of docs/board/rc-board-phase3.json names this report by path, and any condition whose clauses are then ALL met is flipped to pass with `readiness_passed` updated to match, which the board validator already enforces. PLUS `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs docs/board/rc-board-phase3.json` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
READ-ONLY MEANS READ-ONLY AND THE SESSION SAYS SO IN SQL. Set `default_transaction_read_only` on before the first statement, exactly as the 2026-08-26 verification of migration 0006 did. This card writes NOTHING to production. There is no migration here, no seed, no fixture and no test user created.

THE CONNECTION IS DERIVED AT RUNTIME PER CLAUDE.md 8.4 AND CONNECTIVITY IS PROVEN WITH SELECT 1 FIRST. On derivation or connection failure, stop, write the exact error into this card's question, and block. Never guess a hostname.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS ECHOED, LOGGED, PASTED INTO THE REPORT OR WRITTEN TO A BOARD FIELD. Variable names only, as everywhere.

PASTE THE NUMBER YOU GET, INCLUDING AN INCONVENIENT ONE. G2's clause demands the unassigned count taken on the day and pasted rather than described, and a non-zero count is a finding to report, not a reason to re-run until it reads better. A backfill that leaves unmatched rows does not close that condition and the gate notes say so.

A CONDITION FLIPS ONLY IF EVERY ONE OF ITS CLAUSES IS MET. Partial credit is not a thing on a gate. If G3's density review finds a screen that dumps a full table, G3 stays fail, the finding goes in the report, and it becomes a card. Expect G1, G2 and G4 to be the ones that can flip and G3 to be the one that finds something.

THE SCREENS ARE VERIFIED ON THE DEPLOYED SITE, NOT ON LOCALHOST. G3's fourth clause says so in terms and it is the clause the previous four audits could not evidence.

IF PRODUCTION CARRIES NO ROWS AT ALL, WHICH IS LIKELY, SAY SO AND DO NOT SEED ANY. An empty table still answers the RLS question and still answers the count question. It does not answer the cross-link walk, and a walk over an empty database is reported as exactly that rather than as nine passes.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-02 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-093, run 20260902-070904, from the phase 3 gate audit rather than from the input report.
WHY IT EXISTS NOW AND COULD NOT HAVE EXISTED BEFORE. Every audit of this gate since 2026-08-31 carried the same sentence on all nine conditions: no phase 3 migration has been applied to production, so no condition can be evidenced whatever ships. Migrations 0013 to 0027 are now all recorded as applied in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md, the Pending section is empty, and P3-27 is shipped. Four conditions are now short of nothing but a check nobody has run.
WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a card that builds anything. It runs read-only checks and looks at deployed screens, and its whole output is a report and four gate evidence fields.
THE CAPABILITY THIS CARD NEEDS IS THE ONE P2-13 REMOVES, and P2-13's acceptance carries a box for it under R-095, because a cross-board depends_on edge makes the board validator red.
G5 IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE. Its second clause needs one real project reconciled by hand, there is no real project, and there will not be one before the client is using the system. That is a different class of missing and it is recorded on the condition rather than carried here.

--- R-137, 2026-09-05: THIS CARD IS NOW THE DECIDING BLOCKER FOR FOUR OF THE NINE ---
The phase 3 gate audit of run 20260905-010004 re-derived all nine conditions against the tree and found that G2, G3, G4 and G6 are blocked by nothing except the verification this card performs, and that G1's two outstanding clauses are this card's clause 1. That is five of the nine touching one card, which makes it the highest-value phase 3 card on the board today by a distance, whatever its id sorts as.

IT OVERLAPS GATE-01 ON CLAUSE 1 AND APPLY-02 ON CLAUSE 2, and neither is retired. Whoever works this first produces the evidence for both and says so in the pull request; whoever works one of those first, this card cites their output rather than re-running it.

THE PREMISE THAT USED TO EXCUSE THE ABSENCE OF THIS EVIDENCE IS DEAD. Every condition's evidence field said no phase 3 migration had been applied. The wave 1 batch is journalled as applied on 2026-08-31, the pending register is empty, and 0026 through 0034 are recorded applied. There is a schema on production to verify.

--- READ THIS BEFORE FLIPPING G2, added 2026-09-07 by TRIAGE under R-145, run 20260906-220005 ---
AN EMPTY-TABLE ZERO DOES NOT CLOSE G2 CLAUSE 3. This card's section 2 pastes
`select public.unassigned_outbound_count();` whatever it returns, and it will return 0.
P3-27's evidence records outbound_issues at ZERO ROWS on production and says in terms that
"BOTH RECONCILIATIONS RETURNED ZERO BECAUSE BOTH SOURCE TABLES ARE EMPTY, so the backfills
proved nothing about real rows". A zero produced by having no issues at all is not the zero
the condition asks for. G2's plain reads "every release of material points at one of them
instead of at a typed-in name", and no releases is not every release.
SO: PASTE THE NUMBER, RECORD THE ROW COUNT BESIDE IT, AND DO NOT FLIP G2. This is written
here rather than into this card's defaults because DOCTRINE-TRIAGE's list of fields TRIAGE
may edit does not include defaults, and the boundary is kept even where crossing it would be
convenient.
THE SAME CAVEAT DOES NOT APPLY TO G1, G3 OR G4. An empty table still answers the RLS
question and the write-refusal question, and the deployed-screen walk is about screens
rather than rows. This card's own defaults already say so.

--- TRIAGE 2026-09-08, RULING R-175: THREE OF THE FOUR CARDS THE GATE-02 REPORT RECOMMENDS ARE THIS CARD ---
From docs/reports/2026-09-08-executor-gate-02-phase3-gate-audit.md, section "What this audit recommends, and does not do". The report
recommends four cards and authors none, correctly, because its own defaults
forbid building inside an audit. Three of the four are already carried here, in
this card's acceptance, clause for clause:
  report recommendation 1, an anon READ probe against clients, contacts and
  suppliers, closing G1 clause 2  ->  acceptance section (1) RLS REFUSAL
  report recommendation 2, a committed read of unassigned_outbound_count(),
  closing G2 clause 3            ->  acceptance section (2) UNASSIGNED COUNT
  report recommendation 3, an authenticated production verification walk serving
  G3 clause 4 and G4 clause 1    ->  acceptance sections (3) CROSS-LINK WALK and
                                     (4) DEPLOYED SCREENS
NONE OF THE THREE WAS AUTHORED. DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 5 forbids it and there
is a second reason that is specific to this card: P2-13's acceptance names P3-35
BY ID, under R-095, as the box that must be ticked before any credential is
rotated. Three new cards needing the same production connection would be three
capabilities the revocation checklist does not name, which is the exact defect
GATE-03 shipped npm run check:grant-revocation to catch.
THE ONE GAP THE REPORT NAMES AND THIS CARD DOES NOT ANSWER, RECORDED HERE
RATHER THAN FIXED. The report says of recommendation 3 that it is "the hardest,
because nothing in this project currently holds a production session", and this
card's defaults say "There is no migration here, no seed, no fixture and no test
user created." Both are right and together they do not say how a terminal signs
in. Sections (3) and (4) need an authenticated session; sections (1) and (2) do
not. TRIAGE did not rewrite the acceptance, because granting a terminal access
to a production account is item 5 of the closed escalation list and is not
TRIAGE's to decide. WHAT EXECUTOR SHOULD DO: run sections (1) and (2), which
need only the read-only connection CLAUDE.md 8.3 and 8.4 already govern, report
them, and block this card on ivan for sections (3) and (4) with the structured
decision-needed text of CLAUDE.md section 4 naming the session as the thing that
is missing. Half of four conditions evidenced beats none.
THE FOURTH RECOMMENDATION IS NOT HERE AND IS NOT ABOUT THIS CARD. It is
GUARD-07, authored today under R-178.

cards.title: The migration applier stops pinning one function signature forever: create_outbound_issue becomes declared intent like the rest, so a later migration that legitimately changes it can be applied instead of rolling its whole batch back.
cards.plain: The safety check that guards changes to the live database has one rule frozen to how things looked in August. Any future change to how material is issued out would be refused by it, and the refusal would only appear at the very last step, taking unrelated work down with it. This unfreezes that one rule without weakening any of the others.
cards.acceptance: `npm run prove:applier` exits 0 WITH A NEW CASE ADDED, and the case is a fixture migration that legitimately changes the signature of public.create_outbound_issue, applied against the Docker shim, which APPLIES CLEANLY when the file declares the change and is REFUSED, whole batch rolled back, when it does not. BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED and the negative half is the one that matters: an undeclared signature change must still roll the batch back, because the point is to move the decision into the migration file and not to remove it. PLUS THE CONTROL IS PROVED STILL TO BITE: a fixture in which create_outbound_issue exists in TWO versions still fails the assertion, since that half of it catches an ambiguous call and is not what this card relaxes. PLUS `npm run prove:applier` is proved to FAIL against the current scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs on the new case first, with the failing output quoted in the pull request. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE DECLARATION LIVES IN THE MIGRATION FILE AND IS PARSED, NEVER PASSED AT THE PROMPT. R-082 and R-047 both rest on the script deciding rather than the terminal choosing, and anything a terminal can type at run time is a choice. A declaration is honoured only for the exact object it names.

THE ABSOLUTE EXCLUSION IS UNTOUCHED AND NO DECLARATION REACHES IT. DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE and DELETE stay refused with nothing executed. This card touches one function-signature assertion and nothing about what the applier permits.

R-085 IS THE RULE THIS CARD IS AN INSTANCE OF, AND IT DECIDES THE IMPLEMENTATION: a guard that needs to know whether an object EXISTS asks the catalogues at run time, and a guard that needs to know what the batch INTENDED reads the parsed declarations. This assertion is doing the second job with a hardcoded literal, which is neither.

ledger-0010-0011-0012-present IS LEFT EXACTLY AS IT IS AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. It asserts a one-time repair whose rows are now permanently present, so the assertion is permanently true and removing it would be change without benefit. Do not spend a session tidying it.

free-text-columns-untouched IS ALREADY GONE from the script and is not part of this card. It was removed under R-085's audit and the two column drops it named have shipped and applied.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-02 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-090, run 20260902-070904.
IT CARRIES THE STILL-LIVE HALF OF A FINDING FIRST MADE AS R-088 on branch triage/20260901-070544, which is open as pull request 143 and CONFLICTING and has never reached main. R-088 authored that finding as a card P3-29; a different card P3-29 landed on main four hours later, so the id was taken and this card is the re-authoring. R-090 records the whole disposition.
WHAT IS VOID FROM THE ORIGINAL FINDING, STATED SO NOBODY REBUILDS IT: the assertion free-text-columns-untouched, which was its headline, no longer exists in the script, and the two drop cards it would have refused have both shipped and applied.
WHAT IS CONFIRMED AND WAS RE-VERIFIED IN THE TREE ON 2026-09-02: one-create-outbound-issue-five-args pins create_outbound_issue to the exact signature (text, text, text, jsonb, uuid) with no off-ramp, at scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs lines 1012 to 1028.
WHY IT IS WORTH A CARD RATHER THAN A LEARNING. The applier is the only lawful route from a merged migration file to the live database, it runs the whole batch in one transaction, and a refusal rolls back every unrelated migration batched alongside it. The failure is invisible until the apply and the apply is the last step, so whoever hits it will be working a card that has nothing to do with issuing material.

cards.title: Migration 0028 is applied, and a pending register line whose named apply card has already shipped fails the build instead of sitting there.
cards.plain: One finished piece of database work has been published but never switched on in the live system, and the job that was supposed to switch it on has already been closed, so nobody owns it any more. This switches it on and adds a check so the next one cannot go unowned.
cards.acceptance: REWRITTEN 2026-09-07 BY TRIAGE UNDER RULING R-147. HALF A IS DISCHARGED AND IS REMOVED FROM THE ACCEPTANCE; ITS TEXT IS QUOTED IN THIS CARD'S NOTES PER CLAUDE.md 9c AND IS NOT DELETED. WHAT REMAINS IS THE CHECK, AND IT LANDS ALONE. THE CHECK, WIRED INTO THE quality JOB BY NAME AND PROVED TO FAIL FIRST: it reads every `card de aplicare <id>` line in the pending register at docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md and FAILS when that id is carried by no board, or is carried by a card whose status is `shipped`. THE FAILING CASE IS NOW A FIXTURE RATHER THAN THE TREE, because the register is EMPTY: the pull request quotes the check refusing a fixture register carrying the exact line that stood on main when this card was authored, `0028_applied_ledger_version.sql, card de aplicare P3-11e`, with P3-11e shipped. A fixture is required and a hand-edited working tree is not acceptable, for the reason FIXTURE-01 gives. IT ASSERTS ITS OWN INPUT COUNT: zero pending lines parsed from a NON-EMPTY register is a hard failure, not a clean tree; an EMPTY register reads as zero pending lines and exits 0, and both of those are asserted separately. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 and `node docs/board/validate-board.mjs` over all three boards exits 0.
cards.defaults:
HALF B LANDS EVEN IF HALF A CANNOT, AND THEN THIS CARD BLOCKS RATHER THAN SHIPS. If the R-082 grant has expired, if P2-13 has run, or if the 8.2 zero-real-client-data precondition no longer holds, the apply is not attempted: the check ships, the card goes blocked_on ivan with the reason named, and nobody guesses a hostname or tries a credential that was not derived per 8.4.

0028 IS NOT DELETE-CLASS AND THAT WAS ESTABLISHED BEFORE THIS CARD WAS WRITTEN. `grep -inE 'drop table|truncate|delete'` over the file matches nothing. It creates one SECURITY DEFINER function, revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC and grants it to service_role. Section 8.6 is checked again by the applier's own parse before anything runs, as it is for every file.

THE SCRIPT DECIDES AND THE TERMINAL REPORTS. R-082 condition 5. Do not read a grid and judge whether a count looks close enough. If the applier rolls back, the card records what it decided and blocks.

WHEN THE CHECK'S RULE IS AMBIGUOUS, FAIL. A pending line naming a card that no board carries is a failure, not a skip. That is the same shape as a matcher whose empty result reads as nothing-to-do, which docs/LEARNINGS.md already names.

DO NOT REOPEN P3-11e. It shipped correctly on its own acceptance, which is a health route and a deployed-commit check and says nothing about applying anything. R-062 split merged from applied on purpose. This card is the apply, not a correction to that one.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED BY TRIAGE, run 20260903-070005, under ruling R-089. NOT FROM THE DISPATCH REPORT: it came out of the DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 3 sweep and section 4 gate audit, both required every run over committed repository files.

VERIFIED ON main AT 3642d79. docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md line 42 reads `- 0028_applied_ledger_version.sql, card de aplicare P3-11e`. The applied section of that file runs 0001 to 0027 and carries no 0028 entry. P3-11e is shipped and its own notes say '0028 IS AUTHORED AND MERGED, NOT APPLIED'. `grep -c 0028` over all three boards returns 2, both inside P3-11e, so no open card carries this apply.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG, SO THE CARD IS NOT READ AS A REPRIMAND. P3-11e shipping was right, tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts is satisfied because 0028 is in exactly one of the two places, and nothing in the record lied. What has no liveness is the `card de aplicare` field: it names a card and nothing asks whether that card is still open.

WHY IT RECURS WITHOUT THE CHECK. P3-27 existed because thirteen files reached this state at once and were reachable by nobody. One night after P3-27 cleared the register, a fourteenth entered it and its named card closed.

PLACED ON THE PHASE 3 BOARD because 0028 was authored by P3-11e, which lives here. This board is worked by interactive terminals and is not wired into the harness.

RENUMBERED FROM P3-35 TO P3-37 ON 2026-09-03 BY EXECUTOR, BEFORE EITHER PULL REQUEST LANDED. Two open TRIAGE pull requests each allocated P3-35 for different work: #157 for the production read-only schema verification, this one for applying migration 0028. Neither had a way to see the other, which is the exact collision class RULE-02 was built for, caught here on the merge rather than after both had landed.

THIS ONE MOVES AND #157 KEEPS P3-35, on the older-branch-wins rule: #157 was cut first and is the one whose id other text already cites. No content changed, only the identifier, and no id anywhere else was renumbered.

--- ACCEPTANCE REWRITTEN 2026-09-07 BY TRIAGE UNDER R-147, run 20260906-220005 ---
HALF A DESCRIBED A PRODUCTION STATE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, WHICH IS APPLY-02'S SHAPE AND
R-142'S REASONING APPLIED A SECOND TIME. It asked a terminal to apply 0028 through the
assertion-bearing applier and then read a non-null applied ledger version from /api/health.
0028 IS APPLIED. docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md carries it as one of the four RECONSTRUCTED
entries for 0028 to 0031, applied by the Supabase GitHub integration on merge with no
terminal involved, which is the mechanism ruling R-124 established with a prediction and an

with /api/health returning the same value, which is exactly the observation half A asked for,
taken by somebody else for another reason. THE PENDING REGISTER IS EMPTY, so there is no

THE OLD HALF A, QUOTED RATHER THAN DELETED, PER CLAUDE.md 9c:
> "(A) THE APPLY: `node scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs` against the phase 2 Supabase project applies supabase/migrations/0028_applied_ledger_version.sql under ruling R-082, exits 0 ... THEN `curl -s <production origin>/api/health` returns 200 application/json whose applied ledger version is a VALUE and not null, which is the whole reason 0028 exists."
AND THE SENTENCE IN HALF B THAT IS NOW FALSE, ALSO QUOTED:

That line is gone from the register, so the check can no longer be proved to fail against the

cards.title: Apply the six merged migrations 0028 to 0033 to the production Supabase project through the assertion-bearing applier, and journal all three phases.
cards.plain: Six finished pieces of database work have been built and approved but never switched on in the live system, so the features that depend on them are invisible to anyone using the site. This turns them on, and every readiness condition on the second list is waiting behind it.
cards.acceptance: SUPERSEDED IN ITS PREMISE 2026-09-05 BY R-133 AND REWRITTEN AS A VERIFICATION, NOT AN APPLY. READ THIS FIRST: the six files this card was authored to apply are recorded APPLIED, the pending register in docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md is EMPTY, and ruling R-124 established that merging a migration applies it to production within about two minutes with no terminal involved. THE ACCEPTANCE IS NOW ALL FOUR OF THESE. (1) THE REGISTER DECIDES WHICH SHAPE THIS CARD TAKES, and it is read first and quoted in the pull request: if docs/migrations/APPLY-LOG.md lists ANY file under "Pending: authored and merged, NOT applied", node scripts/apply-pending-migrations.mjs runs and must exit 0 having COMMITTED with every assertion passing inside the transaction; if the register is EMPTY, the applier is NOT run and the pull request says so, because an applier invoked against an empty batch proves nothing about production. (2) READ-ONLY AGAINST PRODUCTION, with default_transaction_read_only on: the applied ledger's highest version equals the highest numbered file in supabase/migrations/, and the row count equals the number of files that log records as applied. THE NUMBERS ARE DERIVED FROM THE TREE ON THE DAY AND ARE NOT PINNED HERE; the previous wording pinned 0033 and 33 rows and 0034_error_code_reconciliation_failed.sql merged afterwards. (3) THE JOURNAL SAYS WHICH KIND OF RECORD IT IS: any apply this card performs is journalled with the three phases CLAUDE.md 8.5 requires, and any file it merely VERIFIES as already applied is recorded as an integration apply per section 8.0 and marked as a reconstruction, never as a journal of a run nobody made. (4) The health route from P3-11e reports the same ledger version as the query in (2), so the deployed commit and the applied schema agree rather than being asserted to.
cards.defaults:
THE APPLIER DECIDES AND THE TERMINAL REPORTS WHAT IT DECIDED. CLAUDE.md 8.6's second exception and R-082 are the whole of the authority and their five conditions are not negotiable: one transaction, the pending register and applied ledger recorded before and after, assertions evaluated in SQL inside the transaction after the mutations and before the commit, commit only on all-pass, and the terminal never chooses. A hand-run psql against production is not covered by this and never was, whatever the output looks like.

NONE OF THE SIX CONTAINS A FORBIDDEN STATEMENT, checked 2026-09-04 across all six files for DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE and DELETE, and none appears. THAT FINDING DOES NOT OUTRANK THE PARSER. If the applier's own pgsql-parser pass disagrees, THE PARSER WINS, the applier refuses with nothing executed, and the card goes blocked_on ivan with the statement quoted verbatim. A grep is a string search and the parser is the PostgreSQL grammar.

0030 AND 0031 ARE THE ENUM PAIR AND THE APPLIER ALREADY KNOWS WHAT TO DO WITH THEM. 0030 carries ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE and 0031 uses the labels, which is R-082's one bounded deviation from "one transaction" and is the server's rule rather than a preference. The card RECORDS which files went to the pre-phase and does not argue with the split. If 0030 lacks IF NOT EXISTS on any addition, the applier is right to refuse and the card blocks rather than being edited around.

A MIGRATION FILE IS NEVER EDITED TO MAKE AN APPLY PASS. CLAUDE.md 8.1: a correction is a new numbered file. If a file needs changing, this card stops and a new card authors 0034.

cards.title: listReviewDrafts asks PostgREST for every pending draft's lines in ONE url, so past roughly two hundred pending drafts the request is refused 414 and EVERY draft renders with zero lines, silently.
cards.plain: Once a few hundred documents are waiting to be checked, the checking screen stops showing what is written on any of them. Every document looks empty, there is no error, and the only way to notice is to know what should have been there.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named test proves the review screen renders its line items with MORE pending drafts than the refusal threshold, driven by seeding that many drafts and reading the screen, and it must FAIL against the current implementation with the failure output shown in the pull request. PLUS: the fix removes the unbounded url, by batching the id list, by filtering server-side instead of by id list, or by joining the lines in the same request; whichever is chosen, the choice and the two rejected alternatives are recorded on the card. PLUS: the SILENCE is closed as well as the size. Every ignored `const { data } = await supabase...` on this path reads its error and a failed read becomes a visible failure rather than an empty list, because a screen that cannot tell "no lines" from "I could not read the lines" is the actual defect and the url length is only what triggered it. PLUS: the sibling `.in("id", ids)` against inbound_orders on the same function is fixed in the same pull request or a reason is recorded for why it is not exposed. PLUS COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE SILENCE IS THE DEFECT, THE URL IS THE TRIGGER. lib/data/extraction.ts destructures `const { data: lines }` and never looks at `error`. A 414 therefore renders as "this document has no line items" on every card at once. Fixing only the batching would leave the next unread error just as quiet.

DO NOT SOLVE IT BY CAPPING THE DRAFT LIST. A limit on how many pending drafts the screen shows would hide the older ones instead of the lines, which is a different wrong answer to the same question, and the operator would have no way to know either.

PREFER ONE REQUEST THAT ASKS THE SERVER TO DO THE JOIN, if PostgREST's embedded-resource syntax can express it against extraction_draft_lines, because a batch loop is a size that has to be chosen and a chosen size is a threshold somebody meets again later. If it cannot, batch, and put the batch size in ONE named constant with the measured threshold beside it.

THE THRESHOLD IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT IS ENVIRONMENT-SPECIFIC. 208 ids returned 200 and 209 returned 414 against the local Supabase stack on 2026-09-04, which is about 7.7 KB of request line. The hosted project sits behind different infrastructure and its limit may differ. The test must not encode 208; it must exceed whatever the environment allows, or the fix must remove the dependence on a threshold entirely, which is the reason the paragraph above prefers the join.

evidence.ref:
Branch card/p3-38, cut from main at eff79ed.

THE CHOSEN FIX IS THE EMBEDDED JOIN AND THERE IS NO LONGER AN ID LIST FOR THE LINES.
lib/data/extraction.ts selects `${draftColumns}, extraction_draft_lines(${LINE_COLUMNS})`
in the SAME request as the drafts. extraction_draft_lines.order_id carries a real
foreign key to extraction_drafts.order_id (migration 0008 line 140), so PostgREST
expresses the join itself. The card's defaults asked for exactly this if it could
be expressed, and it can.

THE TWO REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, AS THE CARD REQUIRES, EACH WITH ITS MEASURED REASON.
(1) BATCH THE LINES ID LIST. Rejected on the card's own ground, that a batch size is
a chosen number and a chosen number is a threshold somebody meets again, AND on a
measurement taken for this decision: max_rows = 1000 in supabase/config.toml caps a
FLAT list across the whole result and caps an EMBED per parent. Two drafts of 600
lines each returned [1000] rows flat, losing 200 silently, and [600, 600] embedded.
Batching would have traded a loud 414 for a quiet truncation spread across drafts,
which is the same defect one level harder to see.
(2) FILTER SERVER-SIDE FROM THE LINES TABLE instead of by id list, selecting lines
whose draft is unconfirmed. Rejected because it is the same PostgREST relationship
reached from the weaker side: it returns a flat list under the whole-set cap above,
and the application must then regroup it by order_id, which is the exact step where
the old code lost the ability to tell 'no lines' from 'I could not read the lines'.

THE SILENCE IS CLOSED, WHICH IS THE HALF THE CARD CALLS THE ACTUAL DEFECT. All three
reads on the path now read `error` and throw a Romanian message: the drafts read, the
inbound_orders read, and linesOf(), which refuses a draft row that arrived WITHOUT the
embedded key at all. An empty array means the document has no lines; an absent key
means the select did not ask, and that is a code defect rather than a document.

THE SIBLING IS FIXED IN THE SAME PULL REQUEST, NOT DEFERRED. The .in('id', ids)
against inbound_orders cannot be embedded, because extraction_drafts.order_id
carries NO foreign key to inbound_orders and 0008's header says that is deliberate.
It batches through ID_LIST_BATCH_SIZE in lib/data/id-list.ts, ONE named constant in
ONE file with both measurements written beside it. PROVEN AGAINST THE LIVE STACK at
the pending count this run reached: 336 ids -> 414 at 12495 URL bytes, 100 ids -> 200
at 3763 bytes.

THE THRESHOLD IS MEASURED BY THE TEST, NEVER WRITTEN INTO IT, as the card requires.
review.spec case 15 probes the same PostgREST the application uses, doubling from 32
to a ceiling of 400, and seeds above whatever it found. On this stack on 2026-09-05:
128 ids -> 200 at 4819 URL bytes, 256 ids -> 414 at 9555 bytes. The earlier bisection
of 208 accepted / 209 refused appears in comments as a recorded measurement and in no
assertion. The helper tops up to a TARGET rather than adding a quantity, so a
persistent lane does not accumulate past max_rows on the second run.

THE FAILING HALF, RUN BEFORE THE FIX, OUTPUT IN THE PULL REQUEST AND THE REPORT.
Case 15 against the unchanged implementation, on a lane seeded to 288 pending drafts:

  Locator: getByTestId('review-line-name-0')
  Expected: "Tigla metalica Bilka Classic 0.45mm visiniu mtojto9t"

The review form opened and rendered with NO line inputs at all, which is the defect

COMMANDS, ALL ON A PERSISTENT LOCAL SUPABASE STACK BUILT WITH THE CI RECIPE AND NEVER
RESET BETWEEN RUNS, WHICH IS THE CONDITION CI CANNOT REPRODUCE.
  baseline on origin/main before any change: review.spec 14 of 14 passed

sites exist in the repository and all five were read. Two are on this function and
both are fixed here. The other three each build a URL from an id list that is
unbounded in principle: lib/data/inbound-actions.ts:92, lib/data/extraction-actions.ts:338
and lib/reminders/notify.ts:111. All three ignore their error the same way. They are
NOT fixed here and the reason is their bound: each list is the product ids of ONE

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-04 BY EXECUTOR, FROM A DEFECT THE EXT-18 TEST LANE HIT AND THE PROBE THEN CONFIRMED. NOT BUILT: it is outside the dispatch, and CLAUDE.md 3 says a defect noticed in passing becomes a card rather than a quiet extra commit.

HOW IT WAS FOUND. After eight full runs of extraction.spec and review.spec against one persistent local stack, review.spec case 1 went red on `review-line-name-0` not found: the review form rendered with NO line inputs. The database then held 252 unconfirmed drafts and 451 lines.

HOW IT WAS CONFIRMED, AND IT IS A PROBE WITH A CONTROL RATHER THAN A STORY. Three requests to the local PostgREST, same endpoint, same key, only the id-list length changing:

  50 ids   -> 200
  150 ids  -> 200
  252 ids  -> 414 URI Too Long

Bisected: 208 ids returns 200, 209 returns 414. About 7.7 KB of request line, which is the shape of an 8 KB limit in the gateway in front of PostgREST.

WHAT THE CODE DOES WITH THAT 414. Nothing. `const { data: lines } = await supabase.from("extraction_draft_lines").select(...).in("order_id", ...)` discards the error, `lines` is undefined, the per-order map is empty, and every draft is mapped with an empty line array. THE SCREEN CANNOT TELL "no lines" FROM "I could not read the lines", and neither can the operator.

THE SIBLING IS ON THE SAME FUNCTION. The `.in("id", ids)` against inbound_orders a few lines above has the same unbounded shape. It is less exposed today, because its result is used to EXCLUDE drafts and a 414 there would make the screen show MORE drafts rather than fewer, but it is the same defect and it is named here so the fix does not leave half of it.

IT IS NOT VISIBLE IN CI, AND THAT IS WHY IT SURVIVED. Every CI run starts from `supabase db reset`, so the pending-draft count never leaves single digits. It needs an installation that has been running, which is exactly the installation the client will have.

BUILT AND SHIPPED 2026-09-05 BY EXECUTOR, AHEAD OF THE BOARD ORDER ON THE OWNER'S DISPATCH.

THE DEFECT REPRODUCED EXACTLY AS AUTHORED, AND THE CARD'S OWN NUMBERS WERE RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN TRANSCRIBED. The card records 208 accepted and 209 refused from 2026-09-04. This run measured the same shape again on a stack built the same way: 128 ids accepted at 4819 URL bytes, 256 refused at 9555. Same 8 KB shape, different boundary, which is why the test measures instead of encoding either number.

WHAT THE CARD DID NOT ANTICIPATE AND THIS RUN MEASURED. The row cap behaves DIFFERENTLY on the two shapes: max_rows caps a flat list across the whole result and caps an embedded resource per parent. That makes the embed the better answer for a second reason the card did not state, and it makes the batch alternative worse than the card assumed: it would have replaced a 414 with a silent truncation.

ONE EXPOSURE OF THE SAME CLASS IS FOUND AND NOT FIXED, AND IT IS NAMED HERE SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED TWICE. The drafts query itself is capped at max_rows = 1000 and orders by fired_at descending, so an installation with more than a thousand pending drafts silently drops the oldest from the review screen. It is out of this card's scope, it is a different threshold from the one this card closes, and no card is authored for it because the dispatch says not to author new scope. It is in the session report.

cards.title: The review screen's draft list is capped by PostgREST's row limit and drops the OLDEST drafts silently, because nothing compares what came back against what exists.
cards.plain: Once there are more documents waiting to be checked than the system returns in one go, the oldest ones stop appearing on the checking screen. Nothing says they were left out, so a document can wait for ever without anyone knowing it is there.
cards.acceptance: COMMAND: a named test proves the review screen shows a draft that sits BEYOND the row limit, driven by seeding more pending drafts than the environment returns in one request and then reading the screen for the OLDEST one, and it must FAIL against the current implementation with the failure output shown in the pull request. PLUS: the SILENCE is closed as well as the size, and this is the half that decides the card. The read compares WHAT CAME BACK against WHAT EXISTS, by asking for the count in the same request, and a short answer becomes a VISIBLE failure rather than a shorter list. A screen that cannot tell "these are all the drafts" from "these are the first thousand" is the defect, and the row limit is only what triggers it. PLUS: the limit is MEASURED by the test against the environment it runs in and is NEVER written into the test or the code as a literal, for the same reason P3-38's 208 is not: the local stack sets max_rows in supabase/config.toml and the hosted project may answer differently, and a number copied into a test is a fact about a machine that has since changed. PLUS: whichever fix is chosen, paging until exhausted or a server-side filter that cannot exceed the limit, the choice and the rejected alternative are recorded on the card. PLUS COMMAND: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0. PLUS COMMAND: `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE SILENCE IS THE DEFECT, THE ROW LIMIT IS THE TRIGGER, AND THIS IS THE SAME SENTENCE P3-38 WAS BUILT ON. lib/data/extraction.ts reads the drafts with no limit and no count, so a capped response and a complete one are the same value to every line below it. Fixing only the paging would leave the next cap just as quiet.

DO NOT SOLVE IT BY RAISING max_rows. That is a setting on one environment, it moves the threshold rather than removing it, and it cannot be set on the hosted project from this repository at all. The same reasoning P3-38's defaults use against capping the draft list applies here against raising the cap.

PREFER A READ THAT CANNOT EXCEED THE LIMIT OVER ONE THAT PAGES. Paging is a loop whose size has to be chosen, and a chosen size is a threshold somebody meets again, which is the argument P3-38 settled in favour of the embedded join. If the pending set can be bounded server-side so it cannot reach the cap, do that. If it cannot, page until exhausted, and put the page size in ONE named constant beside the one lib/data/id-list.ts already holds rather than a second one somewhere else.

THE ORDER IS WHY IT IS THE OLDEST THAT VANISH. The query orders fired_at descending with nullsFirst false, so a cap takes the tail, and the tail is the documents that have been waiting longest. That is the worst possible half to drop and it is worth saying on the screen if the fix cannot remove it.

MEASURE THE HOSTED LIMIT BEFORE QUOTING IT. supabase/config.toml sets max_rows = 1000 for the LOCAL stack. The hosted project's limit was NOT verified when this card was authored and could not be, because production holds zero extraction drafts, so there is nothing to page. Whoever builds this measures it rather than assuming the two agree.

THE EMBEDDED LINES ARE NOT THE PROBLEM HERE AND MUST NOT BE RE-OPENED. P3-38 measured that max_rows caps a flat list across the whole result and caps an embed PER PARENT, so the nested lines are safe. This card is about the TOP LEVEL row count only.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS READ, PRINTED OR LOGGED, and no test writes to the hosted project.

evidence.ref:
Pull request #285, branch card/p3-39-fix, cut from origin/main at 8372d39. Not card/p3-39: that branch is left over from PR #226, which authored this card, and is unrelated.

THE CHOSEN FIX IS PAGING UNTIL EXHAUSTED, WITH THE TOTAL ASKED IN THE SAME REQUEST.
lib/data/extraction.ts reads the drafts through readAllPages in lib/data/id-list.ts: `.select(..., { count: "exact" }).range(from, to)`, ordered fired_at descending nulls last THEN order_id, so pages join by position. The page size is ROW_PAGE_SIZE, ONE named constant beside ID_LIST_BATCH_SIZE, and it is not a threshold: each page starts after the rows that ACTUALLY came back, not after the rows asked for, so a server that caps below the page size costs more requests and loses no rows.

THE SILENCE IS CLOSED. Every page carries the total. An empty page before the total, a missing total, or a total that changes between pages throws; the rows collected must equal the total exactly. A short answer is a visible failure (the error screen), never a shorter list. Proved without a database by the case "P3-39: citirea pe pagini aduna tot sub o limita mai mica decat pagina, iar un raspuns scurt este un esec vizibil": a fake server capped below the page size returns every row in order, and short, total-less, shifting and erroring answers each throw.

THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: A SERVER-SIDE READ THAT CANNOT EXCEED THE LIMIT. The pending set has no server-side bound that is not itself a cut: it grows with unreviewed documents, and showing part of it is the defect. The only single-response shape is a function returning everything as one JSON row, which is a migration, and it moves the limit from row count to response size rather than removing it. Raising max_rows was rejected by the card's own defaults. No on-screen notice about the ordering was added, because the fix removes the cap rather than living with it.

THE LIMIT IS MEASURED BY THE TEST, NEVER WRITTEN. measureRowLimit makes one unlimited read with Prefer: count=exact and compares rows returned with the content-range total, doubling the sent drafts until they differ. It counts only drafts WITH fired_at when seeding, because P3-38's filler has none and nulls sort last, so it cannot push the oldest draft past the cap. The measured figure is printed in the run log as a line starting `P3-39 limita masurata`.

cards.plain: Suppliers bill in pallets, boxes and sets, and the system now knows how many of each a product's package holds. cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 WITH FOUR NEW CASES, AND ALL FOUR ARE PROVED TO FAIL FIRST against the current tree with the failing output quoted in the pull request. (2) THE ORDINARY CASE IS UNTOUCHED: the same line against a product carrying NEITHER packaging field confirms and the stock rises by 2. (3) NO CONVERSION ON A GUESS: a line whose unit does NOT match the product's package_unit confirms and the stock rises by the billed quantity unchanged, so a factor is never applied to a unit nobody matched. (4) BOTH NUMBERS ARE VISIBLE BEFORE CONFIRM, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT: with package_factor 2.5 and a billed quantity of 3, the review screen shows the billed figure, the package unit, the factor and the resulting stock figure, all in Romanian, and the stock figure reads exactly 7.5 and not 7.499999999. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS IF ANY MIGRATION IS ADDED, `npm run check:migrations` exits 0 with an assertions file under scripts/poc-free/local-db/assertions/; if none is added the pull request says so in one line rather than leaving a reader to check.

THE EXTRACTION CONTRACT DOES NOT CHANGE AND THIS CARD MUST NOT PROPOSE THAT IT DOES. Block the card, write the structured decision-needed text, and take the next one. Do not negotiate a contract inside a card.

THE STORED DRAFT IS NEVER REWRITTEN. The conversion happens at confirm. What the draft row holds stays what the document said, because the draft is the record of the document and a converted draft can no longer be checked against the paper it came from.

MATCHING IS FOLDED AND FORGIVING, AND IT IS DONE IN TYPESCRIPT WITHOUT A MIGRATION. Compare trimmed, lower-cased, diacritic-folded text, `unit_raw` first and then `unit`. This is a comparison between one line and one product row, not a lookup across a table, so it needs no SQL function and no new index. A blank on either side never matches anything.

NO MATCH AND NO PACKAGING BOTH MEAN NO CONVERSION, AND THAT IS THE ORDINARY CASE RATHER THAN A FAILURE. EXT-10's own defaults say most products have no packaging. A line that converts nothing is not a warning, an error or an empty state; it is a normal line.

A CONVERSION THE USER CANNOT SEE IS WORSE THAN NO CONVERSION. The review screen shows the billed figure and the stock figure together, in Romanian, before the confirm button is reachable. A number that silently multiplied by 48 between the screen and the database is the failure this card exists to prevent, not a convenience it delivers.

DO THE ARITHMETIC IN THE NUMERIC DOMAIN, NOT IN A FLOAT YOU HOPE ABOUT. package_factor is numeric(14,3) and fractional factors are legal: EXT-10's assertions file accepts 2.5 deliberately, because a 2.5 kg set is a real supplier package. Case 4 exists to catch a float that produces 7.499999999.

SCHEMA CHANGES ARE ALLOWED BUT ARE NOT ASSUMED. If the stock write needs a column to record what was billed alongside what was stocked, add it in a new numbered migration with its own assertions file, and gate every read of it behind a capability flag in lib/data/schema-capability.ts exactly as EXT-10 did. cards.plain: When a scan fails, the system keeps the supplier name, the dates and the totals so somebody can type the delivery in by hand. It does not keep how many pages the document had, so nobody typing it in can tell whether they are looking at the whole thing.
cards.question:
DECISION NEEDED, TWO QUESTIONS AND THE SECOND IS NEW. ONE: which document is authoritative about the shape of a scan-sourced `failed` payload, this contract or the fixture? TWO: how does a page count reach that shape, given it has no `_meta` object to put one in? 

QUESTION ONE, MEASURED AT 18f3cb1 AND NOT ASSUMED. THE TWO DISAGREE TODAY. `docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md` section 4.1a says the payload is **SEVENTEEN FIELDS** and lists `order_ref_series` among them, added by card EXT-11 on 2026-09-07, with the count stated out loud in the text. The shipped fixture `scanFailureHeader` at `tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` enumerates **SIXTEEN** keys, does NOT carry `order_ref_series`, and its own comment still reads `Cele saisprezece campuri`. The fixture is the thing a reader checks a real payload against, and the contract is the thing the two sides agreed. They cannot both be right about the count. NO RECOMMENDATION IS OFFERED ON THIS ONE, deliberately: it is a question about which record binds, which is not a terminal's to answer. 

QUESTION TWO, CONTEXT, ALSO MEASURED. `page_count` is read at `app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts` from `_meta.page_count` and from nowhere else, through the guard that turns a broken report into null. The header-only shape carries no `_meta`, so on this shape the page count is null BY CONSTRUCTION, every time, for every document. WHY IT MATTERS ON EXACTLY THIS SHAPE. The header-only payload exists so a human can key the document by hand against a known total. That human cannot tell a one-page delivery note from page one of four, and a delivery keyed from half a document is the failure this board exists to stop. 

OPTIONS FOR QUESTION TWO: A. AN EXTRA TOP-LEVEL FIELD. `page_count` joins the fixed list in section 4.1a as an integer or null. Smallest change to the shape, needs Andre to send it, and 4.1a's stated count moves again in the same edit. B. `_meta` IS PERMITTED ON THIS SHAPE. The whole object returns, today's reader works unchanged, future diagnostics arrive free. It reopens the narrowing EXT-20 made on purpose: the shape is what it is so nothing can be silently added to it. C. WE COUNT THE PAGES OURSELVES from the stored document. Needs nobody's agreement about the contract, and needs a PDF library this repository does not have, which is a vendor decision under item 4 of the closed escalation list. NOT recommended on those grounds alone. 

RECOMMENDATION FOR QUESTION TWO: A. It is the smallest change, it keeps EXT-20's narrowing intact, and it puts the field where a reader of section 4.1a will find it rather than inside an object that section says is absent. 

IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: every hand-keyed delivery is keyed by somebody who cannot tell whether they have the whole document, and the contract and the fixture keep saying different things about the same payload. The system does not get worse while this waits; it stays exactly as blind as it is today.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` exits 0 WITH TWO NEW CASES PROVED TO FAIL FIRST against the current tree, the failing output quoted in the pull request. (1) THE COUNT ARRIVES AND IS STORED: the header-only shape carrying whatever field the answer to this card's question names is accepted 202, and `page_count` is read back off the stored draft as the integer sent. (2) ABSENCE IS STILL NOT AN ERROR: the same shape WITHOUT it is still accepted 202 and the stored `page_count` is null, because EXT-09's rule that a missing diagnostic never rejects a document is not reopened by this card. PLUS the guard at route.ts:83 keeps refusing zero, negative, fractional and non-numeric reports by turning them into null rather than into a 400, asserted by a case. PLUS docs/contracts/extraction-v2.md section 4.1a is edited in the same pull request, with its stated field count moved to match its own rows. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE STATED COUNT AND THE ROWS MOVE TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL. Section 4.1a says its count out loud precisely because a list whose stated count disagrees with its own rows is a list nobody trusts, and it has already been corrected once for that reason when EXT-11 made sixteen into seventeen. A pull request that adds a field and leaves the word `seventeen` standing is incomplete.

THE CODE'S FIXTURE AND THE CONTRACT'S LIST DISAGREE TODAY, AND WHOEVER WORKS THIS CARD FIXES IT IN PASSING BECAUSE THEY CANNOT AVOID IT. The contract lists seventeen fields including `order_ref_series`; `scanFailureHeader` at tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts:1173 enumerates sixteen and does not carry `order_ref_series`, and its own comment still says `Cele saisprezece campuri`. The fixture is the thing a reader checks a real payload against, so it is the thing that is wrong. This is not scope: the card edits that fixture either way.

EXT-20's REJECTION RULE IS NOT TOUCHED. A scan-sourced `failed` payload still carries NO `lines` key, empty or not, and still gets a 400 if it does. Nothing in this card is permission to soften that.

DO NOT ADD A COLUMN. `extraction_drafts.page_count` already exists: migration 0032 is applied and route.ts:442 writes it behind a capability gate. This card is about the payload, not the schema.

cards.title: Two end-to-end specs fail intermittently with `retries` at 0, on a suite with no retries and no quarantine, so a red run means nothing until somebody re-runs it by hand.
cards.plain: Two of the automated checks fail at random and pass when run again. Nothing in the system tells the difference between one of those and a real breakage, so every red result now costs somebody a manual re-run before it can be believed.
cards.acceptance: THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE DELIVERABLE AND A GREEN RUN IS NOT ACCEPTANCE. `npx playwright test tests/e2e/client-detail.spec.ts tests/e2e/cross-links.spec.ts` is run TWENTY consecutive times against one persistent local stack, the pass and fail count of each run recorded in the pull request, and the pull request states the failure rate BEFORE the fix and AFTER it. A single green run proves nothing that can race, and the suite already runs green most of the time. PLUS the named cause: the pull request names the specific await, navigation or assertion that races, with the file and line, and says why it races. A fix with no named cause is a timeout that was raised. PLUS `retries` in playwright.config.ts:104 is STILL 0 at the end, or the pull request argues in terms why it should not be and the argument is a ruling rather than a config line: a retry turns this defect invisible instead of fixing it, and CLAUDE.md's evidence rule is what that would break. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
DO NOT FIX IT BY RAISING A TIMEOUT AND DO NOT FIX IT WITH `retries`. Both make the symptom go away and neither touches the race. `expect` already waits 10 seconds by default and both of these assertions were given explicit 15 and 20 second timeouts by whoever wrote them, which is the shape of a race that has already been papered over once.

THE SUITE IS SERIAL AND THAT NARROWS THE SEARCH. playwright.config.ts has `fullyParallel: false` and `workers: 1`, so this is not two specs colliding over shared database rows. It is a race INSIDE one page: a URL-driven panel that is asserted visible before the navigation that produces it has settled.

BOTH SPECS DRIVE A PANEL FROM THE URL, WHICH IS WHY THEY ARE THE TWO. Phase 3's density doctrine puts filters and tab state in the query string so a view can be linked and the back button works, so the assertion under suspicion is always the same shape: navigate, then assert a `data-testid` panel is visible. client-detail.spec.ts asserts `panel-<tab>` at lines 62 to 101; cross-links.spec.ts asserts `outbound-panel` at line 24 and `product-panel` at lines 143, 185.

IF TWENTY RUNS CANNOT REPRODUCE IT, SAY SO AND STOP. A card that cannot reproduce its own defect is blocked with the twenty run log attached, not closed as fixed.

cards.title: Sidebar navigation is measured before it is optimised: an authenticated render makes about 32 database round trips whatever the route, and that is the whole budget.
cards.plain: Moving between sections of the system feels slow. Before anything is changed, the delay has been measured: every page, even the simplest one, asks the database about thirty-two separate questions before it can be drawn. That fixed cost is the thing to fix.
cards.acceptance: THE FIRST CLAUSE IS REPRODUCTION AND IT COMES BEFORE ANY CHANGE. The 2 to 4 seconds the owner reports was NOT reproduced by the 2026-09-11 measurement on this machine, and a card that optimises something it cannot reproduce is guessing. The pull request states, with numbers, WHERE the owner's 2 to 4 seconds occurs: which build, which environment, which database. Until that is stated, nothing else in this acceptance may be claimed. THEN THE BUDGET. `select xact_commit+xact_rollback from pg_stat_database` is sampled either side of one authenticated page render, three samples per route, for all eleven sidebar routes, BEFORE and AFTER, and both tables are in the pull request. The AFTER figure for the fixed per-render cost is BELOW 12 round trips against a baseline of 32, and no route regresses. THEN THE USER-FACING NUMBER. Click-to-content is measured on the same eleven routes, cold and warm, in a PRODUCTION build, before and after, and the after figure is under 1000ms on every route in the environment where the 2 to 4 seconds was reproduced. PLUS `npx playwright test` exits 0 on the whole suite: this card may not trade correctness for latency, and the suite is what says so. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS if the fix changes any capability probe or session read, the pull request names every screen that could go blank if the probe is wrong, and a case asserts one of them does not.
