  CLICK TO CONTENT, production build, local database: 45ms to 113ms, because
    Next prefetches the RSC payload, so most clicks issue ZERO requests.
  DEV MODE, same machine: 63 to 241ms warm, 190 to 1061ms cold, and /inventar's
    FIRST compile was 33989ms of which only 707ms was server render.

THE FIXED 32 APPEARS ONLY WHEN AUTHENTICATED, which is what points at the cause: the session read, the profile and role lookup, the proxy, and the SIX schema-capability probes in lib/data/schema-capability.ts, each of which is its own PostgREST call with a 60 second cache that every new server instance starts cold.

ARITHMETIC THAT EXPLAINS THE OWNER'S NUMBER WITHOUT PROVING IT. On loopback a round trip is 1 to 3ms, so 32 of them is the measured 0.10 to 0.41s. Against a database in eu-west-1 at a 40ms round trip, 32 SEQUENTIAL round trips is 1.3 seconds and 65 is 2.6. That lands inside the owner's 2 to 4 seconds. IT IS A PROJECTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and the first acceptance clause exists because of that.

DO NOT ADD A CACHE AS THE FIRST MOVE. Thirty-two round trips for a page that displays almost nothing is a structure problem, and a cache in front of it hides the structure and expires at the worst moment. Reduce the count first; cache what is left if it is still slow.

DO NOT BREAK THE CAPABILITY PROBES. They exist because on 2026-08-31 every screen returned 500 when merged code read unapplied columns. lib/data/schema-capability.ts says so at length. A card that removes a probe to save a round trip has re-created INC-05.

EVERY SIDEBAR ROUTE IS `f` DYNAMIC, server-rendered on demand, confirmed from the build output. None is prerendered and none is cached. Whether any of them COULD be is a real question and it is inside this card.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-11 FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH, step 4: "MEASURE, DO NOT FIX." The measurement was taken and NOTHING was optimised, by instruction.

THE HEADLINE THE OWNER ASKED FOR, "where the time actually goes": on this machine, NOT where he sees it. A production build against a local database navigates in 45 to 113ms, nowhere near 2 to 4 seconds, and the click costs nothing at all on most routes because the payload was prefetched before the click. What IS wrong, and is wrong everywhere, is the fixed cost: about 32 database round trips per authenticated render, independent of what the page shows.

WHY THE OWNER'S ENVIRONMENT WAS NOT MEASURED IN THE FIRST PASS, AND THE CORRECTION. The original note read:

  "Both hosts this repository knows, www.rapidconstructmd.com and
   rc-inventory.vercel.app, answered 404 on /api/health and /autentificare on
   2026-09-11, which is consistent with ruling R-176. There is no deployed
   instance this session could reach, and signing in to one would need a
   production credential this session may not read."

IT IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, per CLAUDE.md section 9c, because the conclusion drawn from it is what would mislead the next session. THE FIRST SENTENCE IS TRUE AND THE SECOND IS FALSE. Those two hosts did answer 404. THERE IS A DEPLOYED INSTANCE: it is app.rapidconstruct.md, the owner named it the same day, and card GATE-07 repointed check:deployed-commit at it. A card that tells the next session the platform is unreachable is a card that stops them measuring, which is why this is corrected rather than left.

MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE HOST 2026-09-11, read-only, no credential, NO SIGN-IN. This is the number the first pass could not get:

  GET https://app.rapidconstruct.md/api/health      0.38 to 0.69s TTFB, ten samples
  GET https://app.rapidconstruct.md/autentificare   0.16 to 0.47s TTFB, five samples

THE DELTA IS ABOUT 0.25s, AND WHAT IT IS A DELTA OF MATTERS. /autentificare is a STATIC PRERENDER and touches no database. /api/health reads applied_ledger_version(), which is ONE database round trip. The client-to-edge leg is common to both, so it subtracts out, and what is left is roughly the cost of one round trip from the function to the database plus that endpoint's own work.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It confirms the DIRECTION of the local finding: a database round trip against the production database is expensive in a way it is not on loopback, where it was 1 to 3ms. IT DOES NOT LET ANYBODY MULTIPLY 32 BY 0.25 AND CALL IT THE ANSWER: 32 round trips inside one function invocation do not each pay a fresh connection, some may overlap, and the 0.25s figure includes whatever else /api/health does. THE AUTHENTICATED MEASUREMENT IS STILL OWED and it needs a credential this session may not read, which is why the first acceptance clause of this card is still reproduction.

THE MEASUREMENT TOOL IS NOT COMMITTED, deliberately. scripts/ is a CODE path under check-board-edit, so a tool there needs a card whose status moves, and this card is authored rather than worked. The NUMBERS are committed, here and in the session report, and the method is written out so it can be re-run: sample pg_stat_database either side of one authenticated request, and drive the sidebar with Playwright against a production build.

DEPENDS ON P3-44 FROM 2026-09-12, BY OWNER DISPATCH, step 5c: "P3-40 must reproduce before it optimises." The first acceptance clause of this card already said so and nothing made it a queue position. P3-44 is the reproduction as its own unit of work, and this edge is what stops this card being picked up by somebody who intends to optimise. Nothing else about this card changes; the 32 round trips and the committed baseline stand.

cards.title: Date fields in the manual intake form have no calendar picker, so a delivery date is typed blind into a text box.
cards.plain: When a delivery is entered by hand, the date has to be typed out rather than picked from a calendar. That is slow, and it is the easiest place in the system to record the wrong day without noticing.
cards.question:
ANSWERED 2026-09-13 BY PURPLE, in the factory mailbox answer q005: APPROVED, OPTION A. Keep the native date picker and show the chosen date written out in Romanian under both date fields on the manual intake form, so a day typed in the wrong order is visible before saving. Option B (replace the native control) and option C (close the card) were not chosen: B is a bigger job with more to get subtly wrong, and C leaves the wrong-day risk in place. THE QUESTION AS ASKED, kept verbatim below so the answer reads against it, from pull request #282:

DECISION NEEDED: what this card becomes, because its premise is false. Both date fields on the manual intake form already open a calendar picker.
CONTEXT: the title says a delivery date is typed blind into a text box. The form at /adauga-manual has rendered both of its date fields, Data comenzii and Livrare estimată, as a native `<input type="date">` since P2-04 on 2026-08-25, which is exactly the control this card's defaults say to start with. No style hides the calendar button. The acceptance's first clause therefore passes on today's code and cannot be proved to fail first, so building it would be a green test that proves nothing. Per the phase 3 doctrine, HALT ON A FALSE PREMISE, the card was stopped rather than reinterpreted. THE COMMAND OUTPUT THAT DISPROVES IT, 2026-09-13, on origin/main at 5080cdb:

  $ grep -n 'type="date"' components/orders/InboundOrderForm.tsx
  209:              type="date"
  217:              type="date"

  $ git log -S'type="date"' --format="%h %ad %s" --date=short -- components/orders/InboundOrderForm.tsx
  2536ead 2026-08-25 P2-04: real inbound orders, private document bucket, arrival creating batches

WHAT IS TRUE, AND IS THE RISK THE PLAIN LINE NAMES. The native control orders day and month by the BROWSER'S UI language, not by the page locale and not by lang="ro". Chromium, the suite's browser, page locale ro-RO, the same control, keystrokes 01122026, one launch per browser language:

  {"run":"default-browser-language","type":"date","hasShowPicker":true,"storedValue":"2026-01-12"}
  {"run":"browser-language-ro","type":"date","hasShowPicker":true,"storedValue":"2026-12-01"}

The default launch displayed 01/12/2026 and stored 12 January; the Romanian one displayed 01.12.2026 and stored 1 December. Nothing on the form spells out which day was chosen. The stored value itself is not shifted: the server action passes the YYYY-MM-DD string through and formatDate splits it without a timezone.
OPTIONS: (A) RE-SCOPE: keep the native picker and show the chosen date written out in Romanian beside every date field on the manual intake form, for example marți, 1 decembrie 2026, so a day typed in the wrong order is visible before saving; no dependency, nothing stored changes, and a red-first case exists. (B) Replace the native control with a Romanian-only zi.lună.an entry plus a picker button; fixed order everywhere, but more code and the typed path is easier to break. (C) Close the card as not needed and accept the browser-language behaviour.
RECOMMENDATION: (A). It addresses the wrong-day risk the owner described, stays inside the no-new-dependency and do-not-change-what-is-stored defaults, and its acceptance can be proved red first. The same native control is on the client, leads, project and extraction review forms; that is recorded in docs/LEARNINGS.md, not added to this card.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: this card stays blocked. Nothing depends on it and nothing on the live site changed.
cards.acceptance: RE-SCOPED 2026-09-13 ON PURPLE'S ANSWER TO q005, OPTION A; the original acceptance is quoted in notes. NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/inbound.spec.ts` exits 0 with a new case, proved to fail first, that (1) launches Chromium with its own language set to English, where the native date control reads month before day although the page locale is ro-RO, and asserts that divergence before anything else: the keystrokes 01122027 store 2027-01-12; (2) asserts that the Romanian written-out date under each of the two date fields, Data comenzii and Livrare estimată, is visible and reads exactly the day, month and year its field holds, and that each follows only its own field; (3) saves an order through the typed path and finds the stored delivery date on the order list equal to the written-out one; (4) asserts that an empty Data comenzii, before a date is chosen and after it is cleared, shows no written-out date at all. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS the pull request states in one line that no migration was added.
cards.defaults:
NO NEW THIRD-PARTY DEPENDENCY WITHOUT ASKING. A date picker is the classic reason to reach for a library, and adding one is a vendor decision under item 4 of the closed escalation list in DOCTRINE-TRIAGE section 6. START WITH `<input type="date">`, which every supported browser renders as a native picker, honours the locale, and costs nothing. If that is genuinely insufficient, BLOCK THE CARD and say why rather than installing something.

DESKTOP FIRST, like every screen on this board. The native control's mobile presentation is out of scope.

DO NOT CHANGE WHAT IS STORED. The column, its type and its timezone handling are untouched. This card changes how a value is ENTERED.

THE SCOPE IS THE MANUAL INTAKE FORM. If the same defect exists on other forms, that is a finding for docs/LEARNINGS.md or a second card, not a quiet widening of this one.

evidence.ref: Pull request #283, branch card/p3-41-romanian-date. RED BEFORE: quality run 34787496025 on e7508d4, the head carrying the new tests/e2e/inbound.spec.ts case alone with no application change, concluded failure at End to end only. Exactly one case failed, inbound.spec.ts:267, "fiecare câmp de dată arată în română ziua care se salvează", at :304 with getByTestId('order-expected-at-words') not found, AFTER the divergence assertion at :301 had passed in CI: the keystrokes 01122027 stored 2027-01-12 in an English-language Chromium with page locale ro-RO. 213 passed, cross-links.spec.ts and client-detail.spec.ts among them; every step in front of End to end passed and both applier proof steps were skipped, correctly, since no migration is added. GREEN AFTER: the quality run on the implementation head, whose id and result are recorded in the pull request, because writing them here would move the head away from the run that proved it.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-11 FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH, step 5a: "date fields in manual inventory intake have no calendar picker. Card it." Authored and not worked.

THE PREMISE WAS NOT VERIFIED AGAINST THE FORM IN THIS SESSION, and that is recorded rather than assumed. The dispatch states it as an observation. Whoever picks the card checks it first: if the fields already carry a picker, the card is CORRECTED rather than worked, per the halt-on-a-false-premise rule in the board doctrine.

CHECKED 2026-09-13 BY EXECUTOR AND THE PREMISE IS FALSE. Both date fields on /adauga-manual are native date pickers and have been since P2-04; the command output is in question. Moved todo to blocked on ivan under HALT ON A FALSE PREMISE, not worked and not reinterpreted. No application code, no test and no migration changed in the pull request that records this; it carries this board edit, one docs/LEARNINGS.md entry and the report docs/reports/2026-09-13-executor-p3-41-date-picker.md.

DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged per CLAUDE.md section 5: NO NEW THIRD-PARTY DEPENDENCY was honoured, none was installed or proposed as the recommendation. THE SCOPE IS THE MANUAL INTAKE FORM was honoured: the same native control on the client, leads, project and extraction review forms is a docs/LEARNINGS.md finding, not added here.

WHAT THE CHECK FOUND INSTEAD, and why the recommendation in question is a re-scope rather than a close: the native control orders day and month by the browser's own language. With Playwright's page locale at ro-RO and lang="ro", Chromium at its default language displayed 01/12/2026 for the keystrokes 01122026 and stored 2026-01-12; launched with --lang=ro-RO it displayed 01.12.2026 and stored 2026-12-01. The wrong-day risk in plain is real; its cause is not the one the title names.

RE-SCOPED 2026-09-13 AND WORK STARTED. PURPLE answered the question with option A (factory mailbox answer q005, recorded in question). Branch card/p3-41-romanian-date, cut from origin/main at eb7b34d; the branch card/p3-41 carried the false-premise record in pull request #282 and is merged and closed. Moved blocked to in_flight, blocked_on cleared. The acceptance was rewritten to the re-scoped one, because section 6 requires the acceptance run in the shipping pull request to be the one on the card. The title still states the original, disproved premise and is left as authored; question and the notes above say why it was false. THE ORIGINAL ACCEPTANCE, quoted:

NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/inbound.spec.ts` exits 0 with a new case, proved to fail first, asserting that EVERY date input on the manual intake form opens a date picker and that a date chosen from it reaches the stored row unchanged. THE CASE ENUMERATES THE FIELDS RATHER THAN CHECKING ONE: it reads every date-shaped field on the form and asserts each one, so a field added later without a picker fails this case rather than passing it silently. PLUS THE TYPED PATH STILL WORKS, and this is the half that will be forgotten: an operator who types a valid date into the field still gets that date stored. A picker that makes keyboard entry impossible is slower for the person who can already touch-type a date. PLUS THE ROMANIAN FORMAT IS WHAT IS DISPLAYED, with the locale the rest of the application uses, and the case asserts the rendered text rather than the input's value attribute. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS the pull request states in one line whether any migration was added.

RED ARM 2026-09-13. The new case in tests/e2e/inbound.spec.ts is pushed alone, with no application change, so its quality run must fail on the missing written-out date and on nothing else. The card reads shipped on this head only so the board-edit check lets the end to end suite run; the same shape P3-46 used on pull request #280.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-13 AFTER THE RED ARM, run 34787496025, failed on the missing written-out date and on nothing else. lib/data/format.ts gains formatDateWords, which turns the field's YYYY-MM-DD string into a Romanian date with weekday and month names, for example marți, 12 ianuarie 2027, and returns an empty string for an empty field or a day that does not exist. components/orders/InboundOrderForm.tsx renders it under Data comenzii and Livrare estimată, live, and renders nothing for an empty field.

DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged per CLAUDE.md section 5: NO NEW THIRD-PARTY DEPENDENCY, none added, the spelling is Intl.DateTimeFormat. DO NOT CHANGE WHAT IS STORED, honoured, the display reads the field's string and writes nothing back; no migration. DESKTOP FIRST, honoured. THE SCOPE IS THE MANUAL INTAKE FORM, honoured: the client, leads, project and extraction review forms are untouched and stay a docs/LEARNINGS.md finding.

DECISIONS TAKEN WITHOUT ASKING: (1) locale ro-MD, the one lib/data/format.ts already uses for numbers; for a written-out date it prints the same text as ro-RO, with comma-below letters, checked in Node and in Chromium. (2) The date is built and formatted in UTC, so no local timezone can move the day. (3) The upload screen renders the same InboundOrderForm in manual mode, so the written-out date appears there too. It is the same form by design (the component's header says two copies would diverge), not a second form, so it was not gated off. (4) Nothing is rendered, not an empty line, when a field is empty, so the optional field never shows a date that was not chosen.

cards.title: The stock reminder threshold is reachable from the row that shows it, instead of only from the product sheet in Inventar.
cards.plain: The reminder threshold for a product can only be changed by opening that product in the catalogue. Somebody looking at the reminders list, which is where they notice the threshold is wrong, has no way to get to it from there.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/reminders.spec.ts` exits 0 with a new case, proved to fail first, that starts on the reminders screen and CHANGES A THRESHOLD, reading the new value back from the stored row rather than from the form. PLUS THE EXISTING SURFACE IS UNTOUCHED AND A CASE SAYS SO: the product sheet in Inventar still edits the same field, still stores the same value, and its shipped case still passes. This card adds a way IN, it does not move the capability. PLUS ONE WRITE PATH, ASSERTED: whichever shape is built, the threshold is written by the SAME server action the product sheet uses. A second action that writes the same column is the defect this acceptance exists to refuse, and the pull request names the single function by path. PLUS PERMISSIONS ARE NOT WIDENED: whoever could not change a threshold before still cannot, asserted with the account that lacks the right. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS the pull request states in one line whether any migration was added.
cards.defaults:
DO NOT BUILD A SECOND CONFIGURATION SURFACE. The owner's instruction, in terms. A settings screen, a bulk-threshold editor, or a second form that owns the same field is out of scope and is refused by the acceptance clause about one write path.

TWO SHAPES ARE ACCEPTABLE AND EITHER SATISFIES THIS CARD: inline edit on the reminders row, or a direct link from the row to the product sheet's threshold field. PREFER THE LINK IF INLINE EDIT WOULD NEED A NEW SERVER ACTION. A link is a href and cannot drift from the sheet; an inline editor that grows its own write path is the second surface this card forbids.

RECORD THAT THE CAPABILITY ALREADY EXISTS, explicitly, in the pull request and in this card's evidence. The owner asked for that in terms. This card is about REACHABILITY, not about a missing feature, and a report that describes it as new would be false.

DENSITY DOCTRINE STILL BINDS. The reminders list paginates and stays a list. An inline editor that expands a row into a form is a drill-in, and the board's density rules govern it.

evidence.ref: Pull request #284, branch card/p3-42. THE CAPABILITY ALREADY EXISTED: the threshold was editable before this card, from the product sheet in Inventar, and this card adds only a way to reach it from the reminders row. The single write function is updateProduct in lib/data/product-actions.ts, used by both ways. No migration. RED BEFORE: quality run 34791543786 on ffe15ac, the head carrying the four new tests/e2e/reminders.spec.ts cases alone with no application change, concluded failure at End to end only. Exactly two cases failed, both at reminders.spec.ts:291 waiting for getByTestId('threshold-edit-link'): :314 "pornind din memento, pragul se schimbă și se citește din rândul stocat", after its stored-row read of the starting threshold had passed, and :354 "amândouă drumurile scriu pragul prin aceeași acțiune de server", after its save from the product sheet and stored-row read had passed. 216 passed, among them :342 the product sheet case and :374 the account manager case, every existing reminders case, and products.spec.ts, dashboard.spec.ts and cross-links.spec.ts. Every step in front of End to end passed and both applier proof steps were skipped, correctly, since no migration is added. FIRST IMPLEMENTATION HEAD: quality run 34793382768 on a53c91b, 217 passed and 1 failed, :354 at :371, because the test captured the panel's loadProductDetail request instead of the save; the run's trace shows both saves under one action id. The test now selects the save by its body. GREEN AFTER: the quality run on the repaired head, whose id and result are recorded in the pull request, because writing them here would move the head away from the run that proved it.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-11 FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH, step 5b: "Memento stoc threshold is editable only on the product sheet in Inventar. Card inline edit or a direct link from the row. Do NOT build a second configuration surface, and record that the capability exists."

THE CAPABILITY EXISTS. This is recorded at authoring time because the owner asked for it and because a card titled as though the feature were missing would send somebody to build one. The threshold is already editable; what is missing is a way to reach it from the screen where its wrongness is visible.

THE PREMISE WAS NOT VERIFIED AGAINST THE SCREENS IN THIS SESSION. Whoever picks the card checks first which surfaces write that column and names them, and corrects the card rather than working it if the answer differs.

IN FLIGHT 2026-09-13, EXECUTOR, branch card/p3-42, cut from origin/main at 64f4529.

THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE BEFORE ANY WORK, as the note above asks, and it holds. WHAT WRITES products.threshold, every path, measured with grep over app, components, lib, scripts and supabase/migrations: (1) updateProduct in lib/data/product-actions.ts, called only by components/inventory/ProductForm.tsx, the product sheet in Inventar, and the ONLY path that changes the threshold of an existing product; (2) createProduct in the same file, the same form in add mode, which sets it once at creation; (3) the extraction review confirm in lib/data/extraction-actions.ts, which inserts a new flagged product with threshold 0 and never edits one; (4) the test seed scripts under scripts/, which are not a screen. Migration 0001 declares the column, numeric(14,3) not null default 0, check threshold >= 0. The reminders screen app/(app)/memento/page.tsx reads the threshold and writes nothing, and its card header says in terms that the threshold is edited in the product sheet, from Inventar. So the capability exists and is reachable from one screen only. The card is worked as authored, not corrected.

WHO MAY CHANGE IT TODAY: only the owner role. updateProduct returns the Romanian owner-only refusal for any other role, migration 0001's row level security refuses the write underneath it, and the Inventar screen renders no edit button for any other role. /memento itself is NOT owner-only (lib/routes.ts lists only /setari), so the account manager can open it, and that is the account the permissions clause is asserted with.

RED ARM 2026-09-13. Four cases added to tests/e2e/reminders.spec.ts, pushed alone with no application change: (1) from the reminders row, change the threshold and read it back from the stored products row through PostgREST; (2) the product sheet in Inventar still edits the same field and stores it; (3) both ways write through the same server action, asserted by the Next-Action header on the save request, whose id names one server function; (4) the account manager has no edit link on the reminders row and the link's address typed by hand opens the read-only panel, not the form, and the stored threshold is unchanged. Expected on this head: (1) and (3) fail on the missing threshold-edit-link, (2) and (4) pass, since they guard what must not change.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-13 AFTER THE RED ARM, run 34791543786, which failed on the missing threshold-edit-link and on nothing else. THE SHAPE IS THE LINK, NOT AN INLINE EDIT. updateProduct takes the whole product, so an inline editor on the row would have needed a new server action writing only the threshold, which the one-write-path clause refuses, or a row resubmitting every product field, which is a second form in disguise. app/(app)/memento/page.tsx: for the owner only, the threshold on each row is a RecordLink to /inventar?produs=<sku>&camp=prag, and the card header hint says to click it; other roles see the value and the old hint. components/inventory/InventoryScreen.tsx: camp=prag with produs= opens the existing ProductForm in edit mode directly, for the owner only; without the right to write the same address opens the read-only panel, as produs= alone has since P3-10. components/inventory/ProductForm.tsx: an optional focusField puts the threshold input in focus and selects it; the input gains name="threshold" so the form can find it. Nothing about what is saved changes.

DEFAULTS APPLIED, logged per CLAUDE.md section 5: DO NOT BUILD A SECOND CONFIGURATION SURFACE, honoured, no settings screen, no bulk editor, no second form. PREFER THE LINK IF INLINE EDIT WOULD NEED A NEW SERVER ACTION, applied, for the reason above. RECORD THAT THE CAPABILITY ALREADY EXISTS, recorded in the pull request, in evidence and here. DENSITY DOCTRINE STILL BINDS, honoured, no drill-in added to the list.

FINDING, NOT FIXED HERE: the reminders list does not paginate. This card's defaults say "The reminders list paginates and stays a list" and the board doctrine says a list paginates at 25, but app/(app)/memento/page.tsx renders every active product in one table, and the fired-alerts table the same. It belongs to the density sweep and was not widened into this card.

REPAIR ATTEMPT 1 OF 3, CLAUDE.md section 10, 2026-09-13. The first implementation head, a53c91b, ran quality 34793382768: End to end failed, 1 failed and 217 passed. Cases 1, 2 and 4 passed, so the link and the stored-row read work. Case 3 failed at reminders.spec.ts:371: the product sheet path captured Next-Action 40232ba7... and the reminders path 60f32376.... DIAGNOSED FROM THE RUN'S OWN TRACE, not guessed: on the product sheet path two 40232ba7... POSTs, the panel's loadProductDetail from lib/data/product-detail.ts, went out after the capture began and the save followed as 60f32376...; on the reminders path the save alone, 60f32376.... Both saves used the same action; the helper took the first header it saw. The id's first byte agrees: 40 marks a one-argument action and 60 a two-argument one, and updateProduct takes two. FIX: saveThreshold selects the POST whose body carries "threshold":"<the value just typed>". The equality assertion is unchanged, so a second action writing the column still fails the case. Recorded in docs/LEARNINGS.md.

cards.title: A client carries one of five ordered lifecycle stages, Lead rece to Client, with a follow-up date required at De reluat and every stage change recorded with who and when. Existing clients become Client.
cards.plain: Each customer record gets a stage showing how far along the relationship is: a cold lead, one being worked, one to chase on a set date, one that has been quoted, or a real client. A lead marked to chase cannot be saved without the date to chase it on, every change of stage is remembered with who made it and when, and every customer already in the system is marked as a client.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/clients.spec.ts` exits 0 with new cases, proved to fail first. Each clause names the line of the acceptance list in the owner's handover, Part 4.8, that it proves. (1) THE FIELD, FIVE STAGES, DECLARED ORDER: a client's stage is set from the existing client form and read back from the stored row, and the stages are exactly the tokens `cold`, `nurture`, `follow_up`, `quoted`, `client`, in that order, rendered on screen as `Lead rece`, `În cultivare`, `De reluat`, `Ofertat`, `Client`, each with its colour (red, blue, amber, purple, green) shown BESIDE the label and never instead of it, and the raw token is never visible. (2) THE ORDER IS PART OF THE DATA, NOT OF THE SCREEN: the stages sort in the declared order and NOT alphabetically. The alphabetical order of the tokens and of the Romanian labels both differ from the declared order, and the case asserts against that difference. (3) HANDOFF 4.8 LINE 4, DE RELUAT NEEDS A DATE: saving a client at `follow_up` with no follow-up date is rejected with a Romanian message visible on screen and the stored row is unchanged, AND the database refuses the same write on its own with a check constraint (SQLSTATE 23514), so a path that skips the form cannot store that state either. Saving at `follow_up` WITH a date succeeds and the date reads back unchanged. (4) HANDOFF 4.8 LINE 9, EVERY CHANGE IS RECORDED: a stage change writes exactly one history row carrying the client id, the previous stage, the new stage, the acting user's id and a timestamp, read back from the stored history rather than from the screen. cards.title: Two new error codes, each with its own Romanian sentence and its own instruction, and a check that refuses two codes sharing one sentence.
cards.plain: When the system refuses a document it has to say why in a way the person reading the screen can act on. Two new reasons are added, every existing reason is given an instruction of its own, and a check makes sure no two reasons ever end up telling somebody the same thing.
cards.question: DECISION NEEDED, AND THE CARD DOES NOT WAIT ON IT. The dispatch of 2026-09-12 orders five codes: `document_too_large`, `download_failed`, and `expired_token`, `invalid_token`, `object_not_found` "if absent from the enum". MEASURED AT 404c5ab: all five are absent from `public.extraction_error_code`, whose eight labels are `download_failed`, `url_expired`, `unsupported_format`, `unreadable_document`, `extraction_failed`, `invalid_output`, `timeout`, `reconciliation_failed`. `download_failed` IS ALREADY THERE, so it is not a new code and the card treats it as a copy defect instead. THE OTHER THREE ARE THE QUESTION. They are the failure codes of OUR OWN download route at `app/api/documents/[...path]/route.ts`, where they live as `EXPIRED_TOKEN`, `INVALID_TOKEN` and `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` in a DIFFERENT namespace: the route's JSON `code`, paired with an HTTP status, read by the extractor at download time. Two of the three already have a meaning inside the extraction enum: `url_expired` says the signed link expired, which is what `EXPIRED_TOKEN` reports, and `download_failed` covers a download that did not produce a document, which is where `INVALID_TOKEN` lands today. `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` has no equivalent. BOTH READINGS ARE REAL. Adding them lets the extractor relay our route's code verbatim instead of translating it, and a translation is a place where two sides can disagree. Not adding them keeps one meaning per value and avoids two codes that an operator cannot tell apart on a screen. THE CARD DOES NOT DECIDE THIS. It ships `document_too_large` and the copy work, which need no ruling, and it carries the three-code question to the owner unchanged.
cards.acceptance: FOUR CLAUSES AND THE FOURTH IS THE CONTROL. ONE, THE NEW CODE: `document_too_large` is added to `public.extraction_error_code` in a migration of its own that contains the `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS` and nothing else, for the reason migration 0034's header gives: a newly added enum label cannot be used in the transaction that added it, and `supabase db reset` wraps each FILE in one transaction. It is added to `EXTRACTION_ERROR_CODES` in `lib/data/extraction-types.ts` in the same pull request. TWO, ONE SENTENCE PER CODE AND ONE INSTRUCTION PER SENTENCE: every label in `EXTRACTION_ERROR_LABEL` names what happened and what the reader is to do next, in Romanian with diacritics, and `download_failed`'s sentence gains the instruction it does not have today. THREE, NO TWO CODES ON ONE SENTENCE: a new check, run in `quality`, refuses the label map when any two codes share a sentence or share an instruction clause. FOUR, THE CHECK IS SHOWN FAILING, per ruling R-193: at least four mutants, each a one-value edit to the label map, each proved to make the check exit non-zero, in the pattern `npm run prove:*` already uses. PLUS `npm run check:migrations` exits 0. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS `npx playwright test tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0 with a case asserting the new code's sentence reaches the screen through `data-testid="draft-error-sentence"`.

`document_too_large` IS OURS TO EMIT, NOT HIS. It joins the third surface R-098 declared, the same surface `reconciliation_failed` opened: a payload or an upload that OUR side refuses, where the download succeeded and nothing failed at his end. STARTING TEXT FOR THE TWO SENTENCES THAT CHANGE, AS A PROPOSAL AND NOT AS A CONSTRAINT. `document_too_large`: "Documentul are prea multe pagini pentru serviciul de extragere. Împarte-l în părți mai mici și încarcă-le pe rând." `download_failed`, which today says what happened and gives no instruction: "Documentul nu a putut fi descărcat de serviciul de extragere. cards.title: We count the pages ourselves at upload, from bytes we already hold and with no new dependency, and one count feeds three consumers that today have none.
cards.plain: When somebody uploads a supplier document, the system will count its pages before sending it anywhere. That one number lets us refuse a document too big to read before we pay to send it, lets the reading service refuse it before downloading it, and tells the person keying a failed scan by hand whether they are looking at the whole document or at the first page of four.
cards.acceptance: THE CAPABILITY FIRST, THEN THE THREE CONSUMERS, THEN THE CONTROL. CLAUSE 0, THE COUNTER: a server-side page counter with NO new dependency, unit-tested against the two committed fixtures in `tests/fixtures/` and against at least one PDF whose objects are inside compressed object streams, which is the case a plain text scan of the bytes cannot answer. It returns an integer or null, never a guess, and null is not an error. A non-PDF upload, which for this application means PNG or JPG, counts as one page. CLAUSE 0b, THE STORE: the count is written to a column of its OWN on `extraction_drafts`, in its own migration, and it does NOT write `page_count`, whose comment in migration 0032 says in terms that the column holds the count AS THE MODEL REPORTS IT. Two facts, two columns, and comparing them is what the whole signal is for. It must be stored rather than recomputed because `refireExtraction` in `lib/data/extraction-actions.ts` reads only the draft row and never holds the file bytes. CLAUSE 1, THE COUNTERPARTY CAN REJECT BEFORE DOWNLOADING: the outbound webhook body carries the count. `lib/data/extraction-fire.ts` states today that the body carries EXACTLY six fields, per contract section 3, so section 3 is edited in the same pull request and its stated field count moves with it. CLAUSE 2, OUR OWN REJECTION IS THE CHEAP ONE: an upload whose count is 100 or more is refused BEFORE `fireExtraction` is called, stored `failed` with `document_too_large`, and the operator sees that code's sentence on the screen. A null count does NOT refuse: an unknown page count is not a large document. CLAUSE 3, THE HEADER-ONLY FAILED SHAPE CARRIES IT: the count reaches the review screen on the one payload shape that has no `_meta` and therefore no page count today, which is the half of card EXT-24 that closed unanswered. CLAUSE 4, THE CONTROL, per ruling R-193: the 100-page refusal is shown REFUSING, not only passing, by a case that drives a document over the threshold through the upload path and asserts the stored code, and the counter is shown returning null rather than a wrong integer on a file it cannot read. PLUS `npm run check:migrations` exits 0. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts tests/e2e/review.spec.ts` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE COUNT IS POSSIBLE AT UPLOAD AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The upload path `startExtraction` in `lib/data/extraction-actions.ts` is a server action. It already holds the uploaded `File`, reads `file.size` and `file.type` from it, and hands the whole object to Supabase Storage, so the bytes are in the server's hands before `fireExtraction` is called. Nothing has to be downloaded back to count.

NO NEW DEPENDENCY, AND THAT IS ALSO MEASURED. The premise recorded in card EXT-24's option C, that counting our own pages "needs a PDF library this repository does not have", is FALSE about what is needed. A PDF page count is the `/Count` on the page-tree root, and on a modern file that object lives inside a FlateDecode object stream, which Node's built-in `zlib` inflates with no package at all. Measured on 2026-09-12 against 1535 real PDF files: 1526 counted correctly against `pdfinfo` as ground truth, 2 returned no answer, 7 were wrong. The full method and the seven failures are in this card's report. The build starts from that measurement rather than from zero.

THE SEVEN FAILURES ARE ALL UNDERCOUNTS AND THE CAUSE IS KNOWN. The probe took the LARGEST `/Count` it could see, which on a file with a nested page tree is a subtree rather than the root. Resolving the trailer's `/Root` to its `/Pages` object and reading THAT `/Count` is the fix and is what the card builds. The probe is not the deliverable; its numbers are the floor, not the target.

A WRONG COUNT IS WORSE THAN NO COUNT, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS. An undercount under-refuses at clause 2, which is safe, and produces a false alarm when compared against the model's own report, which is not. Any reading the counter is not sure of is null.

100 IS THE COUNTERPARTY'S CAP AND OURS IS THE SAME NUMBER ON PURPOSE. The dispatch of 2026-09-12: "their cap stays as backstop, ours is the cheap check". Ours is cheap because it costs one inflate of bytes already in memory; theirs costs a signed URL, a download and a model call. A card that makes the two numbers disagree has invented a product decision.

CLAUSE 1 IS A CONTRACT CHANGE THAT REACHES ANDRE AND THIS CARD DOES NOT SEND IT. The outbound body is frozen at six fields by contract section 3. A seventh field arriving at a scenario that does not expect it is his problem before it is ours. The pull request drafts the sentence he needs; the owner sends it, item 6 of the closed escalation list.

IF CLAUSE 1 CANNOT LAND WITHOUT HIM, CLAUSES 0, 0b, 2 AND 3 STILL SHIP. They are entirely ours: a column, a counter, a refusal and a screen. Splitting is allowed and the split is stated in the pull request; abandoning the other three because one needs a counterparty is not.

cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-12 FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH, step 2: "page count, one capability, three consumers", with the three named as (a) emitted in the webhook so the counterparty can reject before downloading, (b) our own rejection at 100 pages before the webhook fires with `document_too_large`, and (c) the page count in the header-only failed shape. The dispatch made (a) and (b) CONDITIONAL: "if step 0 finds we cannot count at upload, card only c and state plainly in the card that a and b are not possible, with the reason."

STEP 0 FOUND THAT WE CAN, SO ALL THREE ARE CARDED. Two findings settle it, both from source and from measurement rather than from documentation.

THE BYTES ARE THERE. `startExtraction` receives the `File` from the form, checks `file.size` against `MAX_DOC_BYTES` and passes the object itself to Storage. It is a server action, so this is server-side already; nothing new is exposed to a browser.

THE LIBRARY IS NOT NEEDED. The 1535-file measurement is in the report and its headline is 1526 correct, 2 no answer, 7 wrong, using nothing but `node:zlib` and a regular expression, at an average of 0.2ms per file over 423 MB. This CORRECTS the premise recorded in card EXT-24's question field, which ruled option C out on the grounds that it "needs a PDF library this repository does not have, which is a vendor decision under item 4 of the closed escalation list". That sentence is kept where it is, per CLAUDE.md section 9c; what is false about it is the necessity, not the caution.

THIS CARD CLOSES THE HALF OF EXT-24 THAT ITS OWN RULING LEFT OPEN. EXT-24 closed on 2026-09-11 by ruling R-191, which answered the field-count question and said in terms that the page-count question was not answered. EXT-24's notes then record: "NO CARD IS AUTHORED FOR THE REMAINDER, because the dispatch that ordered this closure authored three cards by name and none of them is this one." This is that card.

WHY A SECOND COLUMN RATHER THAN WRITING `page_count`. Migration 0032's column comment is explicit: the value is "Pages in the source document AS THE MODEL REPORTS THEM, not as counted by us", and it names the comparison as separate work that "needs a page counter on our side that does not exist yet". Writing our count into that column would destroy the only pair of numbers the signal is made of, and it would do it silently, because afterwards the two would be indistinguishable.

DEPENDS ON EXT-27 FOR ONE REASON ONLY: clause 2 stores `document_too_large`, and until that label exists on `public.extraction_error_code` the write is refused by the database.

cards.title: The 3,500,000 byte threshold is implemented exactly as dictated, read from the declared size and never from the downloaded file, and the card records that its origin is unknown.
cards.plain: Documents above a set file size are handled differently. That size was given to us as a number and nobody can say where it came from, so it is written down once, in one place, with a plain note that it is not a reasoned figure and that anyone who wants to change it is changing a number, not a conclusion.
cards.acceptance: THE NUMBER IS MATCHED EXACTLY AND THE MATCH IS PROVED AT THE BOUNDARY. ONE, THE VALUE: 3500000, decimal, as a named constant in one file, with no arithmetic expression producing it and no second copy anywhere. It is NOT 3.5 times 1024 times 1024, and a test asserts the constant equals 3500000 so that a later rewrite into binary units is a red run rather than a quiet drift of 170,016 bytes. TWO, THE COMPARISON: strictly less than passes. 3499999 passes, 3500000 does NOT pass, 3500001 does not pass. Three cases, at those three values, not near them. THREE, THE INPUT: the threshold is read from the DECLARED `size_bytes`, the value already on the draft row and already sent in the webhook body, and never from the bytes of a downloaded file. A case asserts that nothing on this path performs a download. FOUR, THE RECORD: the constant's own comment says, in the file, that its origin is unknown, that the base64 inflation reconstruction is unproven, and that it is not load-bearing. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. PLUS the pull request quotes the three boundary assertions and their result.
cards.defaults:
ITS ORIGIN IS UNKNOWN AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A DISCLAIMER. Searched at 404c5ab on 2026-09-12: the strings 3500000, 3_500_000 and 3,500,000 appear in no file in this repository, and `git log -S` over all branches returns no commit that ever added or removed any of them. The number entered this project in the owner dispatch of 2026-09-12 and nowhere else.

THE BASE64 RECONSTRUCTION IS UNPROVEN AND IS NAMED ANYWAY. The reading that 3,500,000 bytes is what survives some other limit after base64 inflates a payload by four thirds is a reconstruction somebody could offer; nothing in this repository tests it, and no limit it would be derived from is written down here. It is recorded as a guess so that the next reader does not have to re-derive it and mistake their own derivation for the record.

IT IS NOT LOAD-BEARING AND NO FUTURE CARD MAY CITE IT AS REASONED. This is the whole point of the card. A number with no derivation becomes a number with a derivation the moment somebody writes "per the 3.5 MB limit" in a second place. The comment is the thing that stops that, and it is part of the acceptance for exactly that reason.

STRICTLY LESS THAN, AND THE EXACT VALUE FAILS. The dispatch says "strictly less than passes". A threshold whose boundary case is decided by whoever wrote the comparison is a threshold with two behaviours, and the three-value test is what pins it.

DECLARED, NOT MEASURED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A DOWNLOAD. `size_bytes` is on the draft row from the moment of upload and travels in the webhook body. Reading the real length of the stored object would mean fetching it, which costs a signed URL and a round trip to answer a question the row already answers.

WHAT THE THRESHOLD DOES IS NOT IN THIS CARD. The dispatch gave the number, the comparison and the input, and did not say what happens on either side of it. The card implements the predicate and its constant. A card that invents a behaviour for it has invented a product decision, which CLAUDE.md section 4 forbids, and it is better to have a correct unused predicate than a wrong used one.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-12 FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH, step 3: "byte threshold 3,500,000, decimal, strictly less than passes, read from the declared size_bytes and not the downloaded file. Match it exactly. Record in the card that its origin is unknown, that the base64 inflation reconstruction is unproven, and that it is not load-bearing. No future card may cite it as reasoned."

THE ONLY THING THE CARD ADDS TO THE DISPATCH IS THE SEARCH THAT CONFIRMS THE ORIGIN CLAIM. The dispatch asserted the origin is unknown; step 0 checked rather than transcribed, and the assertion holds: no occurrence in the tree and no occurrence in any commit on any branch.

THE ONE THING THE CARD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO is decide what happens above the threshold. Nothing in the dispatch says, and the neighbouring work gives two plausible answers that are not the same: card EXT-28 refuses an upload at 100 pages, and the existing upload path refuses at `MAX_DOC_BYTES`, which is 10 MB. A third size threshold that silently acquires one of those behaviours would be the kind of number that becomes reasoned by being used.

THE NUMBER IS NOT `MAX_DOC_BYTES` AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. `MAX_DOC_BYTES` is 10 times 1024 times 1024, is enforced on the upload form, and has a user-facing Romanian sentence that says 10 MB. Two thresholds, two purposes, and collapsing them would change a shipped refusal on the strength of a number nobody can source.

cards.title: The document link the counterparty receives is our route on the host that actually serves this application, and the three failure codes are handed to him as three test links he can run against.
cards.plain: The reading service downloads each supplier document through a link we issue. That link must point at the address where our system actually lives, not at the old marketing domain and not straight at the storage provider, and the other side needs three working test links so they can see for themselves what an expired, broken or missing document looks like before it happens for real.
cards.acceptance: THREE CLAUSES, AND THE FIRST ONE IS THE DEFECT. ONE, THE ORIGIN: the `document_url` sent in the webhook body resolves to our own route on `app.rapidconstruct.md`. Not a Supabase Storage URL, not `www.rapidconstructmd.com`. The fallback origin in `lib/data/extraction-fire.ts`, today the literal `https://www.rapidconstructmd.com`, is corrected, and a case asserts the fallback path produces an origin that the deployed-commit guard's own host constant agrees with, so the two cannot drift apart again. TWO, THE CONTRACT HOLDS ON THE LIVE HOST: a read-only probe of the route on `app.rapidconstruct.md` records, in the pull request, the status, content-type and JSON `code` for each failure the probe can reach without a credential, and shows none of them is `text/html`. THREE, THE TEST LINKS: three links are produced, one per code, `EXPIRED_TOKEN`, `INVALID_TOKEN` and `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, issued through the SAME route and the same origin the real `document_url` uses, so the counterparty exercises the path he will actually be given rather than a stand-in. The links go in the pull request for the owner to hand over. NO TOKEN VALUE, NO SIGNED URL AND NO CREDENTIAL IS PRINTED IN THIS REPOSITORY: the pull request states how each link is produced and the owner produces and sends them, per CLAUDE.md section 7. PLUS `npm run check:document-url` exits 0. PLUS `npx playwright test tests/e2e/document-url.spec.ts` exits 0. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
cards.defaults:
THE ROUTE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY CORRECT ABOUT THE THREE CODES. `app/api/documents/[...path]/route.ts`, shipped by card EXT-08, answers `EXPIRED_TOKEN` with 400, `INVALID_TOKEN` with 401, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` with 404 and never returns `text/html` on any failure path, and `proxy.ts` carries the public-path exception that keeps a failure from becoming a login page. Measured live on 2026-09-12: a request with no token returns 401 and `{"code":"INVALID_TOKEN"}` as `application/json`, and a POST returns 405 `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`. THIS CARD DOES NOT REBUILD ANY OF THAT.

THE DEFECT IS THE ORIGIN, AND IT IS ONE LINE. `siteOrigin()` in `lib/data/extraction-fire.ts` falls back to `https://www.rapidconstructmd.com` when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is empty or absent. That host answered 404 with a GitHub Pages error page on 2026-09-12, measured, and card GATE-07 already moved the deployed-commit guard off it for the same reason. Whether production is today running on the fallback cannot be read from outside and this card does not guess: it removes the fallback's ability to be wrong.

`callbackUrl()` READS THE SAME FUNCTION and therefore carries the same fallback. If `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is ever absent in production, the address Make is told to post its result back to is also the dead host. The card fixes the function, so both consumers are fixed, and the pull request says so rather than leaving the second one to be rediscovered.

NO DNS AND NO DOMAIN WORK. The dispatch of 2026-09-12 excludes the .com domain and any DNS change in terms. This card changes a string in this repository and nothing outside it.

THE TTL IS NOT TOUCHED. Fifteen minutes in production, twenty-four hours on the sample script, exactly as ruling R-096 left them and as ruling R-194 and the dispatch of 2026-09-12 both confirm. A test link that expires is produced by waiting or by a sample path, never by lengthening a TTL.

THE THIRD LINK IS THE HARD ONE AND THE CARD SAYS SO UP FRONT. `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` needs a VALID signature over a path that holds no object, which means signing, which means a credential this repository may not read. The mechanism is written in the pull request and the owner runs it. If that turns out to be impossible without a credential read, the card ships two links and states plainly which one it could not produce and why, rather than substituting a link that returns a different code.

cards.title: The counterparty has no way to report a concern about a payload he considers extracted, because the contract answers 400 before the payload is stored.
cards.plain: When the reading service is confident it read a document but is uneasy about part of it, it has nowhere to say so. The system refuses the whole message and stores nothing, so the doubt never reaches the person checking the document on screen.
cards.question: DECISION NEEDED BEFORE THE SHAPE IS CHOSEN, AND THE OPTIONS HAVE DIFFERENT BLAST RADII. The gap is measured and is not in dispute: a payload with `status: "extracted"` and any `error_code` is refused 400 at `app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts`, before storage, and migration 0008's `extraction_drafts_error_code_matches_status` enforces the same disjointness in the database. A. RELAX THE RULE: allow an `error_code` on `extracted`. Smallest edit in our code and the largest change to the meaning of the pair, because every consumer that reads `error_code` as "this failed" is now wrong. It also needs a database migration to drop and recreate the check constraint, and it reopens what ruling R-190 deliberately left closed. B. A SEPARATE CONCERN FIELD: a nullable `concern` or `concern_code` that is valid on any status and is never the reason a payload is refused. The status pair keeps its meaning, the screen gains a place to show doubt, and it is a new field in the contract, which reaches Andre. C. USE `reason`, WHICH IS ALREADY OPEN. Measured: `reason` is stored on every status, including `extracted`, and the review screen already renders it. It carries no code, so nothing can branch on it and no count can be taken of it. Costs nothing and buys only a sentence. NO RECOMMENDATION IS OFFERED. Which of the three is right depends on whether a concern should be something the system ACTS on or something a person READS, and that is a product decision, not a terminal's.
cards.acceptance: THE CARD IS NOT BUILT UNTIL THE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND WHAT IT SHIPS IS FIXED IN ADVANCE FOR EACH ANSWER. UNDER ANY ANSWER: a case proves the gap FIRST, against the current tree, by sending `status: "extracted"` with an `error_code` and asserting 400 and that NOTHING was stored for that `order_id`, with the failing output quoted in the pull request, per ruling R-193. UNDER A: the check constraint is replaced by a migration that drops and adds it by name, the route stops refusing, and every reader of `error_code` in the application is enumerated in the pull request with a line saying whether it still reads correctly. UNDER B: the field is added to contract section 4.1 and to the database in the same pull request, is nullable with no default, is never a reason to refuse a payload, and reaches the review screen with its own Romanian sentence carrying its own instruction, under card EXT-27's rule. UNDER C: no schema change and no contract change; the review screen makes `reason` legible on an `extracted` draft, which today renders as an unlabelled muted line beneath the filename, and a case asserts it appears. IN ALL CASES: the message Andre needs is DRAFTED in the pull request and NOT sent, and `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx playwright test tests/e2e/extraction.spec.ts` both exit 0.
cards.defaults:
THE GAP IS REAL AND IT IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THREE PLACES. Ruling R-190 names it: "Andre has no way to report a concern on a payload he considers extracted, because the contract forbids an error_code there. It is refused with a 400 before it is stored, not overwritten." Ruling R-193 repeats it as the defect underneath its third instance. The route's own comment says it in terms: letting him send an `error_code` on an `extracted` payload "is a contract change that reaches him, and it is item 6 of the closed escalation list. R-190 names the hole and deliberately does not close it here." This card is the closing, and it starts from those sentences rather than rediscovering them.

MAKE DOES NOT RETRY A 4xx, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT A SMALL BUG. A payload refused 400 is dropped once and quietly. If Andre ships a concern field before we accept it, every document carrying one is lost, and the loss looks like nothing at all from his side.

THE FREE TEXT CHANNEL IS ALREADY OPEN AND ALREADY RENDERED, AND THAT IS MEASURED. `reason` is read from the payload with no validation and written on every status, and `components/orders/ExtractionReviewPanel.tsx` renders `draft.reason` in the draft list independently of `draft.errorCode`. So the true statement is narrower than "he cannot report a concern": he cannot report one A MACHINE CAN READ. The card must not be written as though there were no channel at all.

NO OPTION IS TAKEN BY A TERMINAL. CLAUDE.md section 4: never guess a product decision. The question field carries three options, their costs and no recommendation, and the card waits.

DO NOT SEND ANYTHING TO ANDRE. Every one of the three options except C changes what he sends or what we accept. The pull request drafts the text; the owner sends it, item 6 of the closed escalation list.
cards.notes:
AUTHORED 2026-09-12 FROM AN OWNER DISPATCH, step 5a: "the extracted-payload concern gap: the counterparty cannot report a concern on a payload it considers extracted, we answer 400 before storage."

THE DISPATCH'S SENTENCE IS TRUE ABOUT THE SHIPPED CODE AND STEP 0 CONFIRMED IT AT 404c5ab, line by line. `if (status === "extracted" && errorCodeRaw !== null)` returns `CALLBACK_CODES.rejected`, which is 400, and it returns before the first write. The database agrees independently: 0008's check constraint permits `error_code` only when the status is `failed` or `partial`.

ONE NUANCE THE DISPATCH DOES NOT CARRY, AND IT CHANGES OPTION C FROM NOTHING INTO SOMETHING. `reason` is accepted, stored and displayed on an `extracted` payload today. It is free text with no code, so nothing branches on it and nothing counts it, but it is not true that the channel is closed. It is true that the MACHINE-READABLE channel is closed.

STATUS IS `todo` RATHER THAN `blocked`, DELIBERATELY. Clause one of the acceptance, the failing case that proves the gap, needs no answer from anybody and is the evidence the question itself deserves. A card that sits `blocked` while its own premise is unproved is a card that asks the owner to rule on a terminal's reading of a route.

THIS CARD IS WHY RULING R-193's THIRD INSTANCE MATTERED. The instance as the owner wrote it was the inverse of what the code does, and naming the premise correctly is what surfaced this. Ruling R-195 replaces that instance with a true one and keeps both readings of the original in place, per CLAUDE.md section 9c.

The pull request states whether the 32 round trips traverse THAT leg at all, with evidence, because card P3-40's committed measurement says they are function-to-database and that the client-to-edge leg subtracts out. cards.title: A Romanian file picker replaces the browser's own Choose File button everywhere a file is attached, and the date fields read zz.ll.aaaa, day first, whatever language the browser is set to.
cards.plain: Where someone attaches a document, the button and the empty message are in English today, and on a computer set to English the date fields ask for the month before the day, which is how a delivery gets saved on the wrong day. After this the file button and message are in Romanian, and dates are always entered day, month, year.
cards.question:
DECISION NEEDED: replace the browser's own date field with a Romanian day.month.year field plus a calendar button, which an earlier answer declined, or keep the browser's field.
CONTEXT: On 2026-09-13 PURPLE's answer to q005 (card P3-41) kept the browser's own date field and added the date written out in Romanian beneath it (its option A), and declined its option B, a Romanian-only day.month.year entry plus a calendar button, as a bigger job that is easier to get subtly wrong. The owner-requested review of 2026-09-14, finding F4, now asks for option B in substance: date fields whose placeholder and order read zz.ll.aaaa, with P3-41's written-out date kept. The browser's own field cannot be made to read day first on a browser set to English; only a replacement can. The file picker half of this card does not depend on this answer.
OPTIONS: (1) Replace all eight date fields with one shared Romanian field: typed as zz.ll.aaaa, stored as yyyy-mm-dd as today, a calendar button that opens the browser's own calendar, and P3-41's written-out date kept beneath. Always day first on every computer; one new shared component used by five forms, so more to test. (2) Keep the browser's field as q005 decided, do only the file picker, and extend P3-41's written-out date to every date field so a month-first entry is visible before saving. Smaller, but a browser set to English still shows mm/dd/yyyy, which the review asks to remove.
RECOMMENDATION: (1). It is what the owner's review asks for, it removes the wrong-day risk at its source instead of displaying it, and it keeps both the calendar and the written-out date, so nothing q005 protected is lost.
IMPACT IF UNANSWERED: nothing waits before P3-15 ships, because this card depends on it. If still unanswered when this card is picked, the executor builds option (1) and records that in notes.

The price comes from the supplier's price list that was checked by hand, and it can still be changed before saving.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/roofing-product-prices.spec.ts` exits 0. roofing-product-prices.spec.ts is a NEW file with three cases, every expected price written by hand from the verified CSV and not read from the database: (1) on the new product form, picking a combination through Model, Serie and Grosime fills Valoare unitară (MDL) with the exact pret_lei of that combination's line: C-10 Standart Zn 0,45 mm 144, C-10 Standart Zn 0,45 mm Cr matt 134, PS-8 Standart Zn 0,45 mm W 164, VP-20 Econom 0,30 mm 82 and PK/PS-20 Econom 0,30 mm 82 (one shared price line), Dastera Standart Zn 0,45 mm Cr matt 137, H-57 Zinc (România/Turcia) 0,70 mm 253; a product saved with the prefilled price left as it is stores unit_value_mdl 144; (2) the prefilled price is overwritten with 150,50 before saving, and the saved product stores unit_value_mdl 150.5, not the prefill; (3) public.sheet_prices holds exactly 194 rows, their prices sum to 26832, and every one of the 225 sheet_options rows finds its price by price_group, series, thickness_mm and finish. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` exit 0. PLUS `npm run check:no-destructive-migration` exits 0 on the new migration, and on the pull request the quality steps that refuse a row-removing migration, prove the migration applier and prove every applier assertion can fail all RAN and passed. PLUS the pull request names the migration file by path, says in one plain sentence what changes in the live database, and states that the merge is pre-approved by Max ("prices go, merge when green").
cards.defaults:
SOURCE: the operator factory's GOALS.md, goal G13d, owner (Max), 2026-09-15, and the factory task that drafts it; merge pre-approved by Max in the factory's mailbox answer q031b ("prices go, merge when green"), POC merges on green. The only source of prices is the factory file inputs/dasterum-pret-2026-08-07-verificat.csv (194 data lines, sheet Verificare, checked by Max 2026-09-15). The xlsx Import sheet is stale and is never read, nor the PDF price list or the owner's photo.

THE FIX (quoted from the task, dashes replaced by commas per CLAUDE.md 11): "Database change, additive only, DATA not schema-only (no DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, DELETE, or UPDATE of any existing row) ... G13d's own GOALS.md text is explicit that this must be INSERT only, no UPDATE of existing rows, so adding a column to the existing table and filling it via UPDATE is NOT allowed. Instead: create a new table, for example public.sheet_prices (price_group text not null, series text not null, thickness_mm numeric(3,2) not null, finish text not null default '', price_lei numeric not null check (price_lei > 0), primary key (price_group, series, thickness_mm, finish)), matching sheet_options's own check-constraint style (trimmed, non-empty text; finish defaulted to '' the same way). Grant select to authenticated the same way sheet_options does; revoke all from anon and authenticated first." "Load exactly 194 rows via insert into public.sheet_prices (...) values (...) statements generated from the CSV, one row per CSV data line, mapping model (CSV) to price_group, serie to series, grosime_mm to thickness_mm, finisaj to finish (empty string where the CSV cell is empty), pret_lei to price_lei. Idempotent: guard the insert so re-running the migration does not duplicate rows." "Assertion that the loaded count equals the CSV line count: a query in the migration itself ... confirming select count(*) from public.sheet_prices equals 194 after the migration runs." "Wire the picker to use it: wherever G13c's model/series/thickness picker currently leaves the price (unitValueMdl) for the operator to fill by hand, look up sheet_prices by the chosen combination's price_group (read off the matching sheet_options row), series, thickness_mm, finish, and prefill the price field with the match if one exists. The operator can still edit the prefilled price before saving (this is a suggestion, not a lock)." "Column probe: add one to lib/data/schema-capability.ts for the new table's existence, following the exact shape of the existing has* probes, and use it so the prefill degrades silently (no prefill, no crash) until the migration is actually applied on the live database." "Migration file number: the next free number after the highest file already in supabase/migrations/."

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE (quoted from the task): "sheet_options itself: no new columns, no rows added or changed there. This card only adds a new table and reads the existing one." "Do NOT create 194 catalog products. This is reference price data only." No unrelated refactor of ProductForm.tsx or product-actions.ts; the extraction paths are not touched.

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each checked against the tree:
(a) THE KEY IS (price_group, series, thickness_mm, finish) AND THERE IS NO FOREIGN KEY. price_group is not unique in sheet_options (the shared line "PK/PS-20, VP-20" names 40 rows), so no key there can be referenced. Instead the migration asserts, in the same transaction, that the two tables name exactly the same 194 price lines, both ways, and fails the file otherwise.
(b) price_lei IS numeric(14,2), the type of products.unit_value_mdl, which is the field the suggestion fills; lei and MDL are one currency. The task's check (price_lei > 0) is kept.
(c) RE-RUNNABLE, in the house pattern of 0029 and 0031: create table if not exists, the select policy created only when it is missing, and insert ... on conflict (price_group, series, thickness_mm, finish) do nothing. A second run adds no row, and the count of 194 holds on every run.
(d) THE JOIN RUNS ON THE SERVER, in the list the product form already loads: each combination carries the price of its line, and price_group never reaches the browser. Picking the thickness fills Valoare unitară (MDL); a short Romanian note under the field says it is the Dasterum price of 07.08.2026 while the field still holds it. createProduct and updateProduct are unchanged: the server saves whatever the field holds, so an overwritten price is saved as typed.
(e) hasSheetPrices probes public.sheet_prices. Until the migration is applied, combinations carry no price and the form behaves exactly as P3-57 left it.
(f) THE CSV WAS CROSS-CHECKED BY SCRIPT BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN: 194 data lines, 194 distinct (model, serie, grosime_mm, finisaj) lines, identical both ways to the 194 (price_group, series, thickness_mm, finish) lines of migration 0046; "PK/PS-20, VP-20" is 20 CSV lines, each matching two sheet_options rows. The CSV starts with a byte order mark, stripped before the header is read.

evidence.ref: Pull request #306, branch card/p3-58. MIGRATION supabase/migrations/0047_sheet_prices.sql: public.sheet_prices holding the 194 prices of the Dasterum list of 07.08.2026 as verified by Max on 2026-09-15, keyed on (price_group, series, thickness_mm, finish), select for authenticated and no write grant, with a DO block that fails the file unless the table holds 194 rows summing to 26832 lei and names the same 194 price lines as sheet_options in both directions. INSERT only: no DROP, TRUNCATE, DELETE or UPDATE anywhere in it, sheet_options and products untouched, and no catalogue product created. ASSERTIONS scripts/poc-free/local-db/assertions/0047_sheet_prices.sql: shape, eight prices written by hand from the verified CSV, the 225 combinations all finding their price, the refusals (a price of zero, untrimmed text, an empty series, a second price for one line), a re-run adding nothing, and who may read or write. APPLY LOG pending line 0047_sheet_prices.sql, card de aplicare P3-58. ACCEPTANCE tests/e2e/roofing-product-prices.spec.ts, the three cases of the card. CODE hasSheetPrices in lib/data/schema-capability.ts gates the read; listSheetOptions joins each combination to its price line on the server, so price_group never reaches the browser; picking the thickness fills Valoare unitara (MDL) and a Romanian note names the source while the field still holds that value; createProduct and updateProduct are unchanged, so a price typed over the suggestion is saved as typed. LOCAL: npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build exit 0, check:no-destructive-migration exit 0 on the new file, and every other close-out check exit 0. GREEN: the quality run on the head sha, with the migration steps RUN, is recorded in the pull request and in the owner question, because writing its id here would move the head sha. MERGE HELD FOR OWNER APPROVAL (pre-approved by Max, "prices go, merge when green", POC merges): real client data is in production and merging applies 0047 to the live database (CLAUDE.md 8.0). Report docs/reports/2026-09-15-executor-g13d-load-dasterum-prices.md.

AUTHORED 2026-09-15 by AUTHOR, from the operator factory's task for goal G13d. The same session builds it as EXECUTOR, in the same pull request, as that task asks. Depends on P3-57 because it reads public.sheet_options and fills the form P3-57 built; P3-57 is shipped.

cards.title: Modifică produsul shows the Model, Serie and Grosime lists for an existing product, prefilled from its saved combination, changeable and clearable back to Fără model; updateProduct validates and writes the four sheet columns the way createProduct does, and editing any other field leaves the combination as it is.
cards.plain: An operator can now change the model, series and thickness of a roofing sheet or metal tile product after it has been created, or remove that choice, instead of only being able to set it when the product is first added. Changing anything else on the product, such as its name or price, leaves the chosen model, series and thickness as they were.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/product-sheet-edit.spec.ts` exits 0. product-sheet-edit.spec.ts is a NEW file with four cases, every expected value written by hand from the verified list and read back from the row with the local service_role key: (1) a product created through Model, Serie and Grosime (C-10, Standart Zn, 0,45 mm) opened with Modifică shows the three lists, and they hold C-10, Standart Zn and 0,45 mm; (2) on that form the thickness is changed to 0,40 mm of the same series, which suggests that line's price 126 in Valoare unitară (MDL) as on create, and saved, the row stores sheet_thickness_mm 0.40 with model C-10, series Standart Zn and finish empty, and the form reopened shows 0,40 mm; (3) the model is set back to Fără model and saved, the row stores sheet_model, sheet_series, sheet_thickness_mm and sheet_finish all null, and the form reopened shows Fără model with Serie and Grosime disabled; (4) on a product holding a combination, only the name and the unit value are changed and saved, the row stores the new name and price and the combination unchanged. PLUS the P3-57 spec tests/e2e/roofing-product-picker.spec.ts still exits 0, with its edit step now expecting the prefilled lists instead of their absence. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` exit 0. PLUS no file under supabase/migrations/ is added or changed, and the pull request says so in one line.
cards.defaults:
SOURCE: the operator factory's GOALS.md, goal G20, owner (Max), reported live on 2026-09-16: "la un produs deja existent nu pot sa editez Model / Serie / Grosime". POC reproduced it: components/inventory/ProductForm.tsx sets sheetActive = !editing && sheetOptions.length > 0.

THE FIX (quoted from the task, dashes replaced by commas per CLAUDE.md 11): "Show the same three lists (model, series, thickness/finish) when editing is true, exactly as they render when adding, prefilled from the product's saved sheet_model / sheet_series / sheet_thickness_mm / sheet_finish (once those columns reach the form via the query change above). The operator can change them, or clear back to \"Fără model\" (however that state is represented in the add flow today, reuse it, do not invent a second \"no selection\" state)." "lib/data/product-actions.ts's updateProduct gains the same two calls createProduct already makes (validateSheet(input) then sheetColumns(supabase, sheet.value)), and merges sheetCols.value into its update(...) call, mirroring createProduct exactly." "Name, unit, category, supplier and price stay editable and are NOT silently overwritten unless the operator actively picks a new combination. Do not auto-refill those fields on every render just because the saved sheet values are now visible; only the P3-58 prefill behavior (a chosen combination suggesting its price) should still apply when the operator picks a NEW combination, exactly as it already does on create." "Keep the products_sheet_complete constraint satisfied: all four columns null, or all four present. validateSheet already enforces this; do not weaken that check." "No new migration expected. The four columns already exist (migration 0046). If you find you actually need a migration, stop and say so in your report rather than writing one silently."

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE (quoted from the task): "The behavior on CREATE (adding a new product): unchanged." "products_sheet_option_fk / products_sheet_complete: unchanged, still enforced." "The unit-lock logic already in updateProduct (a product with batches/order lines/outbound lines cannot change its unit): unchanged, keep it working alongside the new sheet-column update." The extraction paths are not touched.

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each checked against the tree:
(a) THE TASK'S PREMISE ABOUT sheetColumns IS CORRECTED, NOT FOLLOWED BLINDLY. The task says sheetColumns maps no model into the four columns set to null. It does not: for null it returns an empty object, which writes nothing. On create that is the same thing, on update it would leave a cleared combination in place. updateProduct therefore writes the four columns as null explicitly when the operator chose Fără model, and only while hasSheetOptions says the columns exist.
(b) A FORM THAT DID NOT SHOW THE LISTS SENDS NO COMBINATION AT ALL, and updateProduct then leaves the four columns untouched. That is the case when the list of combinations is empty (not readable, or 0046 absent). Sending null there would clear a saved combination the operator never saw, which is exactly the silent loss validateSheet's own comment warns about.
(c) THE SAVED COMBINATION REACHES THE FORM THROUGH listProducts, as one field sheet on CatalogProduct, null for an ordinary product, selected only when hasSheetOptions says the columns exist, the same gate the probe already uses on those four columns. No new probe is added: hasSheetOptions already probes exactly products.sheet_model, sheet_series, sheet_thickness_mm and sheet_finish.
(d) THE PREFILL IS INITIAL STATE, NOT AN EFFECT. Opening the form sets the three lists and nothing else; name, unit, category, supplier and unit value keep the product's saved values. Only choosing a thickness runs the P3-57 and P3-58 fill, as on create.
(e) P3-57'S OWN SPEC ASSERTED THE DEFECT. roofing-product-picker.spec.ts case 1 expected the lists to be absent on the edit form. That one expectation is changed to the prefilled lists; nothing else in that spec changes, and a test that encodes a bug is fixed by fixing the bug.

evidence.ref: Pull request #308, branch card/p3-59. NO MIGRATION: no file under supabase/migrations/ added or changed. ACCEPTANCE tests/e2e/product-sheet-edit.spec.ts, the four cases of the card, plus tests/e2e/roofing-product-picker.spec.ts with its edit step now expecting the prefilled lists. CODE: ProductForm shows Model, Serie and Grosime on edit, seeded from the saved combination as initial state only; listProducts selects sheet_model, sheet_series, sheet_thickness_mm and sheet_finish behind hasSheetOptions; updateProduct runs validateSheet and sheetUpdateColumns, which checks a chosen combination through sheetColumns, writes four nulls for Fara model, and writes nothing when the form did not show the lists. LOCAL: npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build exit 0, every close-out check exit 0. GREEN: the quality run on the head sha is recorded in the pull request and in the owner question, because writing its id here would move the head sha. MERGE HELD FOR OWNER APPROVAL: real client data is in production. Report docs/reports/2026-09-16-executor-g20-edit-sheet-existing-product.md.
