cards.title: The app shell works on a phone: under 768 px the sidebar becomes a drawer opened from a button in the top bar, the top bar and the sign-in screen fit 390 px with no sideways scroll, and the root layout exports a device-width viewport. Desktop unchanged.
cards.plain: The sign-in screen and the app's menu and top bar now fit and work on a phone screen: the menu tucks away behind a button and slides out when tapped. Nothing changes in how they look or work on a computer.
cards.acceptance: NAMED TEST: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/phone-shell.spec.ts` exits 0. phone-shell.spec.ts is a NEW file run at a 390x844 viewport: (1) on /autentificare, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= document.documentElement.clientWidth`, every visible interactive element (input, button, link) is at least 44 px tall, and every text input computes a font size of at least 16 px; (2) signed in as the owner on the dashboard (/) at 390x844, the sidebar (`aside`) is not visible, a drawer-open button in the top bar is visible, at least 44 px tall and reachable by keyboard, and clicking it shows the sidebar with the same links `aside nav a` lists at desktop width, every link inside the viewport horizontally, the page still not scrolling sideways, and the drawer closes again from its close control and from Escape; (3) the top bar (`header`) at 390 px has no horizontal overflow (its scrollWidth <= clientWidth, every child inside the viewport) and every visible button in it is at least 44 px tall. (4) Desktop unchanged: `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts tests/e2e/crm-landing.spec.ts tests/e2e/button-contrast.spec.ts tests/e2e/favicon.spec.ts tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts tests/e2e/support/auth.ts` exits 0, and those specs pass unchanged in the same run. PLUS `app/layout.tsx` exports `viewport` with `width: "device-width"` and `initialScale: 1` (`grep -n "export const viewport" app/layout.tsx` exits 0). PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` exit 0. PLUS a screenshot at 390x844 of the drawer closed and open, referenced in the report, and one line stating no migration was added.
cards.defaults:
THIS IS G23 PART 1 FROM THE FACTORY GOALS (the shell: sign-in, sidebar, top bar), asked by the owner on 2026-09-16: "also queue the mobile version, like configure the settings so it opens from the phone normal", then "include blue as well for these fixes, we need em ASAP". CLAUDE.md section 11 says desktop-first unless a card says otherwise; THIS CARD SAYS OTHERWISE, for the shell only. The lists, the panels and forms, and the remaining screens are parts 2 to 4 and are separate cards.

THE FIX, quoted from the task: "Target: 390px wide (iPhone) and up. No horizontal scrolling anywhere in these files' screens, no text or button cut off, tap targets at least 44px, form inputs at least 16px. The sidebar becomes a drawer behind a button on narrow screens (under 768px), exactly as G23 states. Above 768px, nothing about the sidebar's current behavior changes. Romanian unchanged, no wording changes, no behaviour changes: layout only. Do not rename, retranslate, or restructure what these screens say or do, only how they lay out at narrow widths. Desktop layout does not change at all. Every existing desktop Playwright spec covering sign-in, the sidebar or the top bar must keep passing unmodified."

ACCEPTANCE, quoted from the task: "A named end to end spec, new file, run at a 390x844 viewport, asserting: 1. On the sign-in screen: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= document.documentElement.clientWidth (no horizontal scroll), every interactive element at least 44px tall, every text input at least 16px font size. 2. On any authenticated screen (pick one, for example the dashboard) at 390x844: the sidebar is NOT visible by default, a drawer-open button is visible and reachable, and clicking it reveals the sidebar's contents (its own links, not cut off, not causing a sideways scroll) the same as they exist today. 3. The top bar itself has no horizontal scroll and no cut-off content at 390px wide. 4. Every existing desktop-viewport spec that touches sign-in, the sidebar or the top bar still passes UNCHANGED."

FILES: app/layout.tsx (only a new `viewport` export), app/autentificare/page.tsx, components/auth/LoginForm.tsx, components/layout/Sidebar.tsx, components/layout/Topbar.tsx. The drawer's open state is shared between Sidebar and Topbar without a new provider in app/(app)/layout.tsx where possible. `.rc-shell { min-width: 1100px }` in app/globals.css forces the whole shell to 1100 px and makes a phone scroll sideways whatever the sidebar does; default: scope that one rule to 768 px and wider, which leaves every desktop width exactly as it is. NEVER TOUCH components/inventory/ProductForm.tsx or anything the price-management goal adds (the other lane's files), or app/api/extraction/**, app/api/documents/**, lib/data/extraction*, docs/contracts/extraction*.

THE TWO SELECTORS EXISTING SPECS READ, KEEP THEM TRUE: crm-landing.spec.ts reads the top bar title as `header span:first`, so the new menu button carries no span before the title; it reads the sidebar links as `aside nav a`, so there is still exactly one `aside` with one `nav`, and any new close control sits outside that `nav`. New control labels are Romanian with diacritics (for example Deschide meniul, Închide meniul). No migration.

evidence.ref: Branch card/p3-60, cut from origin/main at 1a240b5, code commit 096ada3; pull request to be opened by the POC task that picks up this Lane B branch. SPEC tests/e2e/phone-shell.spec.ts, new, three cases at 390x844: (1) sign-in fits, controls 44 px, inputs 16 px; (2) signed in on /, the aside is hidden, the top bar menu button (44 px, reachable by Tab) opens a drawer with the same `aside nav a` labels and hrefs as at 1440x900, no sideways scroll, closes from its X, Escape and navigation; (3) the top bar fits 390 px on / and on /necesar. CASE 1 RAN LOCALLY WITH THE REAL CONFIG AND PASSED (1 passed); cases 2 and 3 sign in and need the local Supabase stack, which this machine lacks, so they run in CI on the pull request; their measurements ran locally on a never-committed harness page with the shell's exact markup, 34 of 35 checks passed and the one miss was the harness address, not the code. DESKTOP UNCHANGED: screenshots of the shell and sign-in at 1440, 1100 and 800 px from origin/main's files and from this branch are byte-identical (sha256), and `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts tests/e2e/crm-landing.spec.ts tests/e2e/button-contrast.spec.ts tests/e2e/favicon.spec.ts tests/e2e/headers.spec.ts tests/e2e/support/auth.ts` exits 0. `grep -n "export const viewport" app/layout.tsx` exit 0, `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0, `npm run build` exit 0, full local gate set exit 0. No migration added. Screenshots at 390x844 and the full report: docs/reports/2026-09-16-executor-g23-phone-shell.md.

cards.plain: The series and thickness fields on the roofing product picker now say why they cannot be clicked yet, and look greyed out until the field above them is chosen, instead of looking broken.

SOURCE: the operator factory's task for goal G21, owner (Max), reported live on 2026-09-16: "cand incerc sa selectez dintre serie si grosime apas si nu se intampla nimic". POC checked the code: Serie is disabled until Model is set and Grosime is disabled until Serie is set, which works by design, but nothing on screen says the field is locked or why, so it reads as broken.

THE FIX (quoted from the task, dashes replaced by commas per CLAUDE.md 11): "Keep the order (model before series before thickness): this is not a request to remove the lock, only to explain it." "A short Romanian hint under each locked field, using Field's existing hint prop: Serie's Field: hint=\"Alege întâi modelul\" while !sheetModel, otherwise no hint override needed (falls back to Field's own (opțional) default, or omit hint entirely once unlocked, match whatever the surrounding fields already do when not showing a special hint, so the picker doesn't suddenly look inconsistent). Grosime's Field: hint=\"Alege întâi seria\" while !sheetSeries, same fallback behavior once unlocked. The hint text disappears (or reverts to the field's normal state) as soon as the field above it is chosen." "A visibly disabled style on the two selects while locked: add disabled-state classes directly to these two <Select> elements' className (via the existing fieldClass(\"sheet\") helper or a small addition alongside it), for example disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:bg-rc-line (match whatever token names this repo's app/globals.css actually defines; do not invent a new color token for this). Scope this to the sheet-picker selects only: do not change the shared CONTROL constant or Select component itself, since that would restyle every disabled select in the app."

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE (quoted from the task): "The lock order or logic itself (still model, then series, then thickness)." "The shared CONTROL class, the Select component, or Field's own definition: reuse what exists, do not modify their shared shape." "Any other field's disabled styling: scoped to the two sheet-picker selects only." The extraction paths are not touched. No database change.

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each checked against the tree:
(a) THE TASK'S PREMISE ABOUT Field IS CORRECTED, NOT FOLLOWED BLINDLY. The task says the picker sits inside Field from components/ui/primitives.tsx, which has a hint prop and prints (opțional) when none is given. It does not: ProductForm.tsx declares its own private Field at the bottom of the file, label and children only, no hint and no (opțional), and every field on the form uses that one. Switching Serie and Grosime to the shared Field would print (opțional) beside them and not beside Model, and drop the private Field's bottom margin, which is exactly the inconsistency the task warns against. So the private Field gains an optional hint prop that renders the SAME line as the shared one (block text-[12px] text-rc-muted mt-1), and the shared Field is not touched. Once unlocked the hint prop is omitted, so Serie and Grosime look exactly like Model.
(b) THE DISABLED CLASSES ARE disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:bg-rc-line, the task's own example. rc-line exists in app/globals.css as --color-rc-line, so no new token is invented.
(c) THE CLASSES LIVE IN ONE CONSTANT beside fieldClass in ProductForm and are joined with fieldClass("sheet") on Serie and Grosime only. Model is never disabled and does not receive them.
(d) THE HINT ALSO SHOWS ON THE EDIT FORM of a product with no combination, because P3-59 renders the same picker there; that is the same lock and the same explanation.

evidence.ref: The pull request from branch card/p3-61 (gh pr list --head card/p3-61 --state all). NO MIGRATION: no file under supabase/migrations/ added or changed, and components/ui/primitives.tsx unchanged. ACCEPTANCE tests/e2e/product-sheet-locked-hint.spec.ts, the five cases of the card, plus tests/e2e/roofing-product-picker.spec.ts, tests/e2e/roofing-product-prices.spec.ts and tests/e2e/product-sheet-edit.spec.ts unchanged. CODE: ProductForm shows Alege întâi modelul under Serie while no model is chosen and Alege întâi seria under Grosime while no series is chosen, through an optional hint on its private Field, and both selects carry disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:bg-rc-line. LOCAL: npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build exit 0, every close-out check exit 0, the built CSS proven on a copy of the markup to give opacity 0.5 and cursor not-allowed. GREEN: the quality run on the head sha is recorded in the pull request and in the owner question, because writing its id here would move the head sha. MERGE HELD FOR OWNER APPROVAL: real client data is in production. Report docs/reports/2026-09-16-executor-g21-locked-sheet-fields-hint.md.

FILES: components/inventory/InventoryScreen.tsx, components/clients/ClientsScreen.tsx, components/projects/ProjectsScreen.tsx, components/orders/OrdersScreen.tsx, and nothing else in the application. NEVER TOUCH components/inventory/ProductForm.tsx, anything the price-management goal adds, components/ui/primitives.tsx, app/(app)/layout.tsx, or app/api/extraction/**, app/api/documents/**, lib/data/extraction*, docs/contracts/extraction*.

HOW, default: ONE DOM, restyled under 768 px with max-md classes only, never a second copy of the rows. Every existing spec counts rows by data-testid (product-row, client-row, project-row, inbound-item, outbound-item); a hidden duplicate list would double every count at desktop. Column labels in a row card come from a data-label attribute on each cell, drawn by CSS, carrying the header text the table already shows, so no cell's text content changes. GOALS.md marks the merge NOT PRE-APPROVED (it carries a migration and it changes who may write price data); the pull request is left open for the owner.

THE FIX (quoted from the task, dashes replaced by commas per CLAUDE.md 11): "Who: owner only, the same gate as the rest of the admin surface (is_owner()). RLS write policies (insert, update) for the owner on both sheet_options and sheet_prices; read stays authenticated, matching what 0046 and 0047 already set up. No write access for anyone else. What the screen does: Lists the combinations grouped by model and series (reuse the visual style of the existing Inventar screens, Romanian, desktop-first, the shared Table/Card/Button primitives). Add a combination: model, serie, grosime, finisaj, unitate, grup de preț (price_group), validate the same way sheet_options's own CHECK constraints do (trimmed, non-empty text; finish empty string when none; thickness_mm > 0), and enforce the primary key's uniqueness with a clear Romanian message on a duplicate, not a raw Postgres error. Edit its price in lei: writes to sheet_prices, matched by (price_group, series, thickness_mm, finish). Retire one: it stops being offered on the product form's Model/Serie/Grosime picker, but is NOT deleted. NOTHING IS DELETED. Add a nullable retired_at timestamptz (or is_active boolean not null default true, pick whichever reads cleaner given the existing style of this codebase's similar soft-deactivate columns, e.g. products.active) to sheet_options, and filter retired rows out of the product form's picker query. Products already pointing at a retired combination keep working: products_sheet_option_fk stays satisfied because the row still exists, just marked retired. A migration that DELETEs or DROPs any of this is refused by doctrine and by the pre-merge check."

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each within the fix above:
(a) retired_at timestamptz null, NOT an active boolean. check:pending-schema-reads searches every source file for a new column name as a whole word, and migration 0046's decision 4 already names that trap: active is an ordinary word across this codebase. retired_at is not, and it also records when.

SOURCE: the operator factory's GOALS.md, goal G28, Ivan's finding F3, quoted: "silent upload failure when MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL is missing: a visible Romanian error on the upload screen and a named test". Confirmed by POC and again by this session reading the code: fireExtraction's missing-URL branch returned BEFORE the extraction_drafts upsert, so no row existed for that order, and both callers mark a failure with `.update(...).eq("order_id", ...)`, which matches zero rows and cannot say so. The Orange-path ban is LIFTED for the cards of findings F2, F3 and F5 to F9 (Ivan, 2026-09-17), with app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts FROZEN by ruling R-202. The merge is NOT pre-approved: real client data is in production.

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each within the task:
(a) THE LABEL IS `config_error` AND NOT `webhook_not_configured`. It means "a setting of ours is missing or wrong, and no document was sent because of it". The narrow name would have needed a second and a third label the first time a sibling variable was given the same treatment; the row's `reason` carries the specific variable, the label carries the class.
(b) THE LABEL IS KEPT OUT OF `EXTRACTION_ERROR_CODES`, AND THIS IS THE DECISION THE WHOLE CARD TURNS ON. That array is contract section 5.2's closed set and it is what the FROZEN callback route tests a payload against through isExtractionErrorCode. Adding the label there would have turned a callback carrying it from a 400 into an accepted payload, which is exactly what R-202 forbids. A second set, LOCAL_ERROR_CODES, holds the codes we write ourselves and never speak on the wire; StoredErrorCode is the union, and it is what a draft row and the screen's label map are typed against. The route is not edited and its behaviour is unchanged, and a case in the named spec proves that rather than promising it.
(c) THE ROW IS WRITTEN INSIDE fireExtraction, NOT AT THE CALLERS, for the reason its own header already gives about the 100-page refusal: three callers call it, and a rule placed at one caller guards one caller. uploadOrderDocument discards the result by design, so a fix that lived at the callers would not have reached it at all.
(d) ONE UPSERT, ALREADY FAILED, not an upsert followed by an update. The page-count refusal needs two writes because the row must exist before the count is judged; here nothing is judged, so the row is written once, complete.
(e) THE CODE IS GATED BY hasConfigErrorCode, like every label before it, because until 0051 is applied the database answers 22P02. WHAT THE GATE FALLS BACK TO IS DIFFERENT FROM document_too_large's, deliberately: there, an unknown label means the refusal does not happen at all. Here the variable really is missing and the document really cannot go, so in that two-minute window the same row and the same Romanian reason are written under `download_failed`, which is already what both callers write for any failure without a code of its own. A more general code beats silence.
(f) THE SPEC NEEDS A THIRD SERVER, started with MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL empty, and a Playwright project of its own, because webhookUrl() reads the process environment on every request: the answer is a property of the server, not of the test, and the branch under test is the one where no fetch is made, so there is nothing a mock could stand in for. Same shape and same reasoning as the existing 'productie' project. Dev mode, not a production build: nothing here turns on a production build, and a second `npm run build` would cost CI minutes for nothing.
(g) THE SIBLING CONFIG REFUSALS ARE LEFT ALONE. A missing NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL and a missing MAKE_WEBHOOK_SECRET already write a row, because they sit after the upsert, and their callers already surface them as `download_failed`. Giving them `config_error` would be more accurate and is scope this card was not given; it is reported, not done.
(h) 0042's ASSERTION FILE IS NARROWED IN THE SAME PULL REQUEST to stop pinning the whole enum set, exactly as 0042 narrowed 0034's, per the docs/LEARNINGS.md entry "An old assertion that pins a whole enum set fails the day a later migration appends a label". The whole set is now pinned by 0051's assertion file, and 0042's keeps its own fact: document_too_large is the ninth label.
(i) OFF LIMITS, untouched: app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts (FROZEN, R-202), app/api/documents/**, docs/contracts/extraction*.

Parsed with pgsql-parser before anything else: 2 statements, 1 AlterEnumStmt with skipIfNewValExists true and 1 SelectStmt, no DROP TABLE, no TRUNCATE, no DELETE, no row touched. WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE, READ COLD. The callback route writes `meta: body._meta ?? null` into the jsonb column that migration 0008 created with the table, and writes `page_count` into the dedicated column that migration 0032 added, both on every callback and both since the day they were written. The gap was entirely on the read side: neither column appeared in the select list that draftColumnsFor builds, neither field existed on ExtractionDraft, and the review panel never mentioned either. Both migration comments say the value is "stored and never shown to the operator", and both also say it exists so that a wrong extraction can be EXPLAINED rather than argued about. Those two sentences cannot both be honoured, and the finding picks the second.

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each within the task:
(a) THE REVIEW SCREEN, NOT A DOCUMENT DETAIL SCREEN, and the choice was not a preference. ExtractionDraft is consumed by exactly one component in the repository, ExtractionReviewPanel, rendered by /incarca-comanda. There is no document detail screen that holds a draft, so the finding's second option does not exist to be chosen.
(b) ON THE DRAFT ROW, NOT INSIDE THE REVIEW FORM. The expandable body renders only for drafts that get one: an extracted or partial draft gets the form, a scan-sourced failed draft gets the header-only view, and a DIGITAL failed draft gets neither. A block placed inside either body would be invisible on exactly the shape the finding names.
(c) INSIDE A CLOSED details ELEMENT. The screen has one job, reconciling the document against what gets saved, and a model name and a millisecond count have no business in front of that job. The named spec asserts the block is hidden BEFORE it clicks, so the claim about not cluttering the screen is proven rather than asserted.
(d) THE MODEL PAGE COUNT ONLY ON THE FAILED SHAPE, which is the finding's own wording. On a document that read successfully the number says nothing the lines do not already say; on a failed one it is the only signal that the model read one page of four and answered consistently with itself, which contract section 4.3a says nothing else in the chain catches. OUR OWN upload-time count is shown beside it, under its own label, because one number alone cannot be compared with anything and two labelled numbers are exactly the question.
(e) meta IS SELECTED WITH NO CAPABILITY PROBE, AND IT IS THE ONLY COLUMN HERE THAT NEEDS NONE. It comes from 0008, the file that creates the table, so the column and the table share a fate and a database on which extraction_drafts exists always has it. page_count comes from 0032, a later file that reaches production on merge while the code ships from the same push, so it is gated by the existing hasExtractionPageCount probe, mirroring exactly how the upload-time count is appended today.
(f) EVERY FIELD OF meta IS READ SEPARATELY AND DISTRUSTED. The column is unvalidated jsonb written verbatim from somebody else's payload; nothing checks its shape at write time and nothing can at read time. A value of the wrong type becomes null, which is what an absent value already means, and case 3 of the spec sends a _meta that is not an object at all to prove the screen survives it.
(g) partial_cause IS READ EVEN THOUGH IT IS NOT IN THE CONTRACT. Contract section 4.3 lists four fields and this is not one of them; the ruling recorded in decisions/inbox.md says in terms that it arrives inside _meta, which our route stores and does not read, and the finding names it. It is shown ONLY when it arrives: a row reading "not reported" would promise a field nobody undertook to send, which the four contract fields did.
(h) A BROKEN REPORT IS THE ABSENCE SENTENCE, NEVER ZERO, for the reason migration 0032 refuses a default on the page count: zero pages is not a smaller reading, and an instantaneous duration is not a faster one.
(i) NO MIGRATION. Both columns exist and both are populated. The two migration comments that say the values are never shown to the operator are now stale, and correcting a comment on an applied migration would take a new file this card was not asked for; it is reported for its own card, not invented here.
(j) OFF LIMITS, untouched: app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts (FROZEN, R-202), app/api/documents/**, docs/contracts/extraction*, and supabase/migrations/**.

cards.title: A documentation-only pull request stops paying for the whole suite: .github/workflows/quality.yml gains a first step, id docs_scope, that classifies the diff against the base commit and sets docs_only, and twelve heavy steps gain a step-level if: on it. The steps gated are Build, Apply every migration to a bare postgres, both applier proofs combined with the existing applier_scope condition, and the whole End to end block from Start local Supabase to Upload Playwright report on failure. Typecheck and every validator and doctrine proof stay unfiltered on every pull request, the board validator and the card-id checks included, because a documentation-only diff is exactly the diff that edits a board. cards.plain: A change that touches nothing but written documents no longer waits about twenty minutes for the system to rebuild and retest an application nobody edited. cards.acceptance: F12'S OWN LINE, QUOTED EXACTLY: "a docs-only PR shows `quality` green in well under 10 minutes; a code PR still runs every step". MACHINE-CHECKABLE FORM, both halves proven by real Action runs whose ids go in the evidence: (1) THE CODE HALF. This card's own pull request changes .github/workflows/quality.yml, which matches none of the documentation patterns, so its quality run must log `docs_only=false` from the step named `Decide whether the diff is documentation only` and must show Build, `Apply every migration to a bare postgres, unmodified` and every step of the End to end block from `Start local Supabase` to `End to end` with a success conclusion, none of them skipped. (2) THE DOCUMENTATION HALF. A second pull request whose diff is one appended line in an existing file under docs/ must log `docs_only=true`, must show Build, `Apply every migration to a bare postgres, unmodified`, `Prove the migration applier against the Docker shim`, `Prove every applier assertion can fail` and all eight End to end steps with conclusion `skipped`, must show `Typecheck`, `Validate boards`, `Refuse a commit whose card id resolves to no card`, `Refuse a migration that removes rows` and `Refuse an assertion with no failing case` as `success`, and the whole job must conclude success in under 10 minutes of wall clock. PLUS the workflow file contains no `paths:` key: `grep -c '^ *paths:' .github/workflows/quality.yml` reports 0. PLUS the check name is unchanged: the workflow's `name:` and the job's `name:` are both `quality`. PLUS `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` exit 0.

SOURCE: the operator factory's GOALS.md, goal G29, Ivan's finding F12 in his approved form, quoted exactly: "F12 in Ivan's approved form. In `.github/workflows/quality.yml`, NO `paths:` key and no change to the check name `quality` or to branch protection. Inside the job, a first step decides whether the diff is docs-only (only `docs/**`, `*.md`, `decisions/**`, board JSON); when it is, the heavy steps (build, migration apply, applier proofs, End to end) are skipped by step-level `if:` and the job still runs the validators and exits green. Repo CLAUDE.md section 3.1 must be amended in the same PR under section 9c (quote, mark, keep) because it currently names exactly two filtered steps. Acceptance: a docs-only PR shows `quality` green in well under 10 minutes; a code PR still runs every step. POC merges on trusted green after reading the workflow diff."

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each within the task:
(a) A SECOND COMPUTED FILTER, NOT A WIDENING OF `applier_scope`. The existing filter answers a different question (did anything that could break the migration applier change) and shares its answer between two steps that are about one file. Folding a documentation test into it would make one output mean two things, and the first person to widen either path set would silently move the other.
(b) THE STEP GOES BEFORE `Typecheck`, not next to `applier_scope`, because it has to gate `Build`, which is the second step in the job. Its position is the only thing about it that differs from the pattern it copies.
(c) IT FAILS OPEN IN THREE PLACES, and always toward running everything: an unresolvable base commit, an empty changed-file list, and a classifier that exits with an error all set `docs_only=false`. The first mirrors `applier_scope` exactly. The second and third have no counterpart there and are additions, because this filter's false positive skips ten more steps than that one's does.
(d) THE OFFENDING FILES ARE COLLECTED, NOT DETECTED WITH `grep -q`, and this is the one place the shape deliberately departs from `applier_scope`. Under `pipefail`, `grep -q` can close the pipe the moment it matches and the pipeline then reports the writer's SIGPIPE as 141, a status indistinguishable from `grep` finding nothing. In `applier_scope` that mistake would run a proof that did not need to run. Here it would classify a code diff as documentation and skip the build and the suite, which is the exact failure this card must not introduce. Reading the whole list has no early exit and no such status.
(e) `^docs/` AND `^decisions/` AS PREFIXES, AND `\.md$` AT ANY DEPTH. The finding names `docs/**`, `*.md`, `decisions/**` and the board JSON. The board files live under `docs/` already and are named in the pattern anyway, because they are the files this exemption most often exists for and a reader should not have to derive that. `CLAUDE.md` is matched by the `.md` rule, which is correct and is why this card's own pull request is still classified as code: `.github/workflows/quality.yml` is in the same diff and matches nothing.
(f) `docs/board/validate-board.mjs` IS CLASSIFIED AS DOCUMENTATION, and it is executable code. It is reported here rather than carved out, because the step that exercises it, `Validate boards`, is NOT gated and runs on every pull request, so a change to it is still proven by the same run. A carve-out would add a rule whose only effect would be to run a build that cannot say anything about it.
(g) THE WHOLE End to end BLOCK IS GATED AS ONE, all eight steps, never a subset. Skipping `Start local Supabase` while running `Apply migrations to the local stack` would be a red run rather than a fast one.
(h) `Upload Playwright report on failure` KEEPS ITS `failure()` AND GAINS THE SECOND CLAUSE. On a documentation-only diff no Playwright run happened, so a failing validator would otherwise send that step looking for a report directory nobody wrote.
(i) THE TWO APPLIER PROOFS CARRY BOTH CONDITIONS EVEN THOUGH THE COMBINATION CANNOT CHANGE BEHAVIOUR TODAY. `applier_scope` answers true only for paths that no documentation-only diff can contain, so when `docs_only` is true, `run` is already false. The clause is written on the step anyway so that whoever widens either filter later sees both gates instead of inferring one from the other, and the reasoning is written into the workflow next to it rather than left to be re-derived.
(j) NOTHING ELSE IS GATED. `Typecheck` and about fifty `Refuse ...` and `Prove ...` steps run on every pull request. The board validator, the card-id checks and the board-edit check are the load-bearing case, because a documentation-only diff is precisely the diff that edits a board.
(k) NO MIGRATION, and nothing under `app/api/extraction/**`, `app/api/documents/**`, `lib/data/extraction*` or `docs/contracts/extraction*` is touched. This card is unrelated to extraction and `app/api/extraction/callback/route.ts` stays byte-identical to main, ruling R-202 held.

cards.plain: When the document reader leaves a number blank on an order, the system now records it as missing instead of recording a zero. It is therefore NOT a new value of public.extraction_error_code: error_code is one document-level field that R-190 makes the sender's, and a per-line disagreement is a different granularity.
(c) STORAGE: per line, platform_math_outcome text constrained to passed, failed, not_run, and platform_math_diff numeric, both nullable with no default; per document, platform_line_math_failed integer, nullable, no default, never negative. A row written before 0052 genuinely does not know, and a default would rewrite it into a claim nobody made. not_run means the check ran and the line lacked quantity, unit_price or line_total. The document count is null when no line could be checked at all (zero lines, or every line not_run), because not_run is not passed, the same rule EXT-18 set for the header.
(e) THE TOLERANCE is round2(max(toleranceFor(1), 0.005 * abs(quantity))). The floor is the reconciliation's own per-line figure called, not restated: toleranceFor(1) is 0.05. The second term is the largest error a unit price printed to whole bani can carry: half a ban per unit, so 1000 units at a price printed 1.23 for a true 1.2345 miss by 4.50 and must not be flagged. A fixed cent amount would flag every large-quantity line whose price was rounded on paper. Both sides are rounded to two decimals BEFORE the subtraction, as round2's header requires.

(a) A NEW, SEPARATE CHECK, run after the existing classification has decided status and error_code. classifyScan, reconcile and headerConsistency are not touched: reconcile never looks at a line's provenance, and a new arm there would move documents between arms, which is the refusal contract.
(b) WHAT IT MOVES, AND ONLY THAT. When the status our route would store is extracted, the sender supplied no error_code, and at least one line carries line_total_source exactly "derived", the stored status becomes partial. Nothing else moves: error_code stays null (partial without a code is legal since P3-29a, and no code is invented on a field R-190 makes the sender's), every line is kept, and a status our classification already set to failed is never softened. A payload that carries its own error_code is never touched, ruling R-190.

Doctrine pattern (h) of the same amendment is exactly the reason not to narrow it: a control filed under the scanned-document heading only was the counterparty's own defect.
(d) EXACT VALUE MATCH. Only the string "derived", after the trim every stored string gets, counts. An unknown value (for example "Derived" or "estimated") is stored as sent and does not move anything, because EXT-34 stores the field uninterpreted and a guess about an unknown value is a new rule nobody made.

Instead a new column extraction_drafts.platform_derived_partial boolean, nullable, no default, the platform_ prefix EXT-26 gave our own verdict, the same shape P3-75 took for its separate check. null means the rule did not run (every row before 0054), false means it ran and did not move the status, true means it moved it.

(g) HTTP CODES UNCHANGED. The code is decided by isRepeat, after every check; a moved payload is still 202 or 200. The response body reports the STORED status, as the route already does for EXT-16 ("what was written, not what arrived"), so a moved payload's body says partial.

R-009 declined a cancel-instead-of-delete variant for P2-15's end-to-end residue; this card is a different thing, an operator action Ivan asked for himself in F20, and the owner's standing rule is that test data is cancelled, never deleted.

DECISIONS TAKEN AT AUTHORING, each from the task:
(a) COLUMNS, NOT AN ENUM VALUE. extraction_status is (extracted, partial, failed) and is guarded by the check extraction_drafts_error_code_matches_status; a new value would also need that check replaced, and ALTER TYPE ADD VALUE cannot be used in the transaction that adds it. Three nullable columns with no default, exactly the shape of confirmed_at (0010, 0011): cancelled_at timestamptz, cancelled_by uuid referencing auth.users with the same referential action as confirmed_by, cancel_reason text. Cancelled means cancelled_at is not null. The enum, the check and every policy are untouched.
(b) WHO MAY CANCEL: the owner, active, and nobody else. The task says owner or active operator and, in terms, that the account manager is not allowed. In this code base the account manager role is the one the screens call Operator, so the two sentences overlap; the explicit exclusion is applied and the ambiguity is written in the report for the owner. The check is in the server action, through getSessionUser, which returns a user only for an active profile, because the write policy on extraction_drafts is to authenticated using true and is not edited here.
(c) WHERE A CANCELLED DRAFT IS FOUND. A draft before confirmation has no order: the order is created only at confirmation (0010). cards.title: The end to end suite stops losing one random test per run to the Next development server restarting itself at its memory threshold: the main Playwright project (394 of the 395 cases) serves a PRODUCTION build through next start in its own NEXT_DIST_DIR, mirroring the productie project's shape from P2-11, instead of npm run dev. No test file, no timeout used as a retry, no retries, no migration, no application code.
cards.plain: The automated test suite used to lose one random, unrelated test on almost every run, because its own copy of the app would restart itself partway through a long run when it ran short of memory, killing whatever was on screen at that second. It now runs a stable, built copy of the app that cannot restart itself, so a red result means a real fault again instead of bad luck.
cards.acceptance: FIVE CONSECUTIVE GREEN FULL RUNS of the complete suite on ONE commit, in CI, their run ids and attempt numbers recorded in the report, none of them printing `Server is approaching the used memory threshold, restarting...` in the End to end step and none of them failing a case for that signature. Full suite means `npx playwright test` with no filter, all three projects (chromium, productie, fara-webhook), 395 of 395 cases collected. AND the diff adds no `retries` anywhere and raises no test, expect or project timeout; the single timeout that changes is the MAIN webServer's own startup budget, from 120000 to 300000 ms, because that server now performs a build before it can answer, which is the same work and therefore the same budget the productie webServer has carried since P2-11. AND `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build` and the board validator on all three boards exit 0.
cards.defaults: SOURCE: the operator factory's GOALS.md, goal G55, the platform owner's words: "The e2e suite fails one random test per run ... Find the shared cause on the local stack ... and fix it at the root: serve the built app rather than the dev server in CI, or lower workers, or a readiness wait, whichever the evidence supports. Not allowed: retries on individual tests, longer timeouts." (a) THE EVIDENCE, and it is a correlation of four for four, not an assumption. In every one of the four affected runs the line `Server is approaching the used memory threshold, restarting...` appears EXACTLY ONCE in the whole log, and the line immediately after it is the failing case: run 35805338724 (PR #352) at 02:06:48.70 then case 374 at 02:06:51.52; run 35814037940 attempt 1 (PR #353) at 04:03:31.87 then case 385 at 04:04:02.78; attempt 2 at 04:59:50.48 then case 374 at 05:00:02.56; attempt 3 at 05:57:37.63 then case 375 at 05:57:38.96. A different case each time, always between 374 and 385 of 395, which is a resource that runs out late and not a case that is wrong. (b) THE CAUSE IS NEXT'S OWN AND IT IS DEVELOPMENT-MODE-ONLY: `getMemoryRestartStats` in node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/utils.js returns undefined the moment `isDev` is false, and otherwise fires when the used heap passes 80 per cent of the heap size limit, after which start-server.js calls `process.exit(RESTART_EXIT_CODE)`. The in-flight request dies with the process, which is exactly `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, `Failed to fetch`, `The destination stream closed early` and `Failed to find Server Action ... older or newer deployment` (the action ids belong to the compilation that just died). It fires once per process because the supervisor clears the flag afterwards, which is why there is exactly one restart and exactly one lost case per run. (c) THE SUSPECT THE GOAL NAMED FIRST IS WRONG, and was checked before anything else: `workers: 1` has been set in playwright.config.ts all along, so the suite was already fully serial. (d) OPTION CHOSEN: the main chromium project gets its OWN production build in its OWN NEXT_DIST_DIR (.next-main), the same shape the productie server has used since P2-11. A production server has no memory-threshold restart at all, does not recompile on demand, and does not accumulate the compilation output of 395 cases. (e) THE CI COST IS ABOUT TEN SECONDS, measured and not guessed: with Turbopack the workflow's own Build step compiled in 7.0 s and finished end to end in 10.4 s (run 35814037940, 05:04:09.7 to 05:04:20.1). The five webServers start one after another, so this is additive, and it is expected to be repaid by a production server answering without compiling. (f) OPTION REJECTED, sharing ONE build between the main and productie servers: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is inlined at build time and the two servers answer on different origins (3100 and 3101), so one build cannot carry both truthfully. (g) OPTION REJECTED, the flag `experimental.devMemoryThresholdRestart: false`, which does exist in this Next version: next.config.ts carries an explicit doctrine against experimental flags, written for P2-11, and the flag would in any case switch off the safety valve rather than remove the growth that opens it. (h) OPTION REJECTED, raising NODE_OPTIONS max-old-space-size: it postpones the same failure instead of removing it, and the goal asks for the root. (i) THE OTHER TWO SERVERS ARE UNCHANGED: productie keeps its own build, its own dist directory and its own origin, and fara-webhook stays in development mode deliberately, because it serves one spec and never approaches the threshold.

Both findings come from the bug sweep in docs/reports/2026-09-22-critic-bug-sweep.md, F6 and F7, and both live in components/clients/ClientsScreen.tsx, which is why they are one card and one pull request. (a) THE DOCTRINE IS THE SCREEN'S OWN, written in its header since P3-06: every filter lives in the URL, so a filtered list can be sent to somebody as a link and the browser's back button remakes it exactly. Both findings are that sentence being false in one place each, so the fix is to obey it rather than to invent a rule. (b) F6 WAS ONE CONTROL OUT OF STEP WITH EVERY OTHER. `push(patch)` reads the current query string, applies only the keys named in the patch and navigates, so every parameter not named survives; the stage chips, the view chips, the type and status selects and the pagination all rely on that. Șterge filtrele alone did `router.push(pathname)`, a bare navigation with no query string, which drops `vedere` with everything else. It now patches exactly the four fields `filtered` tests, and `stare` returns to "active" rather than to the empty string, because "active" is what that field's absence of a filter means and the empty string is not one of its values. (c) F7 NEEDED A WAY TO TELL TWO CAUSES APART, and this repository already had one: the `seen` ref in components/ui/DateField.tsx, whose comment says why it exists, that a half typed date would otherwise be wiped on every keystroke. The same shape is used here: the screen remembers the values of `q` it sent to the URL itself, and only resynchronises the box when the URL's `q` becomes a value it did not send. (d) A LIST OF SENT VALUES AND NOT A SINGLE ONE, which is the one place this is more than a copy of DateField. A navigation this screen asked for can land AFTER the one issued after it, because each one is a server round trip: with a 300ms debounce, the render for "abc" can arrive after the screen has already sent "abcd", and a single remembered value would read that late render as an outside change and eat the last keystrokes. Finding a sent value discards everything sent before it, so the list cannot grow when an intermediate render is superseded and never arrives. (e) THE CLEAR BUTTON ALSO EMPTIES THE BOX DIRECTLY, and this is not belt and braces. With a stage chip applied the button is visible while typed text has not yet reached the URL; in that state the URL's `q` does not change when the button is pressed, so the resynchronisation above cannot fire, and the pending 300ms debounce would have pushed the term straight back. (f) OPTION REJECTED, resynchronising the box on every render where it differs from the URL: that is exactly the failure DateField's comment warns about, it would fight the operator mid-debounce, and the third acceptance case exists to keep it rejected. (g) OPTION REJECTED, listening to `popstate` only: it covers Back and Forward and misses a received link and a client side navigation to the same route, which is the same defect through a different door. (h) OPTION REJECTED, giving `<ClientsScreen>` a `key` in app/(app)/clienti/page.tsx so it remounts on every navigation: it would throw away the two creation dialogs' state and re-run every effect on a page of filters, to fix one input. (i) WHAT IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED: the 300ms debounce and the search-as-you-type feel, `filtered`'s own definition, every other control's URL patching, and the `lead=` PageHeader prop that a careless grep for the word lead would sweep.

B1: the Azi next step column stops printing the stage label De reluat for a lead nobody wrote a step for, and shows the same dash the other branch beside it already shows. F12: the seven hand rolled two form plurals on the CRM and order screens go through the three form Romanian helper lib/data/format.ts already exports, so a count past nineteen reads 20 de leaduri and not 20 leaduri, while the verb phrase N de sunat on Azi is deliberately left alone. F13: the orange and the amber chip text tones are darkened on their own new tokens until each reaches WCAG AA 4.5:1 on its pale background, leaving --color-rc-orange, --color-rc-orange-deep, --color-rc-warn, every chip background, every border, the primary button and the four tones that already pass untouched. F17: tests/e2e/button-contrast.spec.ts, which measured nothing but white labels on the primary button, now measures every one of the six chip tones. cards.plain: Five small things the operator sees are put right. The list of people to call today no longer writes the name of a stage in the column that is supposed to say what the next step is: when nobody has written a step, that column is simply blank. Counts on six more screens now read the way Romanian is actually written, so a header says twenty de clients rather than twenty clients. Two of the small coloured labels, the orange one and the amber one, were too pale to read comfortably and are now dark enough to meet the accessibility standard the rest of the app already meets, and the automatic check that guards those colours now looks at every coloured label instead of only at the big orange buttons. And a perfectly good PDF is no longer turned away by the attach box on an order just because the computer it came from did not tell the browser what kind of file it was; a file that really is the wrong kind is still refused, in Romanian.

Azi shows a blank, not the stage name, when no step text exists; Romanian counts above nineteen take the de form everywhere (20 de produse); the two chip colours reach 4.5:1 and the contrast spec covers chips; the document type check accepts an empty browser MIME on a .pdf extension." The five findings are B1, F12, F13, F17 and F18 of docs/reports/2026-09-22-critic-bug-sweep.md. (a) B1 TAKES THE DASH AND NOT AN INSTRUCTION PHRASE. The critic report offered two repairs, a dash or a phrase that reads as an instruction. The goal line says a blank, so the dash it is, and nothing is invented. dueFrom itself and every rule that decides which rows reach the list are untouched, which the acceptance case proves by asserting the step free row is still present, still red and still first. (b) THE VERB PHRASE ON AZI IS LEFT ALONE, deliberately and against the surface appearance of the goal line. The report is explicit that de sunat is a verb phrase and not a counted noun, so the three form rule does not apply to it; the two branches that produced the identical string are collapsed into one, which changes no character of what is displayed, and the acceptance asserts the displayed form. (c) A SEVENTH CALL SITE IS FIXED BESIDE THE SIX. The report names the upload order confirmation in the same breath as the manual one and it holds the identical hand rolled ternary over a counted noun, so it is repaired the same way and said so here. (d) THE TWO CHIP COLOURS GET THEIR OWN TOKENS rather than moving an existing one. --color-rc-orange is the menu marker, the tab underline and the focus outline and P3-53 recorded that it must not move; --color-rc-orange-deep is the link colour on eleven screens and --color-rc-warn is a background swatch and a border as well as a text colour. Darkening any of those would change surfaces this card was not asked to touch, so two text only tokens are added beside them and nothing else changes. The hue of each is kept to the degree so the chips stay recognisably orange and amber. (e) THE MEASURED RATIOS, with the same WCAG 2.1 formula the spec uses, verified first to reproduce every number in the critic report exactly. Orange chip text moves from 2.92:1 to 4.87:1 and amber from 3.44:1 to 4.98:1, both on their unchanged pale backgrounds. The four tones that already passed are unchanged at 4.99, 4.93, 5.83 and 4.93, and the primary button is unchanged at 4.60. (f) THE CHIP CLASS MAP MOVES TO A PLAIN MODULE, components/ui/chip-tones.ts, and this is what makes F17 possible at all. The contrast spec renders one chip per tone in the real page, and to do that without re-typing the class strings in the test, where they could fall silently out of step, it imports them; a .tsx component carrying React cannot be imported from a Playwright spec, a module of plain data can. primitives.tsx re-exports the names so no other file changes. (g) FOUR OF THE SIX TONES HAVE NO GUARANTEED PLACE ON ANY SCREEN, which is why the all tones case renders rather than navigates: info appears only on an issued quote, danger and ok only where the data happens to put them. The two that are guaranteed are measured where the application renders them, and the bridge between the two halves is an assertion that the real chip's class attribute equals CHIP_BASE plus its tone. (h) F18 NORMALISES THE TYPE BEFORE SENDING, and not only at the point of the message, and this is the load bearing decision of the card. The server repeats the same exact string comparison (lib/data/inbound-actions.ts) and a File with an empty type arrives there as application/octet-stream, because that is what multipart serialisation writes when the type is missing; this was measured on Chromium rather than assumed. Repairing only the browser message would therefore have moved the refusal from the screen to the server, with the same Romanian sentence, and changed nothing at all for the operator. The type is instead taken to its canonical form from the extension, but ONLY when the browser said nothing, and the file is sent with it, so the server check stays exactly as it was and still refuses everything that is not a PDF, a PNG or a JPEG. A declared type that is simply not accepted stays refused: the extension cannot rescue it. (i) A CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING: the page count and the mime type that reach the extraction webhook are now the real ones for such a file, where before the upload never got that far. (j) TWO FINDINGS ARE RECORDED AND NOT FIXED, on the goal's own instruction and under CLAUDE.md section 3: the text-rc-muted-2 hint colour at 3.04:1, which the goal excludes by naming the two chip colours, and the identically shaped MIME comparison in lib/data/extraction-actions.ts, which the goal excludes by naming the one box. Each wants a card of its own. (k) NO MIGRATION and no schema change: the whole diff is display text, two colour tokens, one guard, the tests and the documents.

The file is therefore built in the page with `new File([octets], name)` and placed on the input through a DataTransfer, and the case asserts its own premise, that files[0].type is the empty string, before it asserts anything about the screen.

WHY THE F18 FIX REACHES FURTHER THAN THE REPORT'S LINE, and it is not scope invention. `uploadOrderDocument` in lib/data/inbound-actions.ts repeats the same exact string comparison against the same three types, and a File with an empty type arrives at a server action as application/octet-stream, which was measured on Chromium against a local server rather than reasoned about. A repair confined to the browser message would have moved the refusal from the screen to the server, printed the same Romanian sentence, and left the operator exactly where he was. The type is taken to its canonical form from the extension before the file is sent, ONLY when the browser said nothing, so the server side check is untouched and still refuses everything that is not a PDF, a PNG or a JPEG.
